metadata.title: Select-then-differentiate: Solving Bilevel Optimization with Manifold Lower-level Solution Sets

extraction_notes.note: Environment is a Remark but its content is a cited result (Lipschitz continuity of F, Masiha et al. Lem. 3.2); retyped as an external theorem.
Informal intro theorem combines Theorems 3.1 and 3.2; kept as its own theorem (not a verbatim repeat) with uses edges from both formal theorems.
Proof sketches get rigor semi_formal per the proof-sketch rule, although the rigor rule excludes proofs; finalize warns about these three.
Theorem 5.2 has no proof environment; the prose in Appendix E.4 from 'In the non-singleton regime' to the sentence before Remark 6 is taken as its proof.
Related-work summaries of other papers' results, the proof roadmaps, the limitations section, experimental protocols, tables and figures were not extracted as nodes.

nodes.name: Optimistic bilevel optimization problem
nodes.statement: In this paper, we focus on the optimistic bilevel optimization problem \begin{equation} \min_{\theta \in \Theta}\ F(\theta) \qquad\text{where}\qquad F(\theta):=\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x), \qquad \mathcal{S}(\theta):=\arg\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d} g(\theta,x), \end{equation} with compact convex $\Theta \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Minimize the optimistic hyper-objective F(θ)=min over the lower-level argmin set S(θ) of f(θ,x), over compact convex Θ.

nodes.name: Optimistic bilevel formulation (F, S(θ))
nodes.statement: \min_{\theta \in \Theta}\ F(\theta) \qquad\text{where}\qquad F(\theta):=\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x), \qquad \mathcal{S}(\theta):=\arg\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d} g(\theta,x),
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Defines F(θ) as min of f over S(θ)=argmin_x g(θ,x).
nodes.label: eq:intro_blo

nodes.name: Minima selection and optimistic selection set O(θ)
nodes.statement: We refer to the inner optimization over $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ as \emph{minima selection} and define ${\texttt{O}}(\theta) := \arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Unique optimistic selection x*(θ)
nodes.statement: In particular, when ${\texttt{O}}(\theta)$ is a singleton, we denote the unique optimistic selection as $x^\star(\theta)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Under local PL°, unique optimistic selection gives C^1 F with a pseudoinverse hyper-gradient formula; non-degeneracy adds Lipschitz ∇F.
assumptions: the optimistic minimizer is unique, i.e., ${\texttt{O}}(\theta)=\{x^\star(\theta)\}$

nodes.name: Intrinsic dimension k of the solution manifold
nodes.statement: Here, $\texttt{k}$ denotes the common dimension of the lower-level solution manifold $\{\mathcal{S}(\theta)\}_{\theta \in \Theta}$, rather than the ambient dimension $d$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
also_stated_at: The common intrinsic dimension of \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is denoted by \(\texttt{k}\).

nodes.name: Euclidean projection Proj_C
nodes.statement: For any nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^m\), we write $\mathrm{Proj}_{C}(u) :=\arg\min_{v\in C}\|v-u\|$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Tangent and normal spaces and projectors
nodes.statement: For any embedded \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) submanifold \(\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}\) and \(x\in\mathcal{M}\), we write \(\mathcal{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}\) and \(\mathcal{N}_{x}\mathcal{M}\) for the tangent and normal spaces, and \(P_{\mathcal{T}_x\mathcal{M}}\), \(P_{\mathcal{N}_x\mathcal{M}}\) for the corresponding orthogonal projectors.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Abbreviations T_x^θ and N_x^θ
nodes.statement: When \(\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), we abbreviate \(\mathcal{T}_x^\theta := \mathcal{T}_x\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal{N}_x^\theta := \mathcal{N}_x\mathcal{S}(\theta)\).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Order-2 Rényi divergence R_2
nodes.statement: For probability measures \(\nu\) and \(\mu\), we write \(R_2(\nu\|\mu)\) for the order-$2$ R\'enyi divergence.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local Polyak-Łojasiewicz (PŁ) condition
nodes.statement: Let \(\mathcal{M}\) be the collection of all local minima of \(g\in\mathcal{C}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{R})\). We say that \(g\) is \emph{locally P\L} if there exists \(\mu>0\) such that for any connected component \(\mathcal{M}'\subseteq \mathcal{M}\), there exists an open neighborhood \(\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M}')\supset \mathcal{M}'\) satisfying \[ g(x) - \min_{x' \in \mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M}')} g(x') \;\leq\; (2\mu)^{-1}\,\|\nabla g(x)\|^{2}, \, \forall x \in \mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M}'). \]
nodes.section: 2 Local PL Condition and the Manifold Solution Set
nodes.statement_short: g is locally PŁ if around each connected component of its local minima a PŁ inequality with a common μ holds.
nodes.label: def_local_PL

nodes.name: PŁ° condition
nodes.statement: A function \(g:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies the \(\texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) condition if: (1) \(g\in\mathcal{C}^{2}\) is locally P\L, and \(g\in\mathcal{C}^{4}\) on every neighborhood \(\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M}')\); (2) Let \(\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M}) := \cup_{\mathcal{M}'}\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M}')\). For any \(x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}\setminus \mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})\), if \(\nabla g(x)=0\), then \(\nabla^{2}g(x)\prec 0\); (3) The collection of all local minima \(\mathcal{M}\) is contained in a compact set $\mathcal{V}$.
nodes.section: 2 Local PL Condition and the Manifold Solution Set
nodes.statement_short: Local PŁ with C^4 near minima, strict saddles (negative-definite Hessian) at other critical points, and minima in a compact set.
nodes.label: def_mu_PL_assum

nodes.name: Lower-level PŁ° (uniform in θ)
nodes.statement: There exists a constant \(\mu>0\) and a compact domain $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, both independent of $\theta$, such that for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), the function \(g(\theta,\cdot)\) satisfies the \(\texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) condition.
nodes.section: 2 Local PL Condition and the Manifold Solution Set
nodes.statement_short: g(θ,·) satisfies PŁ° for every θ with constants μ and compact V independent of θ.
nodes.label: ass:plcirc

nodes.name: Characterizations of the lower-level solution set S(θ)
nodes.statement: Under \Cref{ass:plcirc}, the following hold for every \(\theta\in\Theta\): (i) \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is a connected compact \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb{R}^{d}\) without boundary \citep[Prop.~3, Cor.~1]{gong2024poincare}. In particular, all local minima of \(g(\theta,\cdot)\) are global minima. (ii) For any \(x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), the Hessian \(H(\theta,x):=\nabla_{xx}^{2} g(\theta,x)\) satisfies $\ker H(\theta,x) \;=\; \mathcal{T}_x^\theta$ and $\langle v, H(\theta,x)v\rangle \;\ge\; c\,\|v\|^2$ for all $v\in \mathcal{N}_x^\theta$ for some constant \(c>0\) that is uniform over \(\theta\in\Theta\) and \(x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) \citep[Cor.~2.17]{rebjock2024fast}. Moreover, assuming $g\in \mathcal{C}^{3}$, there exists an integer \(\texttt{k}\) such that \( \dim(\mathcal{S}(\theta))=\texttt{k}, \forall \theta\in\Theta \), \citep[Lem.~3.5]{masiha2025superquantile}.
nodes.section: 2 Local PL Condition and the Manifold Solution Set
nodes.origin_citation: Gong et al. 2024 (Prop. 3, Cor. 1); Rebjock & Boumal 2024 (Cor. 2.17); Masiha et al. 2025 (Lem. 3.5)
nodes.statement_short: Under PŁ°, S(θ) is a connected compact C^2 submanifold, the Hessian's kernel is the tangent space with a uniform normal spectral gap c, and dim S(θ)=k is constant.
conclusions: \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is a connected compact \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb{R}^{d}\) without boundary
all local minima of \(g(\theta,\cdot)\) are global minima
there exists an integer \(\texttt{k}\) such that
nodes.label: prop:geometry

nodes.name: Lipschitz continuity of the hyper-objective under PŁ°
nodes.statement: Under the lower-level local \texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\ condition and mild regularity on $f$ and $g$, the hyper-objective function is Lipschitz continuous; see \citep[Lem.~3.2]{masiha2025superquantile}. While this implies that $F$ is differentiable almost everywhere, it remains insufficient for our purpose.
nodes.section: 2 Local PL Condition and the Manifold Solution Set
nodes.statement_short: Under lower-level PŁ° and mild regularity the hyper-objective is Lipschitz, hence a.e. differentiable, which is insufficient here.
assumptions: Under the lower-level local \texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\ condition and mild regularity on $f$ and $g$
conclusions: the hyper-objective function is Lipschitz continuous

nodes.name: Non-unique minima selection creates kinks (circle example)
nodes.statement: Let $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x=[x_1,x_2]\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and write $r(\theta)=\sqrt{1+\theta^2}$. Define $a(\theta):= e^{-1/\theta^2}\!\sin(10/\theta)$ for $\theta \neq 0$ and $a(0) = 0$. Consider the functions $f(\theta,x):=a(\theta)\,x_1 + x_2^2$ and $g(\theta,x):=\big(\|x\|^2-(r(\theta))^2\big)^2$, both of which belong to $\mathcal C^\infty(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^2)$. The lower-level solution set is the circle \( \mathcal{S}(\theta)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:\ \|x\|=r(\theta)\}. \) On $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$, $f(\theta,x)=a(\theta) x_1+r(\theta)^2-x_1^2$, which is a concave quadratic in $x_1$. Therefore, for $a(\theta)\neq 0$, the minimizer is unique and given by \( x^\star(\theta)= [ - \mathrm{sign}(a(\theta)) r(\theta), 0 ]; \) at any $\theta$ with $a(\theta)=0$, we have \( \arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)=\{[-r(\theta),0],[r(\theta),0]\}, \) i.e., the selected optimistic minimizer is \emph{not unique}. Consequently, $F(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)=-r(\theta)\,|a(\theta)|$. Since $a(\theta)=0$ at $\theta_k:=10/(k\pi)$ for each $k\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$, $F$ is not differentiable at every $\theta_k$ (a countably infinite set accumulating at $0$); see \Cref{fig:ex-kink}.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: On a circle of minimizers with f = a(θ)x_1 + x_2^2, ties at a(θ)=0 make F = −r|a| non-differentiable at infinitely many θ_k → 0.
nodes.label: ex:kink

nodes.name: C^1 regularity of the hyper-objective under uniqueness
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{ass:plcirc} hold and assume $f \in \mathcal C^1$ and $g \in \mathcal C^3$. Fix $\theta_0\in\Theta$ and assume there exist an open set $\mathcal U$ containing $\theta_0$ such that, for all $\theta\in\mathcal U$, \(\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)\) is a singleton. Then there exists an open neighborhood $\mathcal U_0\subseteq\mathcal U$ of $\theta_0$ such that $F \in \mathcal{C}^1(\mathcal U_0)$. Moreover, for all $\theta\in\mathcal U_0$, the hyper-gradient is given by \cref{eq:hg_formula}.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: If the optimistic minimizer is unique near θ_0, F is C^1 near θ_0 with the pseudoinverse hyper-gradient formula.
assumptions: assume there exist an open set $\mathcal U$ containing $\theta_0$ such that, for all $\theta\in\mathcal U$, \(\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)\) is a singleton
conclusions: there exists an open neighborhood $\mathcal U_0\subseteq\mathcal U$ of $\theta_0$ such that $F \in \mathcal{C}^1(\mathcal U_0)$

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement:
We sketch the proof in three steps; see Appendix~ef{append:F-diff-unique} for the full argument. \smallskip
oindent \emph{Step 1: parameterize \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) locally by solving the normal equations.} Let \(x_0:=x^\star(	heta_0)\), and abbreviate \(\mathcal{T}_0:=\mathcal{T}_{x_0}^{	heta_0}\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0:=\mathcal{N}_{x_0}^{	heta_0}\). Choose orthonormal bases \(U_{\mathcal{T}_0}\) and \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\) spanning \(\mathcal{T}_0\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0\). Write \[ x=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v \] and consider \[ \Phi(	heta,u,v) := U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{	op}
abla_x g(	heta,x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v). \] By the normal nondegeneracy implied by \Cref{ass:plcirc} (see \Cref{prop:geometry}), \[ D_v\Phi(	heta_0,0,0) = U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{	op}
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_0,x_0)U_{\mathcal{N}_0} \] is invertible. The implicit function theorem gives a \(\mathcal C^2\) map \(v=\varphi(	heta,u)\) solving \(\Phi(	heta,u,\varphi(	heta,u))=0\) near \((	heta_0,0)\). Defining \[ \psi(	heta,u):=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\varphi(	heta,u), \] we obtain a local chart for the normal critical set. The \(	exttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) geometry, the fixed local dimension of \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\), and local Hausdorff continuity then identify this chart with the nearby branch of the true minimizer manifold \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\). \smallskip
oindent \emph{Step 2: reduce to a fixed-domain minimization.} By uniqueness of the optimistic minimizer and compactness of the lower-level solution set, \(x^\star(	heta)\) remains in this chart patch for all \(	heta\) close to \(	heta_0\). After possibly shrinking the parameter neighborhood, choose a compact coordinate set \(U\subset\mathbb R^{	exttt{k}}\), contained in the chart domain, that contains the coordinate \(u^\star(	heta)\) of the selected minimizer for all such \(	heta\). The optimistic problem becomes the fixed-domain minimization \[ F(	heta)=\min_{u\in U}	ilde f(	heta,u), \qquad 	ilde f(	heta,u):=f(	heta,\psi(	heta,u)). \] \smallskip
oindent \emph{Step 3: apply an envelope argument and compute the hyper-gradient.} We apply the Danskin-type envelope lemma in Appendix~ef{append:F-diff-unique}, namely \Cref{lem:envelope-unique}. For a value function \(F(	heta)=\min_{u\in U}\phi(	heta,u)\) over a fixed compact set, uniqueness of the minimizer allows one to differentiate \(F\) by differentiating only \(\phi\) with respect to \(	heta\) at the minimizing point; no derivative of the argmin map is needed. Applying this lemma pointwise, and then using continuity of the unique minimizer on the fixed compact domain, yields the local \(\mathcal C^1\) regularity of \(F\). Finally, differentiating the lower-level stationarity identity \(
abla_x g(	heta,\psi(	heta,u))=0\) gives the pseudoinverse hyper-gradient formula \eqref{eq:hg_formula}.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: local normal chart by the implicit function theorem, fixed-domain reduction by uniqueness, then a Danskin envelope argument.

nodes.name: Normal chart via implicit function theorem
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 1: parameterize \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) locally by solving the normal equations.} Let \(x_0:=x^\star(\theta_0)\), and abbreviate \(\mathcal{T}_0:=\mathcal{T}_{x_0}^{\theta_0}\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0:=\mathcal{N}_{x_0}^{\theta_0}\). Choose orthonormal bases \(U_{\mathcal{T}_0}\) and \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\) spanning \(\mathcal{T}_0\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0\). Write \[ x=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v \] and consider \[ \Phi(\theta,u,v) := U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{\top}\nabla_x g(\theta,x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v). \] By the normal nondegeneracy implied by \Cref{ass:plcirc} (see \Cref{prop:geometry}), \[ D_v\Phi(\theta_0,0,0) = U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{\top}\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta_0,x_0)U_{\mathcal{N}_0} \] is invertible. The implicit function theorem gives a \(\mathcal C^2\) map \(v=\varphi(\theta,u)\) solving \(\Phi(\theta,u,\varphi(\theta,u))=0\) near \((\theta_0,0)\). Defining \[ \psi(\theta,u):=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\varphi(\theta,u), \] we obtain a local chart for the normal critical set. The \(\texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) geometry, the fixed local dimension of \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), and local Hausdorff continuity then identify this chart with the nearby branch of the true minimizer manifold \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\).
nodes.statement_short: Solve the normal equations by the IFT to get a local chart ψ of S(θ).
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Fixed-domain reduction
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 2: reduce to a fixed-domain minimization.} By uniqueness of the optimistic minimizer and compactness of the lower-level solution set, \(x^\star(\theta)\) remains in this chart patch for all \(\theta\) close to \(\theta_0\). After possibly shrinking the parameter neighborhood, choose a compact coordinate set \(U\subset\mathbb R^{\texttt{k}}\), contained in the chart domain, that contains the coordinate \(u^\star(\theta)\) of the selected minimizer for all such \(\theta\). The optimistic problem becomes the fixed-domain minimization \[ F(\theta)=\min_{u\in U}\tilde f(\theta,u), \qquad \tilde f(\theta,u):=f(\theta,\psi(\theta,u)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness keeps x*(θ) in the chart, so F is a min over a fixed compact coordinate set.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Envelope argument
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 3: apply an envelope argument and compute the hyper-gradient.} We apply the Danskin-type envelope lemma in Appendix~\ref{append:F-diff-unique}, namely \Cref{lem:envelope-unique}. For a value function \(F(\theta)=\min_{u\in U}\phi(\theta,u)\) over a fixed compact set, uniqueness of the minimizer allows one to differentiate \(F\) by differentiating only \(\phi\) with respect to \(\theta\) at the minimizing point; no derivative of the argmin map is needed. Applying this lemma pointwise, and then using continuity of the unique minimizer on the fixed compact domain, yields the local \(\mathcal C^1\) regularity of \(F\). Finally, differentiating the lower-level stationarity identity \(\nabla_x g(\theta,\psi(\theta,u))=0\) gives the pseudoinverse hyper-gradient formula \eqref{eq:hg_formula}.
nodes.statement_short: Danskin envelope lemma gives C^1; differentiating stationarity gives the pseudoinverse formula.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Pseudoinverse via normal-space basis
nodes.statement: For compactness, denote \(\mathbf{H}:=\nabla^{2}_{xx}g(\theta,x^\star(\theta))\), and let $\mathbf{N}_\theta$ and $\mathbf{T}_\theta$ be orthogonal bases that span \(\mathcal{N}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta\) and \(\mathcal{T}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta\), respectively. Under the \(\texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) condition, \Cref{prop:geometry} implies \(\mathbf{N}_\theta^\top H \mathbf{N}_\theta \succ 0\); Besides, we have \(\mathbf{T}_\theta^\top \mathbf{H} \mathbf{T}_\theta = 0\). Consequently, $\mathbf{N}_\theta\left(\mathbf{N}_\theta^\top \mathbf{H} \mathbf{N}_\theta\right)^{-1} \mathbf{N}_\theta^\top$ coincides with the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse of $\mathbf{H}$.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: Since the Hessian is zero on the tangent space and positive definite on the normal space, N(NᵀHN)^{-1}Nᵀ is its Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse.
nodes.label: remark_pseudoinverse

nodes.name: Degenerate and non-degenerate optimistic minimizers
nodes.statement: Consider the setting of \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique}. Let \(\bar f_\theta:=f(\theta,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\). We say that $x^*(\theta)$ is a \emph{non-degenerate optimistic minimizer} for $\theta \in \mathcal{U}_0$ if the Riemannian Hessian\footnote{See \Cref{eq:riem-hess-restricted} in Appendix~\ref{append:regularity-assumption} for the convention used here.} of the restricted objective is positive definite at \(x^*(\theta)\), i.e., $\big\langle v,\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\bar f_\theta(x^*(\theta))[v]\big\rangle>0$ for all $v\in\mathcal{T}_{x^*(\theta)}^{\theta}\setminus\{0\}$. Equivalently, \(f(\theta,\cdot)\) has strictly positive intrinsic second-order derivative along every tangent direction of the manifold \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) at \(x^*(\theta)\). If this condition fails, we call $x^*(\theta)$ a \emph{degenerate optimistic minimizer}.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: x*(θ) is non-degenerate if the Riemannian Hessian of f restricted to S(θ) is positive definite there; degenerate otherwise.
nodes.label: def:degenerate-optimistic

nodes.name: Uniqueness does not imply Hölder continuity of ∇F
nodes.statement:
Consider the following smooth construction. For $	heta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, let \[ a(	heta):=  egin{cases}  rac14 \exp({-1/	heta^2})\sin(10/	heta), & 	heta
eq 0,\ 0, & 	heta=0, \end{cases} \qquad \eta(t):=  egin{cases} \operatorname{sign}(t)\exp({-1/t^2}), & t
eq 0,\ 0, & t=0, \end{cases} \] and define $\phi(t):=\int_0^t \eta(s)\,\mathrm ds$. Then $\eta,\phi\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$, $\eta=\phi'$ is strictly increasing, and $\phi''(0)=\eta'(0)=0$. Set \[ g(	heta,x):= ig(\|x\|^2-(1+	heta^2) ig)^2, \qquad f(	heta,x):=\phi(x_2)+a(	heta)x_2+ho(-x_1)+b ig(\|x\|^2-(1+	heta^2) ig), \] where \(b>0\) is arbitrary, $ho(s)=\exp({-1/s})$ for $s>0$, and $ho(s)=0$ for $s\le 0$. Thus $\mathcal{S}(	heta)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:\|x\|=r(	heta)\}$ with $r(	heta):=\sqrt{1+	heta^2}$. The added \(b\)-term is identically zero on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\), so it does not change the constrained minimization problem. As in \Cref{ex:kink}, the term $ho(-x_1)$ forces the optimistic minimizer to lie on the right semicircle, so minimizing $f(	heta,\cdot)$ over $\mathcal{S}(	heta)$ reduces to \[ \min_{|t|\le r(	heta)}  igl(\phi(t)+a(	heta)t igr). \] Since $\eta$ is strictly increasing, this scalar problem has a unique critical point determined by $\eta(t)+a(	heta)=0$, namely \[ t^\star(	heta)=  egin{cases} -\operatorname{sign}(a(	heta)) igl(\log(1/|a(	heta)|) igr)^{-1/2}, & a(	heta)
eq 0,\ 0, & a(	heta)=0. \end{cases} \] Moreover, $|t^\star(	heta)|\le(\log 4)^{-1/2}<1\le r(	heta)$, so this critical point is feasible and therefore is the unique minimizer. Hence the optimistic minimizer is unique for every $	heta$ and is \[ x^\star(	heta)= igl(\sqrt{r(	heta)^2-(t^\star(	heta))^2},\,t^\star(	heta) igr). \] By \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique}, the hyper-objective $F$ is $\mathcal C^1$. Since the \(b\)-term vanishes on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\), the scalar envelope formula gives $F'(	heta)=a'(	heta)t^\star(	heta)$. Let $	heta_k:=10/(k\pi)$, so $a(	heta_k)=0$ and $a'(	heta_k)
eq 0$. Then $F'(	heta_k)=0$. Since \(a'\) is continuous and nonzero at \(	heta_k\), and since \(	heta_k\) is a simple zero of \(a\), we have \(|a'(	heta)|\asymp1\) and \(|a(	heta)|\asymp|	heta-	heta_k|\) near \(	heta_k\). Therefore \[ |F'(	heta)-F'(	heta_k)| =|F'(	heta)| \asymp  rac{1}{\sqrt{\log(1/|	heta-	heta_k|)}} \qquad	ext{as }	heta	o	heta_k. \] Consequently, for every $\alpha>0$, \[  rac{|F'(	heta)-F'(	heta_k)|}{|	heta-	heta_k|^\alpha}	o\infty \qquad	ext{as }	heta	o	heta_k, \] because $|	heta-	heta_k|^\alpha\sqrt{\log(1/|	heta-	heta_k|)}	o 0$. Thus $
abla F$ is not locally $\alpha$-{H"older}\ continuous near $	heta_k$ for any $\alpha>0$, even though the optimistic minimizer is unique for every $	heta$. This example also shows why non-degeneracy must be intrinsic to \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\). At any zero \(	heta_k\), we have \(x^\star(	heta_k)=(r(	heta_k),0)\), and the unit tangent direction is \(v=(0,1)\). The ambient tangent Hessian satisfies \[  ig\langle v,
abla^2_{xx}f(	heta_k,x^\star(	heta_k))v igangle=2b>0, \] because the vanishing term \(b(\|x\|^2-r(	heta_k)^2)\) contributes \(2bI\) to the ambient Hessian. However, this term is zero on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta_k)\), so it contributes nothing to the restricted objective. The Riemannian Hessian of \(f(	heta_k,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(	heta_k)}\) in direction \(v\) is therefore \(0\), since the restricted scalar objective has second derivative \(\phi''(0)=0\). A condition based only on the ambient tangent Hessian would incorrectly classify this example as non-degenerate, even though the intrinsic restricted problem is degenerate and \(
abla F\) has no positive H"older modulus.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: A smooth construction with unique optimistic minimizer for every θ but ∇F not α-Hölder at θ_k for any α>0; ambient tangent Hessian positivity misses the degeneracy.
nodes.label: ex:unique-nonsmooth

nodes.name: Smoothness of the hyper-objective under a unique non-degenerate optimistic minimizer
nodes.statement: Let $f \in \mathcal C^2$, $g \in \mathcal C^3$ and satisfy \Cref{ass:plcirc}. Fix $\theta_0\in\Theta$ and set \(x_0:=x^\star(\theta_0)\). Suppose that \(x_0\) is the unique optimistic minimizer and is non-degenerate in the sense of \Cref{def:degenerate-optimistic}. Then there exists a neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $\theta_0$ and a (unique) $\mathcal C^1$ selection $x^\star:\mathcal U\to\mathbb{R}^d$ with $x^\star(\theta)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ such that $F(\theta)=f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))$ for all $\theta\in\mathcal U$. Consequently, \(\nabla F\) is locally Lipschitz.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: A unique non-degenerate optimistic minimizer gives a C^1 selection x*(θ) with F(θ)=f(θ,x*(θ)) locally, so ∇F is locally Lipschitz.
assumptions: Suppose that \(x_0\) is the unique optimistic minimizer and is non-degenerate in the sense of \Cref{def:degenerate-optimistic}
conclusions: there exists a neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $\theta_0$ and a (unique) $\mathcal C^1$ selection $x^\star:\mathcal U\to\mathbb{R}^d$ with $x^\star(\theta)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ such that $F(\theta)=f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))$ for all $\theta\in\mathcal U$
nodes.label: thm_hyp_obj_diff

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement:
Let \(x_0:=x^\star(	heta_0)\), and abbreviate \(\mathcal{T}_0:=\mathcal{T}_{x_0}^{	heta_0}\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0:=\mathcal{N}_{x_0}^{	heta_0}\). Let \(\dim(\mathcal{T}_0)=	exttt{k}\), and choose orthonormal bases \(U_{\mathcal{T}_0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d	imes	exttt{k}}\) and \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d	imes(d-	exttt{k})}\) spanning \(\mathcal{T}_0\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0\). \smallskip
oindent \emph{Step 1: parameterize \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) locally by solving the normal equations.} This is the same normal-chart construction as in the proof sketch of \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique}. The implicit function theorem yields a \(\mathcal C^2\) map \(v=\varphi(	heta,u)\), and hence the local chart \[ \psi(	heta,u):=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\varphi(	heta,u). \] On a sufficiently small neighborhood, \(u\mapsto\psi(	heta,u)\) parameterizes the local branch of \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) near \(x_0\). \smallskip
oindent \emph{Step 2: reduce the optimistic minimization to intrinsic coordinates.} Define the pullback objective \(	ilde f(	heta,u):=f(	heta,\psi(	heta,u))\). A point \(x=\psi(	heta,u)\) is a constrained critical point of \(f(	heta,\cdot)\) on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) if and only if \(
abla_u	ilde f(	heta,u)=0\). At \((	heta_0,0)\), this stationarity holds. The non-degeneracy assumption in \Cref{def:degenerate-optimistic} says precisely that the second-order variation of \(	ilde f(	heta_0,\cdot)\) at \(u=0\) is positive definite, so \(D_u(
abla_u	ilde f)(	heta_0,0)\) is invertible. Applying the implicit function theorem again gives a \(\mathcal C^1\) map \(u^\star(	heta)\), unique among nearby solutions, satisfying \[ 
abla_u	ilde f(	heta,u^\star(	heta))=0. \] Set \(x_{\mathrm{loc}}(	heta):=\psi(	heta,u^\star(	heta))\). This gives the unique local optimistic branch. The full proof then uses the strict value gap from the uniqueness of \(x_0\) on the compact set \(\mathcal{S}(	heta_0)\) to rule out competitors outside the chart patch, yielding the local identity \[ x^\star(	heta)=x_{\mathrm{loc}}(	heta), \qquad F(	heta)=f(	heta,x^\star(	heta)). \] \smallskip
oindent \emph{Step 3: obtain the hyper-gradient by the chain rule.} Since \(F(	heta)=f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\), the hyper-gradient follows from the chain rule. At a constrained minimizer, the tangential component of \(
abla_x f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\) vanishes, so only the normal component of \(D_	heta x^\star(	heta)\) is needed. Differentiating the lower-level stationarity condition \(
abla_x g(	heta,x^\star(	heta))=0\) and applying the pseudoinverse of \(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\) gives this normal sensitivity. Substitution gives \eqref{eq:hg_formula}. The same formula, together with constant rank and the normal spectral gap from \Cref{prop:geometry}, implies local Lipschitz continuity of \(
abla F\).
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: normal chart, implicit function theorem on the pullback stationarity (non-degeneracy), value gap to rule out far competitors, chain rule.

nodes.name: Fix bases
nodes.statement: Let \(x_0:=x^\star(\theta_0)\), and abbreviate \(\mathcal{T}_0:=\mathcal{T}_{x_0}^{\theta_0}\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0:=\mathcal{N}_{x_0}^{\theta_0}\). Let \(\dim(\mathcal{T}_0)=\texttt{k}\), and choose orthonormal bases \(U_{\mathcal{T}_0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times\texttt{k}}\) and \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times(d-\texttt{k})}\) spanning \(\mathcal{T}_0\) and \(\mathcal{N}_0\).
nodes.statement_short: Fix x_0 and orthonormal tangent/normal bases.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Normal chart
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 1: parameterize \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) locally by solving the normal equations.} This is the same normal-chart construction as in the proof sketch of \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique}. The implicit function theorem yields a \(\mathcal C^2\) map \(v=\varphi(\theta,u)\), and hence the local chart \[ \psi(\theta,u):=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\varphi(\theta,u). \] On a sufficiently small neighborhood, \(u\mapsto\psi(\theta,u)\) parameterizes the local branch of \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) near \(x_0\).
nodes.statement_short: Same normal-chart construction as for Theorem 3.1.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Intrinsic IFT for the selected branch
nodes.statement:
\emph{Step 2: reduce the optimistic minimization to intrinsic coordinates.} Define the pullback objective \(	ilde f(	heta,u):=f(	heta,\psi(	heta,u))\). A point \(x=\psi(	heta,u)\) is a constrained critical point of \(f(	heta,\cdot)\) on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) if and only if \(
abla_u	ilde f(	heta,u)=0\). At \((	heta_0,0)\), this stationarity holds. The non-degeneracy assumption in \Cref{def:degenerate-optimistic} says precisely that the second-order variation of \(	ilde f(	heta_0,\cdot)\) at \(u=0\) is positive definite, so \(D_u(
abla_u	ilde f)(	heta_0,0)\) is invertible. Applying the implicit function theorem again gives a \(\mathcal C^1\) map \(u^\star(	heta)\), unique among nearby solutions, satisfying \[ 
abla_u	ilde f(	heta,u^\star(	heta))=0. \] Set \(x_{\mathrm{loc}}(	heta):=\psi(	heta,u^\star(	heta))\). This gives the unique local optimistic branch. The full proof then uses the strict value gap from the uniqueness of \(x_0\) on the compact set \(\mathcal{S}(	heta_0)\) to rule out competitors outside the chart patch, yielding the local identity \[ x^\star(	heta)=x_{\mathrm{loc}}(	heta), \qquad F(	heta)=f(	heta,x^\star(	heta)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Non-degeneracy makes the pullback stationarity invertible; IFT gives a C^1 branch, and a value gap rules out far competitors.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Chain rule
nodes.statement:
\emph{Step 3: obtain the hyper-gradient by the chain rule.} Since \(F(	heta)=f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\), the hyper-gradient follows from the chain rule. At a constrained minimizer, the tangential component of \(
abla_x f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\) vanishes, so only the normal component of \(D_	heta x^\star(	heta)\) is needed. Differentiating the lower-level stationarity condition \(
abla_x g(	heta,x^\star(	heta))=0\) and applying the pseudoinverse of \(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\) gives this normal sensitivity. Substitution gives \eqref{eq:hg_formula}. The same formula, together with constant rank and the normal spectral gap from \Cref{prop:geometry}, implies local Lipschitz continuity of \(
abla F\).
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate F=f(θ,x*(θ)) and stationarity to get the formula and local Lipschitzness.
nodes.section: 3 Local Differentiability of the Hyper-objective

nodes.name: Unique and non-degenerate optimistic minimizer (global)
nodes.statement: For every $\theta\in\Theta$, the selected optimistic minimizer $x^\star(\theta)$ is unique and non-degenerate in the sense of \Cref{def:degenerate-optimistic}.
nodes.section: 4 \textsc{HG-MS}: a Select-then-Differentiate Algorithm
nodes.statement_short: For every θ∈Θ the optimistic minimizer x*(θ) is unique and non-degenerate.
nodes.label: ass:unique_min

nodes.name: Global smoothness of the hyper-objective
nodes.statement: Let $f \in \mathcal C^2$, $g \in \mathcal C^3$, and suppose \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:unique_min} hold. There exists $L_F<\infty$ such that $\|\nabla F(\theta)-\nabla F(\theta')\|\le L_F\|\theta-\theta'\|$, for all $\theta,\theta'\in\Theta$. In particular, $F$ is $L_F$-smooth on $\Theta$.
nodes.section: 4 \textsc{HG-MS}: a Select-then-Differentiate Algorithm
nodes.statement_short: Under PŁ° and global uniqueness/non-degeneracy, F is L_F-smooth on Θ.
conclusions: There exists $L_F<\infty$ such that $\|\nabla F(\theta)-\nabla F(\theta')\|\le L_F\|\theta-\theta'\|$, for all $\theta,\theta'\in\Theta$
nodes.label: prop:F-smooth

nodes.name: Projected hyper-gradient update
nodes.statement: Thus, the natural upper-level update is projected gradient descent, $\theta_{t+1}:=\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}\big(\theta_t-\alpha_t\nabla F(\theta_t)\big),$ with $\nabla F$ given by \cref{eq:hg_formula}.
nodes.section: 4 \textsc{HG-MS}: a Select-then-Differentiate Algorithm

nodes.name: Gibbs measure μ_θ^λ
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ is implicit, we approximate it using the Gibbs measure $\mu_\theta^\lambda(\delta x)\propto \exp\{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda\}\,\delta x$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design
also_stated_at: The Gibbs measure is \[ \mu_\theta^\lambda(\delta x)\propto \exp\{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda\}\,\delta x. \]

nodes.name: Best-of-N (BoN) selection
nodes.statement: Given samples $X_1,\ldots,X_N\sim\mu_\theta^\lambda$, we approximate optimistic selection by choosing $i^\star\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le N} f(\theta,X_i)$ and setting $\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta):=X_{i^\star}$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design
also_stated_at: First, it approximates the minima selection using a \emph{Best-of-N} (\texttt{BoN}\xspace) strategy: it draws $N$ samples from the Gibbs measure $\mu_\theta^\lambda(\mathrm{d}x)\propto \exp(-g(\theta,x)/\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}x,$ and outputs $\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta)$, the one achieving the smallest upper-level value $f(\theta, \cdot)$, as a proxy for $x^\star(\theta)$.

nodes.name: Comparison with superquantile-Gibbs value approximation
nodes.statement: Approximating $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ via $\mu_\theta^\lambda$ also appears in \citep{masiha2025superquantile}, but their goal is to approximate only the \textbf{value} of $F$. Here we must approximate the selected \textbf{solution} itself in order to compute a hyper-gradient, which requires a different analysis.
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design

nodes.name: Hessian H_t and gradient b_t at the selected point
nodes.statement: Let $H_t:=\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta_t,\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t))$ and $b_t:=\nabla_x f(\theta_t,\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t))$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design

nodes.name: Clipped implicit vector v_t
nodes.statement: For the theoretical guarantee, we also allow clipping, \(v_t:=\mathrm{Proj}_{\mathbb B_d(0;R_v)}(\tilde v_t)\).
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design

nodes.name: Hyper-gradient estimate ĥ_t
nodes.statement: The hyper-gradient estimate is then \begin{align} \widehat h_t := \nabla_\theta f(\theta_t,\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t)) - \nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta_t,\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t))v_t, \end{align} followed by a projected step on $\Theta$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design
nodes.statement_short: The estimate ĥ_t = ∇_θ f − ∇²_{θx} g · v_t at the selected point, followed by a projected step.

nodes.name: Hyper-gradient estimate at the selected point
nodes.statement: \widehat h_t := \nabla_\theta f(\theta_t,\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t)) - \nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta_t,\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t))v_t,
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design

nodes.statement:
\For{$t=0,1,2,\ldots$}
    \State Sample in parallel $X_{t,i}\gets \textsc{ULA}(\theta_t,g,X^{(0)}_{t,i},\lambda,K,h)$

nodes.statement_short: Iterate select-then-differentiate updates.

nodes.name: Parallel ULA sampling
nodes.statement: Sample in parallel $X_{t,i}\gets \textsc{ULA}(\theta_t,g,X^{(0)}_{t,i},\lambda,K,h)$

nodes.statement_short: Draw N candidates by running ULA chains on g(θ_t,·).

nodes.statement:
$i_t^\star\gets\arg\min_{1\le i\le N} f(\theta_t,X_{t,i})$; \quad
    $\hat{x}_N^\lambda(\theta_t)\gets X_{t,i_t^\star}$
nodes.section: 4.1 Algorithm Design
nodes.statement_short: Pick the candidate with the smallest upper-level value f.

nodes.name: Ridge CG solve
nodes.statement:
Solve
    \(

nodes.name: Convergence to near-stationarity with inexact hyper-gradients
nodes.statement: Suppose that $F$ is $L_F$-smooth on $\Theta$. Let $F_\star:=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}F(\theta)>-\infty$. Initialize $\theta_0\in\Theta$ and run the projected update $\theta_{t+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(\theta_t-\alpha \widehat h_t)$ with a constant stepsize $\alpha\le 1/L_F$ (last line of \Cref{alg:hg-minsel-lmc}), then \begin{align} \forall\ T \geq 1, \quad \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\big[\|\mathcal G_{\Theta}(\theta_t,\nabla F(\theta_t);\alpha)\|^2\big]\le \frac{8\,(F(\theta_0)-F_\star)}{\alpha T}+ \frac{10}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\big]. \end{align}

nodes.statement: Let \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:curvature_g,ass:unique_min,assum_sample_comp} hold. Fix \(\gamma>0\), choose a tube radius \(r(\gamma)=\mathcal{O}(\gamma)\) as in \Cref{lem:tube-invertibility}, and define \(\mathsf{D}_{t}:=\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\) and \(\mathcal E_t:=\{\mathsf{D}_{t}\le r(\gamma)\}\). Choose the clipping radius in \Cref{alg:hg-minsel-lmc} so that \(R_v=\mathcal{O}((L_{f,1}+\eta_t)/\gamma)\) as in \Cref{lem:off-tube-et}. Then for all \(t\), \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 &\le 3C_x^2\Big(1+\tfrac{2}{\gamma}+\tfrac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)}\Big)^{\!2} \mathbb E\big[\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big]\\ &\quad+\ \tfrac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\,\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\,\gamma^2+\ C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\, \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big], \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \(C_x,C_{\mathrm{lin}},C_{\mathrm{reg}}<\infty\) are stability constants depending on the global smoothness bounds and the normal spectral gap of \(\nabla^2_{xx}g\) on \(\Theta\), \(c>0\) is the uniform normal spectral gap from \Cref{prop:geometry}, and \(C_{\mathrm{off}}<\infty\) depends on \(C_{\theta x},D_{\theta x},\mathsf n_{\theta x}\) from \Cref{assum_sample_comp}.

u_i\) be the marginal law of \(X_i\), and write \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2:=\max_{1\le i\le N}R_2(
u_i\|\mu_	heta^\lambda)\). Assume \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), and let \(	ilde x\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le N}f(	heta,X_i)\) be the hard-selection output, with a measurable tie-breaking rule. ootnote{For example, one may choose the smallest index among all candidates attaining the minimum value of \(f(	heta,X_i)\), and set \(	ilde x\) to that candidate.} Then  egin{align} \mathbb E\|	ilde x-x^\star(	heta)\|^2 \ \le\ & 2e^{1/2}C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\log(1+N)

nodes.name: Total oracle complexity of HG-MS
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:curvature_g,assum_sample_comp,ass:unique_min} hold and run \textsc{HG-MS} with $\alpha=1/L_F$. Suppose \(\texttt{k}\ge 1\). Initialize every ULA chain from \(\lambda\)-scaled Gaussians (see \Cref{lem:gaussian-init-r3}). For all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), with the same parameter choices as in Appendix~\ref{append:param-tuning} ensuring $\sup_t\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$, \Cref{thm:main-et2-bound,prop:outer-inexact} yield an $\varepsilon$-stationarity guarantee after $T=\mathcal{O}\big(L_F(F(\theta_0)-F_\star)/\varepsilon^2\big)$ outer iterations. Moreover, under the explicit scaling $N=\lceil\varepsilon^{-4\texttt{k}}\rceil$, $\lambda=\varepsilon^{8}/\log(1+N)$, the square-root R\'enyi tolerance $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}=\varepsilon^{4+2\texttt{k}}$, \(\gamma=\varepsilon\), \(\eta_t=\varepsilon^2\), \(R_v=\Theta(\varepsilon^{-1})\), and $K=\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\lambda^{-4}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^{-2})$, each outer iteration uses $NK$ evaluations of $\nabla_x g$ (ULA), $N$ evaluations of $f$ (hard selection), and \(\#\mathrm{HVP}\) Hessian--vector products for CG. Hence the total oracle complexity for achieving an $\varepsilon$-stationary point is \( T(NK+N+\#\mathrm{HVP}) = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\Big(\varepsilon^{-42-8\texttt{k}}\Big). \)

conclusions: yield an $\varepsilon$-stationarity guarantee after $T=\mathcal{O}\big(L_F(F(\theta_0)-F_\star)/\varepsilon^2\big)$ outer iterations

nodes.name: On the k-dependence of the complexity
nodes.statement: The intrinsic dimension enters through the minima-selection subproblem, most visibly via the \(N^{-1/\texttt{k}}\) approximation term in \Cref{thm:main-et2-bound}. This matches the worst-case intuition that optimizing over a \(\texttt{k}\)-dimensional nonconvex minimizer manifold can reduce to \(\texttt{k}\)-dimensional global optimization and exhibit \(\Omega(\varepsilon^{-\texttt{k}})\)-type hardness \citep[Rem.~1.1]{masiha2025superquantile}.

nodes.name: Controlled two-source LLM source reweighting
nodes.statement: Let \(\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_1,\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_2\) be the two training sources and let \(\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}\) be the target validation set. The outer variable is a two-dimensional source-logit vector \(\theta\), with source weights \(\omega=\operatorname{softmax}(\theta)\), and the lower variable \(y\) is the full trainable GPT-2 (124M) parameter state. With token-level next-token loss \(\ell(y;\xi)\), the controlled source-reweighting objective is \[ g_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(\theta,y) := \sum_{s=1}^{2}\omega_s\,|\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_s|^{-1} \sum_{\xi\in\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_s}\ell(y;\xi), \qquad f_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(y) := |\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}|^{-1} \sum_{\xi\in\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}}\ell(y;\xi). \] Thus \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(\theta)=\arg\min_y g_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(\theta,y)\) is the set of lower-level GPT-2 states obtained under the current source mixture, and the optimistic upper objective is \(F_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(\theta)=\min_{y\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(\theta)} f_{\mathrm{ctrl}}(y)\).
nodes.section: 6.1 Controlled LLM source reweighting
nodes.statement_short: Optimistic bilevel source reweighting: outer softmax source weights, inner GPT-2 training loss, outer validation loss.
also_stated_at: Let \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}^2\) be source logits, \(\omega=\operatorname{softmax}(\theta)\in\Delta^1\) the induced source weights, and \(y\) the GPT-2 parameter vector. The lower-level and upper-level losses are \[ g(\theta,y) \;:=\; \sum_{s=1}^2 \omega_s\, \frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\ell(y;\xi^{\mathrm{tr}}_{s,i}), \qquad f(y) \;:=\; \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{val}}}\sum_{j=1}^{n_{\mathrm{val}}}\ell(y;\xi^{\mathrm{val}}_{j}). \] Here \(\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_s=\{\xi^{\mathrm{tr}}_{s,i}\}_{i=1}^{n_s}\) are the two training sources, \(\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}=\{\xi^{\mathrm{val}}_j\}_{j=1}^{n_{\mathrm{val}}}\) is the target validation set, and \(\ell(y;\xi)\) is the token-level language-model negative log-likelihood. Thus the lower level trains on a source-weighted mixture, while the upper level evaluates held-out target loss.

nodes.name: Multi-source LLM source reweighting
nodes.statement: Let \(p\) be the number of training sources, let \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}^p\) be source logits, let \(\omega=\operatorname{softmax}(\theta)\in\Delta^{p-1}\), and let \(y\) denote the LoRA adapter parameters for a fixed base model. With source datasets \(\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_1,\ldots,\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_p\) and held-out validation set \(\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}\), the reweighting stage solves the bilevel problem induced by \[ g_{\mathrm{rw}}(\theta,y) := \sum_{s=1}^{p}\omega_s\,|\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_s|^{-1} \sum_{\xi\in\mathcal D^{\mathrm{tr}}_s}\ell(y;\xi), \qquad f_{\mathrm{rw}}(y) := |\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}|^{-1} \sum_{\xi\in\mathcal D^{\mathrm{val}}}\ell_{\mathrm{val}}(y;\xi), \] namely \(F_{\mathrm{rw}}(\theta)=\min_{y\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{rw}}(\theta)}f_{\mathrm{rw}}(y)\) with \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{rw}}(\theta)=\arg\min_y g_{\mathrm{rw}}(\theta,y)\). Here \(\ell\) is the token-level next-token cross-entropy on source examples, and \(\ell_{\mathrm{val}}\) is the same loss on validation examples used only during source reweighting.

nodes.statement_short: Multi-source version: source logits θ∈R^p, LoRA adapter lower level, optimistic validation-loss upper level.

nodes.statement: \caption{\textsc{ULA}$(\theta,g,x^{(0)},\lambda,K,h)$} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \Require $\theta$; lower objective $g(\theta,\cdot)$; initial state $x^{(0)}$; temperature $\lambda$; steps $K$; stepsize $h$. \State $x\leftarrow x^{(0)}$. \For{$s=0$ to $K-1$} \State Draw $\xi^{(s)}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)$. \State $x\leftarrow x-h\nabla_x g(\theta,x)+\sqrt{2\lambda h}\,\xi^{(s)}$. \EndFor \State \textbf{return} $x$. \end{algorithmic}

nodes.name: Poincaré inequality
nodes.statement: A probability measure \(\mu\) over \(\mathbb{R}^d\) is said to satisfy the Poincar\'e inequality with constant \(C_{\mathrm{PI}}\) if, for every test function \(\varphi \in H^1(\mu)\), \begin{equation*} \int \Bigl(\varphi-\int \varphi \,\delta \mu\Bigr)^2 \delta \mu \;\le\; C_{\mathrm{PI}} \int \|\nabla \varphi\|^2 \,\delta \mu, \end{equation*} where \(H^1(\mu)\) denotes the Sobolev space weighted by \(\mu\).

nodes.name: λ-uniform Poincaré constant for low-temperature Gibbs measures under PŁ°
nodes.statement: Importantly, for Gibbs measures of the form \(\mu_\theta^\lambda(\delta x)\propto \exp(-g(\theta,x)/\lambda)\,\delta x\), \citet{gong2024poincare} show that under \(\texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) the corresponding Poincar\'e constant admits a bound independent of \(\lambda\) for all sufficiently small \(\lambda\le \lambda_0\).

nodes.name: Regularity of g (third derivative in a tube)
nodes.statement: There exist constants \(\rho>0\) and \(L_{g,3}<\infty\) such that for all \(\theta\in\Theta\), \(g(\theta,\cdot)\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{3}\) on the tube \(\{x:\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le \rho\}\) and \[ \sup_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le \rho}\ \big\|\nabla^3_{xxx}g(\theta,x)\big\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ \le\ L_{g,3}. \]

nodes.statement_short: g(θ,·) is C^3 on a ρ-tube around S(θ) with third derivative bounded by L_{g,3}.

nodes.name: Global regularity and growth for sampling and selection
nodes.statement: The following statements hold for all \(\theta\in\Theta\). \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]\setlength{\itemsep}{0.5pt} \item \textbf{Regularity of \(f\).} \(f\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) with respect to \((\theta,x)\). Moreover, \(f\) is \(L_{f,1}\)-Lipschitz and \(L_{f,2}\)-smooth with respect to \((\theta,x)\). Since \(\Theta\) is compact, this global Lipschitz condition implies the derived linear-growth bound \(|f(\theta,x)|\le C(1+\|x\|)\), uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta\). \item \textbf{Regularity of \(g\).} \(g\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{3}\) with respect to \((\theta,x)\). For every \(\theta\), the map \(x\mapsto g(\theta,x)\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) and \(L_{g,2}\)-smooth (i.e., \(\nabla_x g(\theta,\cdot)\) is \(L_{g,2}\)-Lipschitz). Moreover, for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\), \[ \|\partial_{\theta}g(\theta,x)\| \;\le\; C_{g}\|x\|^{\mathsf{n}_{g}} + D_{g}, \] for constants \(C_{g},D_{g}\ge 0\) and an integer \(\mathsf{n}_{g}\ge 1\). We also assume polynomial growth of the mixed derivative used in the hyper-gradient: \[ \|\nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta,x)\| \;\le\; C_{\theta x}\|x\|^{\mathsf{n}_{\theta x}} + D_{\theta x}, \] for constants \(C_{\theta x},D_{\theta x}\ge 0\) and an integer \(\mathsf{n}_{\theta x}\ge 0\). The Hessian \(\partial_x^2 g(\theta,x)\) is continuous with respect to \((\theta,x)\). Moreover, there exist constants \(\mathsf{D}>0\) and \(\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}>0\) such that for all \(\|x\|\ge \mathsf{D}\), \[ \frac{\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}}{2}\,\mathrm{dist}^{2}\!\bigl(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)\bigr) \;\le\; g(\theta,x)-\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}} g(\theta,z). \] W.l.o.g.\ we take \(\mathsf{D}\) large enough so that \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf{D})\) for all \(\theta\in\Theta\). \end{itemize}

nodes.statement_short: f Lipschitz and smooth; g C^3 and L_{g,2}-smooth with polynomially growing ∂_θ g and ∇²_{θx} g, continuous Hessian, and quadratic growth outside a ball.

nodes.name: Uniform restricted curvature from global non-degeneracy
nodes.statement: Let \(f\in\mathcal{C}^{2}\), \(g\in\mathcal{C}^{3}\), and suppose \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:unique_min} hold. For every \(\theta\in\Theta\), let \[ \bar f_\theta:\mathcal{S}(\theta)\to\mathbb{R}, \qquad \bar f_\theta(x):=f(\theta,x), \] denote the restriction of the upper-level objective to the lower-level solution manifold. There exists a constant \(m_{\mathrm R}>0\), independent of \(\theta\), such that \[ \big\langle v,\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\bar f_\theta(x^\star(\theta))[v]\big\rangle \ \ge\ m_{\mathrm R}\|v\|^2, \qquad \forall \theta\in\Theta,\ \forall v\in\mathcal{T}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta . \]
nodes.section: A.3 Regularity assumptions for sampling and selection
nodes.statement_short: Global non-degeneracy gives a θ-uniform lower bound m_R>0 on the Riemannian Hessian of f restricted to S(θ) at x*(θ).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4
nodes.statement: If \(\texttt{k}=0\), the tangent spaces are trivial and the claim is vacuous; take any \(m_{\mathrm R}>0\). Assume \(\texttt{k}\ge1\). For each \(\bar\theta\in\Theta\), \Cref{thm_hyp_obj_diff} and \Cref{ass:unique_min} give a neighborhood \(U_{\bar\theta}\), a \(\mathcal{C}^{1}\) selected branch \(x^\star(\theta)\), and a \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) local chart \(\psi_{\bar\theta}(\theta,u)\) for \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) near \(x^\star(\theta)\). Let \(u^\star(\theta)\) be the local coordinate satisfying \(x^\star(\theta)=\psi_{\bar\theta}(\theta,u^\star(\theta))\), and write \[ \tilde f_{\bar\theta}(\theta,u):=f(\theta,\psi_{\bar\theta}(\theta,u)), \qquad A_{\bar\theta}(\theta):=D_u\psi_{\bar\theta}(\theta,u^\star(\theta)). \] For a tangent vector \(v=A_{\bar\theta}(\theta)w\), the second variation of the pullback equals the Riemannian Hessian quadratic form, while \(\|v\|^2=w^\top A_{\bar\theta}(\theta)^\top A_{\bar\theta}(\theta)w\). Hence the local restricted curvature can be written as the smallest generalized eigenvalue \[ \mu_{\bar\theta}(\theta):= \min_{w\neq0} \frac{w^\top\nabla^2_{uu}\tilde f_{\bar\theta}(\theta,u^\star(\theta))w} {w^\top A_{\bar\theta}(\theta)^\top A_{\bar\theta}(\theta)w}. \] This quantity is continuous on \(U_{\bar\theta}\) and is positive at every point by the intrinsic non-degeneracy in \Cref{ass:unique_min}. Shrinking \(U_{\bar\theta}\) if necessary, there is a smaller neighborhood \(V_{\bar\theta}\) with \(\overline{V_{\bar\theta}}\subset U_{\bar\theta}\) on which \(\inf_{\theta\in V_{\bar\theta}}\mu_{\bar\theta}(\theta)>0\). Since \(\Theta\) is compact, choose a finite subcover \(V_{\bar\theta_1},\ldots,V_{\bar\theta_J}\) and set \[ m_{\mathrm R}:=\min_{1\le j\le J}\inf_{\theta\in V_{\bar\theta_j}}\mu_{\bar\theta_j}(\theta)>0. \] This gives the stated uniform lower bound.

nodes.statement_short: Local branches from Theorem 3.2 give a continuous positive generalized eigenvalue; a finite subcover of compact Θ gives the uniform constant.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition for uniform restricted curvature
nodes.statement: Thus the conclusion of \Cref{prop:uniform-riem-nondeg} holds, for instance, if the ambient tangent Hessian has a uniform positive margin and the second-fundamental-form correction is not too negative. Concretely, it is sufficient that for some \(m_{\mathrm{amb}}>0\) and \(\kappa<m_{\mathrm{amb}}\), \[ \langle v,\nabla^2_{xx}f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))v\rangle \ge m_{\mathrm{amb}}\|v\|^2, \qquad \langle \nabla_x f(\theta,x^\star(\theta)), \mathrm{II}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta(v,v)\rangle \ge -\kappa\|v\|^2 \] uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta\) and \(v\in\mathcal{T}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta\).
nodes.section: A.3 Regularity assumptions for sampling and selection
nodes.statement_short: Uniform restricted curvature holds if the ambient tangent Hessian has margin m_amb exceeding the negative part κ of the second-fundamental-form term.

nodes.name: Further sufficient condition via the second fundamental form bound
nodes.statement: Using \Cref{prop:second-fund-from-g}, a further sufficient condition is \[ m_{\mathrm{amb}} > \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|\nabla_x f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))\|\frac{L_{g,3}}{c}, \] where \(c\) is the uniform normal spectral gap in \Cref{prop:geometry}.

nodes.statement_short: It suffices that m_amb > sup ‖∇_x f(θ,x*(θ))‖ L_{g,3}/c.

nodes.name: Global PŁ forces singleton or unbounded minimizer sets
nodes.statement: For a \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) lower-level objective satisfying a global P\L\ condition, the minimizer set \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) can only be either a singleton or an unbounded subset of \(\mathbb{R}^d\) \citep{criscitiello2025,masiha2025superquantile}.

nodes.name: Penalty-perturbed lower-level objective h_σ
nodes.statement: We compare our standing assumptions to penalty-based differentiability analyses such as \citet{kwon2023penalty} and \citet{chen2023bilevel}, which study the perturbed lower-level objective \[ h_\sigma(\theta,x)\;:=\;g(\theta,x)+\sigma f(\theta,x),\qquad \sigma>0. \]

nodes.name: Proximal error bound is equivalent to a PŁ inequality
nodes.statement: In the smooth unconstrained setting, such a proximal error bound is equivalent to a P\L\ inequality \citep[Prop.~C.1]{chen2023bilevel}.

conclusions: such a proximal error bound is equivalent to a P\L\ inequality

nodes.name: No σ-uniform local PŁ constant for the penalized objective
nodes.statement: Fix \(\theta\) and let \(x^\star\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) be the unique optimistic minimizer. Assume there exists \(\bar x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) such that \(f(\theta,\bar x)>f(\theta,x^\star)\) (i.e., \(f(\theta,\cdot)\) is not constant on \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\)). Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be any neighborhood containing both \(x^\star\) and \(\bar x\). If \(h_\sigma(\theta,\cdot)\) satisfies a (local) P\L\ inequality on \(U\) with constant \(\mu_\sigma>0\), i.e., \[ h_\sigma(\theta,x)-\inf_{y\in U} h_\sigma(\theta,y)\ \le\ (2\mu_\sigma)^{-1}\,\|\nabla_x h_\sigma(\theta,x)\|^2 \qquad\forall x\in U, \] then \begin{equation} \mu_\sigma \ \le\ \frac{\sigma}{2}\cdot \frac{\|\nabla_x f(\theta,\bar x)\|^2}{f(\theta,\bar x)-f(\theta,x^\star)}. \end{equation} In particular, \(\mu_\sigma=\mathcal{O}(\sigma)\) as \(\sigma\downarrow 0\), so no constant bounded away from \(0\) can hold uniformly over \(\sigma\in(0,\sigma_0]\) on any such neighborhood.
nodes.section: B.1 Comparison with penalty-based differentiability analyses
nodes.statement_short: Any local PŁ constant of g+σf on a neighborhood containing x* and a higher-value manifold point is O(σ).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Fix such a neighborhood \(U\) and point \(\bar x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap U\). Since \(x^\star\in U\), we have \(\inf_{y\in U}h_\sigma(\theta,y)\le h_\sigma(\theta,x^\star)\), hence \[ h_\sigma(\theta,\bar x)-h_\sigma(\theta,x^\star) \ \le\ h_\sigma(\theta,\bar x)-\inf_{y\in U}h_\sigma(\theta,y). \] Applying the P\L\ inequality at \(x=\bar x\) and using that \(\bar x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) (so \(\nabla_x g(\theta,\bar x)=0\) and \(g(\theta,\bar x)=g(\theta,x^\star)\)) gives \[ \sigma\big(f(\theta,\bar x)-f(\theta,x^\star)\big) \ \le\ (2\mu_\sigma)^{-1}\,\|\sigma\nabla_x f(\theta,\bar x)\|^2, \] which rearranges to \eqref{eq:mu-sigma-upper-bound}.

nodes.name: Higher-value manifold points occur arbitrarily close to x*
nodes.statement: When \(\texttt{k}>0\) and \(x^\star\) is non-degenerate in the sense of \Cref{def:degenerate-optimistic}, such higher-value points occur arbitrarily close to \(x^\star\): along any nonzero tangent direction, the restricted objective \(f(\theta,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\) increases quadratically for sufficiently small geodesic displacement. Thus the obstruction above is genuinely local in the non-singleton manifold regime.

nodes.name: Minimizers converge
nodes.statement: We first note that every local choice of minimizers converges to the unique minimizer at \(\theta_0\). Let $\theta_n\to\theta_0$ and pick any minimizer $u_n\in\arg\min_{u\in U}\phi(\theta_n,u)$. By compactness of $U$, along a subsequence (not relabeled) we have $u_n\to \bar u\in U$. For any fixed $u\in U$, optimality of $u_n$ gives $\phi(\theta_n,u_n)\le \phi(\theta_n,u)$. Taking $n\to\infty$ and using continuity of $\phi$ yields $\phi(\theta_0,\bar u)\le \phi(\theta_0,u)$ for all $u\in U$, so $\bar u\in\arg\min_{u\in U}\phi(\theta_0,u)=\{u_0\}$. Thus every convergent subsequence of $u_n$ converges to $u_0$, hence $u_n\to u_0$.

We claim that the integrand is uniformly \(o(\|h\|)\). Indeed, since \(u_h	o u_0\) and \(	heta_0+s h	o	heta_0\) uniformly in \(s\in[0,1]\), continuity of \(
abla_	heta\phi\) at \((	heta_0,u_0)\) gives \[ \sup_{s\in[0,1]}  ig\| 
abla_	heta\phi(	heta_0+s h,u_h)-a  ig\| 	o0. \] Consequently, \[ \left| \phi(	heta_0+h,u_h)-\phi(	heta_0,u_h)-\langle a,hangle ight| \le \|h\| \sup_{s\in[0,1]}  ig\| 
abla_	heta\phi(	heta_0+s h,u_h)-a  ig\| =o(\|h\|). \]
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of ∇_θφ makes the integrand o(‖h‖) uniformly.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Uniform convergence
nodes.statement: Indeed, since \(u_h\to u_0\) and \(\theta_0+s h\to\theta_0\) uniformly in \(s\in[0,1]\), continuity of \(\nabla_\theta\phi\) at \((\theta_0,u_0)\) gives \[ \sup_{s\in[0,1]} \big\| \nabla_\theta\phi(\theta_0+s h,u_h)-a \big\| \to0. \]
nodes.statement_short: u_h→u_0 and continuity of ∇_θφ give a vanishing supremum.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Lower bound is first order
nodes.statement: Consequently, \[ \left| \phi(\theta_0+h,u_h)-\phi(\theta_0,u_h)-\langle a,h\rangle \right| \le \|h\| \sup_{s\in[0,1]} \big\| \nabla_\theta\phi(\theta_0+s h,u_h)-a \big\| =o(\|h\|). \]
nodes.statement_short: Hence the lower bound expands as ⟨a,h⟩+o(‖h‖).
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Conclude differentiability
nodes.statement: Combining the upper and lower bounds yields \[ F(\theta_0+h)-F(\theta_0)-\langle a,h\rangle=o(\|h\|), \] which proves differentiability of \(F\) at \(\theta_0\) with gradient \(a=\nabla_\theta\phi(\theta_0,u_0)\).
nodes.statement_short: Both bounds give F(θ_0+h)−F(θ_0)=⟨a,h⟩+o(‖h‖).
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Local parameter-dependent chart for the minimizer manifold
nodes.statement: Let \(g\in\mathcal{C}^{3}\) and let \Cref{ass:plcirc} hold. Fix \(\theta_0\in\Theta\) and \(x_0\in\mathcal{S}(\theta_0)\). Then, after shrinking the neighborhood if needed, there exist neighborhoods \(\mathcal U_\theta\) of \(\theta_0\), \(\mathcal U_u\) of \(0\in\mathbb{R}^{\texttt{k}}\), and \(\mathcal W\) of \(x_0\), together with a \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) map \[ \psi:\mathcal U_\theta\times\mathcal U_u\to\mathcal W, \qquad \psi(\theta_0,0)=x_0, \] such that \(u\mapsto\psi(\theta,u)\) is an embedded chart and \[ \mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W=\{\psi(\theta,u):u\in\mathcal U_u\}, \qquad \theta\in\mathcal U_\theta . \]
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1
nodes.statement_short: Near (θ_0,x_0), S(θ) is locally the image of a C^2 chart ψ(θ,·) over a fixed neighborhood of 0 in R^k.
conclusions: such that \(u\mapsto\psi(\theta,u)\) is an embedded chart and
nodes.label: lem:parametric-S-chart

nodes.name: Proof of the chart lemma
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1
nodes.statement_short: Implicit function theorem on the normal equations gives a chart of the normal critical set; a clopen argument in connected coordinates identifies it with S(θ).

nodes.name: Coordinates and normal map
nodes.statement: Let \(\mathcal{T}_0:=\mathcal{T}_{x_0}^{\theta_0}\), \(\mathcal{N}_0:=\mathcal{N}_{x_0}^{\theta_0}\), and choose orthonormal matrices \(U_{\mathcal{T}_0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times \texttt{k}}\) and \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times(d-\texttt{k})}\) spanning these spaces. For \((u,v)\) near \((0,0)\), write \(x(u,v):=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v\) and define \[ \Phi(\theta,u,v):=U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{\top}\nabla_x g(\theta,x(u,v)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Choose tangent/normal bases and define Φ = normal component of ∇_x g.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Implicit function theorem
nodes.statement: By \Cref{prop:geometry}, \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{\top}\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta_0,x_0)U_{\mathcal{N}_0}\) is positive definite. The implicit function theorem therefore gives a \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) map \(h(\theta,u)\), defined for \((\theta,u)\) near \((\theta_0,0)\), such that \(\Phi(\theta,u,h(\theta,u))=0\). Set \[ \psi(\theta,u):=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}h(\theta,u). \]
nodes.statement_short: Positive-definite normal Hessian lets the IFT solve v=h(θ,u); define ψ.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Local graph of the normal critical set
nodes.statement: For each fixed \(\theta\), this parametrizes the \(\texttt{k}\)-dimensional manifold \[ \widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta):=\{x:\ U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{\top}\nabla_x g(\theta,x)=0\} \] near \(x_0\). This last statement is local in the following precise sense. The IFT gives open neighborhoods \(\mathcal U_\theta^{0}\) of \(\theta_0\), \(\mathcal U_u^{0}\) of \(0\in\mathbb{R}^{\texttt{k}}\), and \(\mathcal U_v^{0}\) of \(0\in\mathbb{R}^{d-\texttt{k}}\) such that every solution of \(U_{\mathcal{N}_0}^{\top}\nabla_x g(\theta,x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v)=0\) with \((\theta,u,v)\in\mathcal U_\theta^{0}\times\mathcal U_u^{0}\times\mathcal U_v^{0}\) is uniquely represented as \(v=h(\theta,u)\). We now choose a connected open set \(\mathcal U_u\) containing \(0\) whose closure is contained in \(\mathcal U_u^{0}\), shrink the parameter neighborhood to \(\mathcal U_\theta\subseteq\mathcal U_\theta^{0}\), and choose an ambient neighborhood \(\mathcal W\) of \(x_0\) small enough so that every \(x\in\mathcal W\) can be written uniquely as \(x=x_0+U_{\mathcal{T}_0}u+U_{\mathcal{N}_0}v\) with \(u\in\mathcal U_u^{0}\) and \(v\in\mathcal U_v^{0}\), and such that the points of the graph over \(\mathcal U_u\) lie in \(\mathcal W\). With these choices, the local piece of \(\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\) inside \(\mathcal W\) is exactly the graph: for every \(\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta\), \[ \widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W = \{\psi(\theta,u):u\in\mathcal U_u\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: ψ parametrizes the normal critical set S̃(θ) as a graph inside W.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Inclusion S ⊆ S̃
nodes.statement: Finally, since every point of \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is a lower-level minimizer and hence satisfies the full first-order condition \(\nabla_x g(\theta,x)=0\), it satisfies the projected condition defining \(\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\) and therefore \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\).
nodes.statement_short: Minimizers satisfy the full first-order condition, so S(θ)∩W ⊆ S̃(θ)∩W.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Set up Z_θ
nodes.statement: It remains to show that this inclusion is equality on a smaller neighborhood. By the fixed-dimension conclusion in \Cref{prop:geometry} and the local Hausdorff continuity of the solution manifolds \citep[Lem.~3.2]{masiha2025superquantile}, after shrinking \(\mathcal U_\theta\) and \(\mathcal W\), for every \(\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta\), \[ \dim\mathcal{S}(\theta)=\texttt{k} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\neq\emptyset . \] For such a \(\theta\), define \[ Z_\theta:=\{u\in\mathcal U_u:\psi(\theta,u)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: By constant dimension and Hausdorff continuity S(θ)∩W≠∅; define Z_θ.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Z_θ nonempty and closed
nodes.statement: The set \(Z_\theta\) records which points of the graph for \(\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\) are genuine lower-level minimizers. It is nonempty by the local Hausdorff-continuity step above: since \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\neq\emptyset\) and \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\), at least one point of \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\) has the form \(\psi(\theta,u)\). It is closed relative to \(\mathcal U_u\) because \[ Z_\theta=\{u\in\mathcal U_u:\psi(\theta,u)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\} = \psi_\theta^{-1}(\mathcal{S}(\theta))\cap\mathcal U_u, \qquad \psi_\theta(u):=\psi(\theta,u), \] where \(\psi_\theta\) is continuous and \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is compact, hence closed, by \Cref{prop:geometry}.
nodes.statement_short: Z_θ is nonempty and relatively closed.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Z_θ open
nodes.statement: We next show that \(Z_\theta\) is open. Take \(u_1\in Z_\theta\) and set \(x_1:=\psi(\theta,u_1)\). Near \(x_1\), both \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) and \(\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\) are embedded \(\texttt{k}\)-dimensional submanifolds, and we already know that \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\). Consider the inclusion map \[ i:\mathcal{S}(\theta)\hookrightarrow\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta),\qquad i(x)=x. \] This map is smooth because both manifolds are embedded submanifolds of the same ambient space. Its derivative at \(x_1\) is the identity map on tangent vectors: \[ D i(x_1):\mathcal{T}_{x_1}\mathcal{S}(\theta)\to \mathcal{T}_{x_1}\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta),\qquad v\mapsto v. \] Since the two tangent spaces both have dimension \(\texttt{k}\), this derivative is an isomorphism. The inverse function theorem for manifolds therefore gives a neighborhood \(\mathcal O_S\) of \(x_1\) in \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) such that \(i(\mathcal O_S)\) is an open neighborhood of \(x_1\) in \(\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\). But \(i\) is just inclusion, so \(i(\mathcal O_S)=\mathcal O_S\subseteq\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Thus some neighborhood of \(x_1\) inside \(\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\) is contained in \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Pulling this neighborhood back through the chart \(u\mapsto\psi(\theta,u)\), we obtain a neighborhood of \(u_1\) contained in \(Z_\theta\). Since this argument works for every \(u_1\in Z_\theta\), each point of \(Z_\theta\) has a relative neighborhood in \(\mathcal U_u\) contained in \(Z_\theta\). Thus \(Z_\theta\) is open in \(\mathcal U_u\).
nodes.statement_short: The inclusion map between equal-dimensional manifolds is a local diffeomorphism, so Z_θ is open.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Connectedness
nodes.statement: Now \(Z_\theta\) is nonempty and is both closed and open relative to \(\mathcal U_u\). If \(Z_\theta\neq\mathcal U_u\), then \(Z_\theta\) and \(\mathcal U_u\setminus Z_\theta\) would form a separation of \(\mathcal U_u\): two nonempty disjoint relatively open sets whose union is \(\mathcal U_u\). This contradicts the connectedness of \(\mathcal U_u\). Hence \(Z_\theta=\mathcal U_u\). Therefore every point of the local graph \(\{\psi(\theta,u):u\in\mathcal U_u\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Together with the earlier inclusion \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W\), this gives \[ \mathcal{S}(\theta)\cap\mathcal W = \{\psi(\theta,u):u\in\mathcal U_u\}, \] after shrinking \(\mathcal W\) within the chart neighborhood if needed.
nodes.statement_short: Connectedness of U_u gives Z_θ=U_u, so the inclusion is an equality.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1

After possibly shrinking $\mathcal U_	heta$, we may assume $x^\star(	heta)$ lies in the chart patch for all $	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$. \emph{Step 2b: fixed-domain reduction.} Write $x^\star(	heta)=\psi(	heta,u^\star(	heta))$ for some $u^\star(	heta)\in\mathcal U_u$. The convergence \(x^\star(	heta)	o x_0\) from Step~2a and the fact that \(u\mapsto\psi(	heta,u)\) is a local chart imply \(u^\star(	heta)	o0\) as \(	heta	o	heta_0\). Hence, after shrinking \(\mathcal U_	heta\) once more, we may choose a compact neighborhood \(U\subset\mathcal U_u\) of \(0\) such that \(u^\star(	heta)\in U\) for all \(	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta\). Hence, after shrinking \(\mathcal U_	heta\) once more, we may choose a compact neighborhood \(U\subset\mathcal U_u\) of \(0\) such that \(u^\star(	heta)\in U\) for all \(	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta\). Then, for all $	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$, \[ F(	heta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)} f(	heta,x)=\min_{u\in U}	ilde f(	heta,u). \] \emph{Step 2c: differentiability via an envelope lemma.} Since $f$ is $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ and $\psi$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$, $	ilde f$ is continuous and $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ in $	heta$ with continuous $
abla_	heta	ilde f$. We claim that for every $	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$, the minimizer of $u\mapsto 	ilde f(	heta,u)$ over $U$ is unique and equals $u^\star(	heta)$. Applying \Cref{lem:envelope-unique} at each $	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$ yields that $F$ is differentiable on $\mathcal U_	heta$ and  egin{equation} 
abla F(	heta)=
abla_	heta 	ilde f(	heta,u^\star(	heta)) \qquad	ext{for all }	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta. \end{equation} Importantly, \eqref{eq:env-grad} does \emph{not} require differentiability of $	heta\mapsto u^\star(	heta)$. \emph{Step 2d: continuity of $
abla F$ (hence $F\in\mathcal{C}^{1}$).} We show that $	heta\mapsto u^\star(	heta)$ is continuous on $\mathcal U_	heta$. Fix $ ar	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$ and let $	heta_n	o ar	heta$ with $	heta_n\in\mathcal U_	heta$. By compactness of $U$, along a subsequence (not relabeled) we have $u^\star(	heta_n)	o  ar u\in U$. Optimality of $u^\star(	heta_n)$ gives $	ilde f(	heta_n,u^\star(	heta_n))\le 	ilde f(	heta_n,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Sending $n	o\infty$ and using continuity of $	ilde f$ yields $	ilde f( ar	heta, ar u)\le 	ilde f( ar	heta,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Thus $ ar u\in\arg\min_{u\in U}	ilde f( ar	heta,u)=\{u^\star( ar	heta)\}$, hence $ ar u=u^\star( ar	heta)$. Therefore $u^\star(	heta_n)	o u^\star( ar	heta)$, proving continuity. Since $

nodes.statement_short: Keep x*(θ) in the chart, reduce to a fixed compact domain, apply the envelope lemma, show continuity.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Need to stay in the patch
nodes.statement: Step 1 only gives a $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ chart near $x_0$. Since $u\mapsto \psi(\theta,u)$ parametrizes only the part of $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ near $x_0$, we first show that the minimizer stays in this chart patch for $\theta$ close to $\theta_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The chart only covers S(θ) near x_0.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: x*(θ) stays near x_0
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 2a: $x^\star(\theta)$ stays near $x_0$.} Let $\theta_n\to\theta_0$ with $\theta_n\in\mathcal U_\theta$ and set $x_n:=x^\star(\theta_n)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta_n)\subseteq\mathcal V$. By compactness of $\mathcal V$, along a subsequence (not relabeled) we have $x_n\to \bar x\in\mathcal V$. For any fixed $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, since $x_n\in\arg\min_x g(\theta_n,x)$ we have $g(\theta_n,x_n)\le g(\theta_n,y)$. Taking $n\to\infty$ and using continuity of $g$ yields $g(\theta_0,\bar x)\le g(\theta_0,y)$ for all $y$, hence $\bar x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta_0)$. Moreover, $\psi(\theta_n,0)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta_n)$ is a feasible competitor for the optimistic problem at $\theta_n$, so \[ f(\theta_n,x_n)=F(\theta_n)\ \le\ f(\theta_n,\psi(\theta_n,0)). \] Sending $n\to\infty$ and using continuity of $f$ and $\psi$ gives $f(\theta_0,\bar x)\le f(\theta_0,x_0)=F(\theta_0)$. By uniqueness of $x_0\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta_0)} f(\theta_0,x)$ and $\bar x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta_0)$, we conclude $\bar x=x_0$. Thus every convergent subsequence of $x_n$ converges to $x_0$, hence $x_n\to x_0$. After possibly shrinking $\mathcal U_\theta$, we may assume $x^\star(\theta)$ lies in the chart patch for all $\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta$.
nodes.statement_short: Compactness and uniqueness force x*(θ_n)→x_0.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Fixed-domain reduction
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 2b: fixed-domain reduction.} Write $x^\star(\theta)=\psi(\theta,u^\star(\theta))$ for some $u^\star(\theta)\in\mathcal U_u$. The convergence \(x^\star(\theta)\to x_0\) from Step~2a and the fact that \(u\mapsto\psi(\theta,u)\) is a local chart imply \(u^\star(\theta)\to0\) as \(\theta\to\theta_0\). Hence, after shrinking \(\mathcal U_\theta\) once more, we may choose a compact neighborhood \(U\subset\mathcal U_u\) of \(0\) such that \(u^\star(\theta)\in U\) for all \(\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta\). Define $\tilde f(\theta,u):=f(\theta,\psi(\theta,u))$. Then, for all $\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta$, \[ F(\theta)=\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)=\min_{u\in U}\tilde f(\theta,u). \]
nodes.statement_short: Write x*=ψ(θ,u*) with u* in a compact U and F=min_U f̃.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Envelope lemma
nodes.statement:

abla_	heta	ilde f$. We claim that for every $	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$, the minimizer of $u\mapsto 	ilde f(	heta,u)$ over $U$ is unique and equals $u^\star(	heta)$. Indeed, by Step~2b, \[ F(	heta)=\min_{u\in U}	ilde f(	heta,u), \qquad 	ilde f(	heta,u^\star(	heta))=f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))=F(	heta), \] so $u^\star(	heta)$ is a minimizer. Conversely, if $ ar u\in U$ also minimizes $	ilde f(	heta,\cdot)$, then \[ f(	heta,\psi(	heta, ar u))=	ilde f(	heta, ar u)=F(	heta), \] so $\psi(	heta, ar u)\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)} f(	heta,x)$. By the uniqueness assumption in \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique}, this implies $\psi(	heta, ar u)=x^\star(	heta)=\psi(	heta,u^\star(	heta))$. Since $u\mapsto \psi(	heta,u)$ is a chart parametrization on the patch, it is injective, hence $ ar u=u^\star(	heta)$. nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Regularity of f̃
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 2c: differentiability via an envelope lemma.} Since $f$ is $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ and $\psi$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$, $\tilde f$ is continuous and $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ in $\theta$ with continuous $\nabla_\theta\tilde f$.

nodes.name: Unique minimizer on U
nodes.statement: We claim that for every $\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta$, the minimizer of $u\mapsto \tilde f(\theta,u)$ over $U$ is unique and equals $u^\star(\theta)$. Indeed, by Step~2b, \[ F(\theta)=\min_{u\in U}\tilde f(\theta,u), \qquad \tilde f(\theta,u^\star(\theta))=f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))=F(\theta), \] so $u^\star(\theta)$ is a minimizer. Conversely, if $\bar u\in U$ also minimizes $\tilde f(\theta,\cdot)$, then \[ f(\theta,\psi(\theta,\bar u))=\tilde f(\theta,\bar u)=F(\theta), \] so $\psi(\theta,\bar u)\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)$. By the uniqueness assumption in \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique}, this implies $\psi(\theta,\bar u)=x^\star(\theta)=\psi(\theta,u^\star(\theta))$. Since $u\mapsto \psi(\theta,u)$ is a chart parametrization on the patch, it is injective, hence $\bar u=u^\star(\theta)$.
nodes.statement_short: u*(θ) is the unique minimizer of f̃(θ,·) on U.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: u* is a minimizer
nodes.statement: Indeed, by Step~2b, \[ F(\theta)=\min_{u\in U}\tilde f(\theta,u), \qquad \tilde f(\theta,u^\star(\theta))=f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))=F(\theta), \] so $u^\star(\theta)$ is a minimizer.

nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Any minimizer maps into O(θ)

nodes.name: Uniqueness

nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Injectivity
nodes.statement: Since $u\mapsto \psi(\theta,u)$ is a chart parametrization on the patch, it is injective, hence $\bar u=u^\star(\theta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity of the chart gives ū=u*(θ).
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Apply envelope lemma
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{lem:envelope-unique} at each $\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta$ yields that $F$ is differentiable on $\mathcal U_\theta$ and \begin{equation} \nabla F(\theta)=\nabla_\theta \tilde f(\theta,u^\star(\theta)) \qquad\text{for all }\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta. \end{equation} Importantly, \eqref{eq:env-grad} does \emph{not} require differentiability of $\theta\mapsto u^\star(\theta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4 at each θ gives the envelope gradient formula.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Continuity of ∇F
nodes.statement:
\emph{Step 2d: continuity of $
abla F$ (hence $F\in\mathcal{C}^{1}$).} We show that $	heta\mapsto u^\star(	heta)$ is continuous on $\mathcal U_	heta$. Fix $ ar	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta$ and let $	heta_n	o ar	heta$ with $	heta_n\in\mathcal U_	heta$. By compactness of $U$, along a subsequence (not relabeled) we have $u^\star(	heta_n)	o  ar u\in U$. Optimality of $u^\star(	heta_n)$ gives $	ilde f(	heta_n,u^\star(	heta_n))\le 	ilde f(	heta_n,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Sending $n	o\infty$ and using continuity of $	ilde f$ yields $	ilde f( ar	heta, ar u)\le 	ilde f( ar	heta,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Thus $ ar u\in\arg\min_{u\in U}	ilde f( ar	heta,u)=\{u^\star( ar	heta)\}$, hence $ ar u=u^\star( ar	heta)$. Therefore $u^\star(	heta_n)	o u^\star( ar	heta)$, proving continuity. Since $

nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: u* is continuous
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 2d: continuity of $\nabla F$ (hence $F\in\mathcal{C}^{1}$).} We show that $\theta\mapsto u^\star(\theta)$ is continuous on $\mathcal U_\theta$. Fix $\bar\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta$ and let $\theta_n\to\bar\theta$ with $\theta_n\in\mathcal U_\theta$. By compactness of $U$, along a subsequence (not relabeled) we have $u^\star(\theta_n)\to \bar u\in U$. Optimality of $u^\star(\theta_n)$ gives $\tilde f(\theta_n,u^\star(\theta_n))\le \tilde f(\theta_n,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Sending $n\to\infty$ and using continuity of $\tilde f$ yields $\tilde f(\bar\theta,\bar u)\le \tilde f(\bar\theta,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Thus $\bar u\in\arg\min_{u\in U}\tilde f(\bar\theta,u)=\{u^\star(\bar\theta)\}$, hence $\bar u=u^\star(\bar\theta)$. Therefore $u^\star(\theta_n)\to u^\star(\bar\theta)$, proving continuity.
nodes.statement_short: Compactness and uniqueness give continuity of u*.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Subsequence
nodes.statement: Fix $\bar\theta\in\mathcal U_\theta$ and let $\theta_n\to\bar\theta$ with $\theta_n\in\mathcal U_\theta$. By compactness of $U$, along a subsequence (not relabeled) we have $u^\star(\theta_n)\to \bar u\in U$.
nodes.statement_short: Take θ_n→θ̄ and a convergent subsequence of u*(θ_n).
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Limit is the minimizer
nodes.statement: Optimality of $u^\star(\theta_n)$ gives $\tilde f(\theta_n,u^\star(\theta_n))\le \tilde f(\theta_n,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Sending $n\to\infty$ and using continuity of $\tilde f$ yields $\tilde f(\bar\theta,\bar u)\le \tilde f(\bar\theta,u)$ for all $u\in U$. Thus $\bar u\in\arg\min_{u\in U}\tilde f(\bar\theta,u)=\{u^\star(\bar\theta)\}$, hence $\bar u=u^\star(\bar\theta)$. Therefore $u^\star(\theta_n)\to u^\star(\bar\theta)$, proving continuity.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit in optimality; uniqueness identifies the limit.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1

nodes.name: Conclude C^1

nodes.statement_short: Continuity of ∇_θ f̃ and u* gives continuity of ∇F.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1
