nodes.name: Global C^1 sufficient condition
nodes.statement: Assume $\Theta$ is compact and $\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)} f(\theta,x)$ is a singleton for every $\theta\in\Theta$. If, in addition, the lower-level solution manifolds are uniformly bounded in the sense that there exists a compact set $\mathcal V\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal V$ for all $\theta\in\Theta$ (e.g., $\mathcal V=\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)$ under \Cref{assum_sample_comp}), then $F$ is $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ on $\Theta$ and \eqref{eq:hg_formula} holds for all $\theta\in\Theta$. Indeed, \Cref{thm:F-diff-unique} applies at each $\theta_0\in\Theta$; compactness of $\Theta$ allows us to extract a finite subcover of the resulting local $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ neighborhoods.
nodes.section: C.1 Proof of 3.1
nodes.statement_short: Global uniqueness plus uniformly bounded solution manifolds give F∈C^1(Θ) by a finite subcover of local C^1 neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement:
Let \(x_0:=x^\star(	heta_0)\). We prove the result in four steps. First, we write the moving manifold \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) in fixed local coordinates. Second, we use intrinsic non-degeneracy and the implicit function theorem to obtain a \(\mathcal C^1\) local selected branch. Third, we use uniqueness at \(	heta_0\) to show that this local branch is the global optimistic branch for nearby parameters. Finally, we differentiate through lower-level stationarity to obtain the pseudoinverse formula and local Lipschitzness of \(
abla F\). \paragraph{Step 1: Reduce the moving-manifold problem to fixed local coordinates.} By \Cref{lem:parametric-S-chart}, after shrinking neighborhoods if necessary, there are an open neighborhood \(\mathcal U_	heta\) of \(	heta_0\), a bounded convex open ball \(\mathcal U_u\subset\mathbb{R}^{	exttt{k}}\) around \(0\) whose closure lies in a slightly larger coordinate domain, an open neighborhood \(\mathcal W\) of \(x_0\), and a \(\mathcal C^2\) map \[ \psi:\mathcal U_	heta	imes\mathcal U_u	o\mathcal W, \qquad \psi(	heta_0,0)=x_0, \] such that, for every \(	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta\), \[ \mathcal{S}(	heta)\cap\mathcal W=\{\psi(	heta,u):u\in\mathcal U_u\}. \] We keep the same symbol \(\psi\) for its extension to this slightly larger coordinate domain and shrink \(\mathcal U_u\), if needed, so that \(u\mapsto\psi(	heta,u)\) is injective on a neighborhood of \(\overline{\mathcal U_u}\) for all \(	heta\in\mathcal U_	heta\). In these coordinates, the local restriction of the upper-level objective to \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) is \[ 	ilde f(	heta,u):=f(	heta,\psi(	heta,u)). \] Since \(f\in\mathcal C^2\) and \(\psi\in\mathcal C^2\), we have \(	ilde f\in\mathcal C^2\). \paragraph{Step 2: Non-degeneracy gives a smooth local minimizer branch.} At \(	heta=	heta_0\), the point \(u=0\) corresponds to \(x_0\). Since \(x_0\) minimizes \(f(	heta_0,\cdot)\) over \(\mathcal{S}(	heta_0)\), \(u=0\) is a local minimizer of \(	ilde f(	heta_0,\cdot)\), and hence \[ 
abla_u	ilde f(	heta_0,0)=0. \] Let \(A:=D_u\psi(	heta_0,0)\). Then \(A\) has full column rank and \(\mathrm{range}(A)=\mathcal{T}_{x_0}^{	heta_0}\), because \(u\mapsto\psi(	heta_0,u)\) is an embedded chart for \(\mathcal{S}(	heta_0)\) around \(x_0\). nodes.name: Plan

Second, we use intrinsic non-degeneracy and the implicit function theorem to obtain a \(\mathcal C^1\) local selected branch. Third, we use uniqueness at \(\theta_0\) to show that this local branch is the global optimistic branch for nearby parameters. Finally, we differentiate through lower-level stationarity to obtain the pseudoinverse formula and local Lipschitzness of \(\nabla F\).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement:
For each $ ar	heta\in\Theta$, \Cref{ass:unique_min} and \Cref{thm_hyp_obj_diff} give an ambient open neighborhood $W_{ ar	heta}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m$ on which the local selected branch exists and $F$ is smooth. Choose a smaller open neighborhood $\mathcal U_{ ar	heta}$ of $ ar	heta$ such that $\overline{\mathcal U_{ ar	heta}}\cap\Theta\subset W_{ ar	heta}$, and set $V_{ ar	heta}:=\mathcal U_{ ar	heta}\cap\Theta$. On this compact patch there is a finite constant $L_{ ar	heta}$ such that  egin{equation} \|
abla F(	heta)-
abla F(	heta')\| \le L_{ ar	heta}\|	heta-	heta'\|, \qquad  orall\,	heta,	heta'\in V_{ ar	heta}. \end{equation} The local constant above can be obtained in the standard hyper-gradient way from the closed-form formula. On such a local patch, let $x^\star_{ ar	heta}$ denote the selected $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ branch and define $z(	heta):=(	heta,x^\star_{ ar	heta}(	heta))$. Write, for compactness, \[ a(z):=
abla_	heta f(z),\qquad A(z):=
abla^2_{	heta x}g(z),\qquad P(z):= ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(z) ig]^\dagger,\qquad b(z):=
abla_x f(z). \] After shrinking the local patch if necessary, choose finite constants $\kappa_{ ar	heta}$, $B_{A, ar	heta},B_{P, ar	heta},B_{b, ar	heta}$ and $L_{a, ar	heta},L_{A, ar	heta},L_{P, ar	heta},L_{b, ar	heta}$ such that \[ \|z(	heta)-z(	heta')\| \le \kappa_{ ar	heta}\|	heta-	heta'\|, \] and, on the local graph $\{z(	heta):	heta\in V_{ ar	heta}\}$, the functions $a,A,P,b$ have Lipschitz constants $L_{a, ar	heta},L_{A, ar	heta},L_{P, ar	heta},L_{b, ar	heta}$, while $A,P,b$ are bounded by $B_{A, ar	heta},B_{P, ar	heta},B_{b, ar	heta}$. The pseudoinverse constants are finite because, along this local graph, the Hessian $
abla^2_{xx}g$ has constant rank and its nonzero eigenvalues are bounded away from zero by the normal spectral gap in \Cref{prop:geometry}. We use the hyper-gradient formula \[ 
abla F(	heta)=a(z(	heta))-A(z(	heta))P(z(	heta))b(z(	heta)) \] as follows. Fix $	heta,	heta'\in V_{ ar	heta}$ and abbreviate $z:=z(	heta)$ and $z':=z(	heta')$. Then  egin{align*} 
abla F(	heta)-
abla F(	heta') &= a(z)-a(z') - ig(A(z)P(z)b(z)-A(z')P(z')b(z') ig), \end{align*} and the product difference is decomposed by adding and subtracting $A(z')P(z)b(z)$ and $A(z')P(z')b(z)$:  egin{align*} A(z)P(z)b(z)-A(z')P(z')b(z') &=  ig(A(z)-A(z') ig)P(z)b(z)\ &\quad +A(z') ig(P(z)-P(z') ig)b(z)\ &\quad +A(z')P(z') ig(b(z)-b(z') ig). \end{align*} Therefore, using the local Lipschitz and boundedness constants above,  egin{align*} \|
abla F(	heta)-
abla F(	heta')\| &\le \|a(z)-a(z')\| +\|A(z)-A(z')\|\,\|P(z)\|\,\|b(z)\|\ &\quad +\|A(z')\|\,\|P(z)-P(z')\|\,\|b(z)\|\ &\quad +\|A(z')\|\,\|P(z')\|\,\|b(z)-b(z')\|\ &\le \Big( L_{a, ar	heta} +L_{A, ar	heta}B_{P, ar	heta}B_{b, ar	heta} +B_{A, ar	heta}L_{P, ar	heta}B_{b, ar	heta} +B_{A, ar	heta}B_{P, ar	heta}L_{b, ar	heta} \Big)\|z-z'\|. \end{align*} Combining this with $\|z-z'\|\le\kappa_{ ar	heta}\|	heta-	heta'\|$ yields the explicit local bound  egin{equation} L_{ ar	heta} \;:=\; \kappa_{ ar	heta} \Big( L_{a, ar	heta} +L_{A, ar	heta}B_{P, ar	heta}B_{b, ar	heta} +B_{A, ar	heta}L_{P, ar	heta}B_{b, ar	heta} +B_{A, ar	heta}B_{P, ar	heta}L_{b, ar	heta} \Big), \end{equation} which is one admissible choice in \eqref{eq:local-smoothness-cover}. The sets $\{V_{ ar	heta}\}_{ ar	heta\in\Theta}$ form an open cover of the compact metric space $\Theta$ (with the relative topology). Choose a finite subcover $V_1,\ldots,V_J$, with corresponding local constants $L_1,\ldots,L_J$, and define  egin{equation} L_F := \max_{1\le j\le J} L_j \quad \left( 	ext{equivalently, one may take } L_j = \sup_{\substack{	heta,	heta'\in V_j\ 	heta
eq	heta'}}  rac{\|
abla F(	heta)-
abla F(	heta')\|}{\|	heta-	heta'\|} ight). \end{equation} This quantity is finite by the local smoothness bound \eqref{eq:local-smoothness-cover}. It remains to show that the local constants globalize without any additional Lipschitz assumption on the selected branch. Let $\delta>0$ be a Lebesgue number of the finite cover $\{V_j\}_{j=1}^J$ of $\Theta$: every subset of $\Theta$ with diameter strictly smaller than $\delta$ is contained in some $V_j$. Fix $	heta,	heta'\in\Theta$. If $	heta=	heta'$, the claim is trivial. Otherwise, since $\Theta$ is convex, the line segment \[ 	heta_s:=	heta+s(	heta'-	heta),\qquad s\in[0,1], \] is contained in $\Theta$. Choose an integer $M$ such that $\|	heta-	heta'\|/M<\delta$, and set $	heta_\ell:=	heta_{\ell/M}$ for $\ell=0,\ldots,M$. For each $\ell$, the two-point set $\{	heta_\ell,	heta_{\ell+1}\}$ has diameter below $\delta$, so it lies in some $V_{j_\ell}$. Applying the local bound on that set gives \[ \|
abla F(	heta_{\ell+1})-
abla F(	heta_\ell)\| \le L_{j_\ell}\|	heta_{\ell+1}-	heta_\ell\| \le L_F\|	heta_{\ell+1}-	heta_\ell\|. \] Summing over $\ell=0,\ldots,M-1$ yields \[ \|
abla F(	heta')-
abla F(	heta)\| \le L_F\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\|	heta_{\ell+1}-	heta_\ell\| = L_F\|	heta'-	heta\|, \] which proves the global smoothness claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement:
Fix $T\ge 1$ and write $g_t:=\widehat h_t=
abla F(	heta_t)+e_t$. Define the (used) gradient mapping \[ \widetilde{\mathcal G}_t :=\alpha^{-1} ig(	heta_t-\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(	heta_t-\alpha g_t) ig) =\alpha^{-1}(	heta_t-	heta_{t+1}). \] \paragraph{Step 1: a descent inequality in terms of $\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t$.} Let $\Delta_t:=	heta_{t+1}-	heta_t=-\alpha\,\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t$. By $L_F$-smoothness of $F$ on $\Theta$ and convexity of $\Theta$, we have \[ F(	heta_{t+1}) \le F(	heta_t)+\langle 
abla F(	heta_t),\Delta_tangle+ rac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2. \] Since $	heta_{t+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(	heta_t-\alpha g_t)$ and $	heta_t\in\Theta$, the projection optimality condition yields \[ \langle g_t,\Delta_tangle\ \le\ - rac{1}{\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2. \] Using $
abla F(	heta_t)=g_t-e_t$, Cauchy--Schwarz, and the weighted Young inequality \[ uv\le  rac{1}{4\alpha}u^2+\alpha v^2,\qquad u,v\ge0, \] gives  egin{align*} F(	heta_{t+1}) &\le F(	heta_t)+\langle g_t,\Delta_tangle-\langle e_t,\Delta_tangle+ rac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2\ &\le F(	heta_t)- rac{1}{\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\|e_t\|\,\|\Delta_t\|+ rac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2\ &\le F(	heta_t)- rac{1}{\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+ rac{1}{4\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2+ rac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2\ &= F(	heta_t)-\Big( rac{3}{4\alpha}- rac{L_F}{2}\Big)\|\Delta_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2. \end{align*} Using $\alpha\le 1/L_F$ gives $ rac{3}{4\alpha}- rac{L_F}{2}\ge  rac{1}{4\alpha}$, hence \[ F(	heta_{t+1}) \le F(	heta_t)- rac{1}{4\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2 = F(	heta_t)- rac{\alpha}{4}\|\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2. \] Summing over $t=0,\dots,T-1$ and using $F(	heta_T)\ge F_\star$ yields  egin{equation} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\|^2 \le  rac{4\,(F(	heta_0)-F_\star)}{\alpha} +4\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|e_t\|^2. \end{equation} \paragraph{Step 2: relate $\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t$ to the true gradient mapping.} By nonexpansiveness of projection, \[ \|\mathcal G_{\Theta}(	heta_t,
abla F(	heta_t);\alpha)-\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\| =  rac{1}{\alpha} ig\|\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(	heta_t-\alpha g_t)-\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(	heta_t-\alpha
abla F(	heta_t)) ig\| \le \|e_t\|. \] Therefore $\|\mathcal G_{\Theta}(	heta_t,
abla F(	heta_t);\alpha)\|^2\le 2\|\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\|^2+2\|e_t\|^2$, and combining with \eqref{eq:sum-Gtilde} gives \[ \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\mathcal G_{\Theta}(	heta_t,
abla F(	heta_t);\alpha)\|^2 \le  rac{8\,(F(	heta_0)-F_\star)}{\alpha} +10\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|e_t\|^2. \] Dividing by $T$ and taking expectations yields \eqref{eq:outer-inexact}.

nodes.name: Descent inequality
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 1: a descent inequality in terms of $\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t$.} Let $\Delta_t:=\theta_{t+1}-\theta_t=-\alpha\,\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t$. By $L_F$-smoothness of $F$ on $\Theta$ and convexity of $\Theta$, we have \[ F(\theta_{t+1}) \le F(\theta_t)+\langle \nabla F(\theta_t),\Delta_t\rangle+\frac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2. \] Since $\theta_{t+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(\theta_t-\alpha g_t)$ and $\theta_t\in\Theta$, the projection optimality condition yields \[ \langle g_t,\Delta_t\rangle\ \le\ -\frac{1}{\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2. \] Using $\nabla F(\theta_t)=g_t-e_t$, Cauchy--Schwarz, and the weighted Young inequality \[ uv\le \frac{1}{4\alpha}u^2+\alpha v^2,\qquad u,v\ge0, \] gives \begin{align*} F(\theta_{t+1}) &\le F(\theta_t)+\langle g_t,\Delta_t\rangle-\langle e_t,\Delta_t\rangle+\frac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2\\ &\le F(\theta_t)-\frac{1}{\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\|e_t\|\,\|\Delta_t\|+\frac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2\\ &\le F(\theta_t)-\frac{1}{\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\frac{1}{4\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2+\frac{L_F}{2}\|\Delta_t\|^2\\ &= F(\theta_t)-\Big(\frac{3}{4\alpha}-\frac{L_F}{2}\Big)\|\Delta_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2. \end{align*} Using $\alpha\le 1/L_F$ gives $\frac{3}{4\alpha}-\frac{L_F}{2}\ge \frac{1}{4\alpha}$, hence \[ F(\theta_{t+1}) \le F(\theta_t)-\frac{1}{4\alpha}\|\Delta_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2 = F(\theta_t)-\frac{\alpha}{4}\|\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\|^2+\alpha\|e_t\|^2. \] Summing over $t=0,\dots,T-1$ and using $F(\theta_T)\ge F_\star$ yields \begin{equation} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\|^2 \le \frac{4\,(F(\theta_0)-F_\star)}{\alpha} +4\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|e_t\|^2. \end{equation}

abla F(	heta_t);\alpha)-\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\| =  rac{1}{\alpha} ig\|\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(	heta_t-\alpha g_t)-\mathrm{Proj}_{\Theta}(	heta_t-\alpha
abla F(	heta_t)) ig\| \le \|e_t\|. \] Therefore $\|\mathcal G_{\Theta}(	heta_t,
abla F(	heta_t);\alpha)\|^2\le 2\|\widetilde{\mathcal G}_t\|^2+2\|e_t\|^2$, and combining with \eqref{eq:sum-Gtilde} gives \[ \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\mathcal G_{\Theta}(	heta_t,
abla F(	heta_t);\alpha)\|^2 \le  rac{8\,(F(	heta_0)-F_\star)}{\alpha} +10\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|e_t\|^2. \] Dividing by $T$ and taking expectations yields \eqref{eq:outer-inexact}.

nodes.name: Tube radius ensuring ridge invertibility
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:curvature_g} hold. Recall from \Cref{ass:curvature_g} that \(\rho\) is the radius of the tube around \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) on which the third-derivative bound \(L_{g,3}\) holds. Let \(\bar L_{g,3}:=\max\{L_{g,3},1\}\) and define \[ r(\gamma):=\min\left\{\rho,\frac{\gamma}{2\bar L_{g,3}}\right\}. \] Then for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le r(\gamma)$, we have \[ \nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)+\gamma I \ \succeq\ \tfrac{\gamma}{2}\,I, \qquad\text{and hence}\qquad \big\|\big(\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)+\gamma I\big)^{-1}\big\|\ \le\ \tfrac{2}{\gamma}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement:
Let \(y\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) be a nearest projection of \(x\), so \(\|x-y\|=\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\le r(\gamma)\). By \Cref{prop:geometry}, \(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,y)\succeq 0\). Since \(r(\gamma)\leho\), the segment from \(y\) to \(x\) stays inside the \(ho\)-tube around \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\). Assumption~ef{ass:curvature_g} therefore gives \[ \|
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x)-
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,y)\| \le L_{g,3}\|x-y\| \le  ar L_{g,3}r(\gamma) \le \gamma/2. \] Weyl's inequality yields \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x))\ge-\gamma/2\). Thus \(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x)+\gamma I\succeq(\gamma/2)I\), and the inverse-norm bound follows.

nodes.name: General stability bound for the inexact ridge hyper-gradient
nodes.statement:
Let \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:unique_min,assum_sample_comp} hold, and let $x^\star:\Theta	o\mathbb{R}^d$ denote the unique optimistic selection described above. Fix \(\gamma>0\), an iteration $t$, a parameter $	heta_t\in\Theta$, and a candidate point $	ilde x_t\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Let $\mathcal V\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be any compact convex set containing $\{x^\star(	heta):	heta\in\Theta\}\cup\{	ilde x_t\}$. Assume \(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I\) is invertible and satisfies \[  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} ig\|\le \kappa_\gamma . \] Let $	ilde v_t$ satisfy the residual bound \[  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)	ilde v_t-
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t) ig\|\ \le\ \eta_t. \] Define \[ \widehat h_t := 
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)	ilde v_t, \qquad e_t:=\widehat h_t-
abla F(	heta_t). \] Then \[ \|e_t\|\ \le\ C_x\Bigl(1+\kappa_\gamma+ rac{\kappa_\gamma}{c+\gamma}\Bigr)\,\|	ilde x_t-x^\star(	heta_t)\| \ +\ C_{\mathrm{lin}}\cdot\kappa_\gamma\,\eta_t \ +\ C_{\mathrm{reg}}\cdot\gamma, \] where one admissible choice of constants is \[  egin{aligned} C_{\mathrm{lin}} &:=\sup_{(	heta,x)\in\Theta	imes\mathcal V}\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta,x)\|,\[2pt] C_x &:=L_{	heta f,x} + L_{	heta x,x}\,B_{f,x} + B_{	heta x}\,L_{f_x,x} + B_{	heta x}\,L_{g_{xx},x}\,B_{f,x},\ C_{\mathrm{reg}} &:=\sup_{	heta\in\Theta}  rac{\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\|\,\|
abla_x f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\|}{c^2}, \end{aligned} \] where $c>0$ is the normal spectral gap constant from \Cref{prop:geometry}, \[  egin{aligned} B_{	heta x} &:=\sup_{(	heta,x)\in\Theta	imes\mathcal V}\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta,x)\|,\qquad B_{f,x} :=\sup_{(	heta,x)\in\Theta	imes\mathcal V}\|
abla_x f(	heta,x)\|, \end{aligned} \] and $L_{	heta f,x},L_{	heta x,x},L_{f_x,x},L_{g_{xx},x}<\infty$ are uniform Lipschitz constants on $\mathcal V$ (uniform over $	heta\in\Theta$) for $x\mapsto 
abla_	heta f(	heta,x)$, $x\mapsto 
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta,x)$, $x\mapsto 
abla_x f(	heta,x)$, and $x\mapsto 
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x)$, respectively. Such constants exist and are finite because these maps are continuously differentiable and $\Theta	imes\mathcal V$ is compact and convex.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement:
Write $x_t^\star:=x^\star(	heta_t)$. By \Cref{thm_hyp_obj_diff} and \Cref{ass:unique_min}, \[ 
abla F(	heta_t) = 
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) -
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)  ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star). \] Let \[ v_{t,\gamma} :=  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t). \] Add and subtract the ridge-regularized expressions at \(	ilde x_t\) and \(x_t^\star\), and write \[ e_t=(I)+(II)+(III), \] where \[ (I):=
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\,(v_{t,\gamma}-	ilde v_t), \] \[  egin{aligned} (II):={}& 
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t) -
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)v_{t,\gamma} -
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\ &\quad +
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star), \end{aligned} \] and \[ (III):= 
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) \Big(  ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger - ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} \Big) 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star). \] For term (II), the \(
abla_	heta f\) difference is bounded by \[ \|
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\| \le L_{	heta f,x}\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|. \] For the product difference, add and subtract \[ 
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t) \] and \[ 
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star). \] This gives \[  egin{aligned} \MoveEqLeft[2]\Big\| 
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\ &\quad- 
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) \Big\|\ &\le \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|\,  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} ig\|\, \|
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|\ &\quad+ \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|\,  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} ig\|\, \|
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|\ &\quad+ \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|\, \Big\| \Big[  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}\ &\hspace{39mm} - ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} \Big]
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) \Big\|. \end{aligned} \] The first two terms are bounded by \[ L_{	heta x,x}\kappa_\gamma B_{f,x}\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\| \quad	ext{and}\quad B_{	heta x}\kappa_\gamma L_{f_x,x}\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|. \] For the last term, use the resolvent identity to obtain \[  egin{aligned} \MoveEqLeft[2]\Big\| \Big[  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} - ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} \Big]
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) \Big\|\ &\le \kappa_\gamma\, \|
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|\,  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\|. \end{aligned} \] Since $x_t^\star\in\mathcal{S}(	heta_t)$ and \(
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\in\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}\), \Cref{prop:geometry} implies \[  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\| \le  rac{\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|}{c+\gamma} \le  rac{B_{f,x}}{c+\gamma}. \] Moreover, \[ \|
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\| \le L_{g_{xx},x}\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|. \] Therefore, the last product term is bounded by \[ B_{	heta x}\kappa_\gamma L_{g_{xx},x}B_{f,x}\,  rac{\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|}{c+\gamma}. \] Combining these bounds yields \[ \|(II)\| \le C_x\Bigl(1+\kappa_\gamma+ rac{\kappa_\gamma}{c+\gamma}\Bigr)\,\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|. \] For term (I), define the residual \[ r_t:=  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)	ilde v_t-
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t). \] Then \[ 	ilde v_t-v_{t,\gamma} =  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}r_t, \] and hence \[ \|(I)\| = \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)(	ilde v_t-v_{t,\gamma})\| \le \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|\,  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} ig\|\, \|r_t\| \le C_{\mathrm{lin}}\,\kappa_\gamma\,\eta_t. \] For term (III), note that $x_t^\star$ is a minimizer of $f(	heta_t,\cdot)$ over the manifold $\mathcal{S}(	heta_t)$, so the first-order condition implies $
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\in\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$. By \Cref{prop:geometry}, the restriction of $
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)$ to $\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$ has eigenvalues in $[c,\infty)$. Let $\{u_i\}_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}$ be an orthonormal eigenbasis of $\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$ with $
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)u_i=\lambda_i u_i$ and $\lambda_i\ge c$. Since $
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\in\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$, we can write $
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)=\sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}  eta_i u_i$. On $\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$, the pseudoinverse coincides with the inverse, hence \[  ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) = \sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}( eta_i/\lambda_i)u_i, \] while \[  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) = \sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}} ig( eta_i/(\lambda_i+\gamma) ig)u_i. \] Therefore \[  egin{aligned} & ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) - ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\ &\qquad = \sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}  eta_i\Big( rac{1}{\lambda_i+\gamma}- rac{1}{\lambda_i}\Big)u_i . \end{aligned} \] Hence \[  egin{aligned} & ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) - ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\|\ &\qquad\le \max_{i=1,\dots,d-	exttt{k}}\Big| rac{1}{\lambda_i+\gamma}- rac{1}{\lambda_i}\Big|\, \|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|. \end{aligned} \] Using $ ig| rac{1}{\lambda+\gamma}- rac{1}{\lambda} ig|= rac{\gamma}{\lambda(\lambda+\gamma)}$ and $\lambda_i\ge c$ gives  egin{align*} \MoveEqLeft[2] ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) - ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\|\ &\le  rac{\gamma}{c(c+\gamma)}\,\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\| \le  rac{\gamma}{c^2}\,\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|. \end{align*} Multiplying by $\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|$ and taking the supremum over $	heta\in\Theta$ yields $\|(III)\|\le C_{\mathrm{reg}}\gamma$. Combining the three bounds gives the claim.

nodes.name: Resolvent identity
nodes.statement:
For the last term, use the resolvent identity to obtain \[  egin{aligned} \MoveEqLeft[2]\Big\| \Big[  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} - ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} \Big]
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) \Big\|\ &\le \kappa_\gamma\, \|
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|\,  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\|. \end{aligned} \] Since $x_t^\star\in\mathcal{S}(	heta_t)$ and \(
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\in\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}\), \Cref{prop:geometry} implies \[  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\| \le  rac{\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|}{c+\gamma} \le  rac{B_{f,x}}{c+\gamma}. \] Moreover, \[ \|
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)-
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\| \le L_{g_{xx},x}\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|. \] Therefore, the last product term is bounded by \[ B_{	heta x}\kappa_\gamma L_{g_{xx},x}B_{f,x}\,  rac{\|	ilde x_t-x_t^\star\|}{c+\gamma}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Resolvent identity and the normal spectral gap bound the last term.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Bound on (II)
nodes.statement: Combining these bounds yields \[ \|(II)\| \le C_x\Bigl(1+\kappa_\gamma+\frac{\kappa_\gamma}{c+\gamma}\Bigr)\,\|\tilde x_t-x_t^\star\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Collect the bounds on (II).
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Bound term (I)
nodes.statement:
For term (I), define the residual \[ r_t:=  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)	ilde v_t-
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t). \] Then \[ 	ilde v_t-v_{t,\gamma} =  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}r_t, \] and hence \[ \|(I)\| = \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)(	ilde v_t-v_{t,\gamma})\| \le \|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|\,  ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I ig)^{-1} ig\|\, \|r_t\| \le C_{\mathrm{lin}}\,\kappa_\gamma\,\eta_t. \]
nodes.statement_short: The CG residual gives ‖(I)‖ ≤ C_lin κ_γ η_t.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Bound term (III)
nodes.statement:
For term (III), note that $x_t^\star$ is a minimizer of $f(	heta_t,\cdot)$ over the manifold $\mathcal{S}(	heta_t)$, so the first-order condition implies $
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\in\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$. By \Cref{prop:geometry}, the restriction of $
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)$ to $\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$ has eigenvalues in $[c,\infty)$. Let $\{u_i\}_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}$ be an orthonormal eigenbasis of $\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$ with $
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)u_i=\lambda_i u_i$ and $\lambda_i\ge c$. Since $
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\in\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$, we can write $
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)=\sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}  eta_i u_i$. On $\mathcal{N}_{x_t^\star}^{	heta_t}$, the pseudoinverse coincides with the inverse, hence \[  ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger 
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) = \sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}( eta_i/\lambda_i)u_i, \] while \[  ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) = \sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}} ig( eta_i/(\lambda_i+\gamma) ig)u_i. \] Therefore \[  egin{aligned} & ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) - ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\ &\qquad = \sum_{i=1}^{d-	exttt{k}}  eta_i\Big( rac{1}{\lambda_i+\gamma}- rac{1}{\lambda_i}\Big)u_i . \end{aligned} \] Hence \[  egin{aligned} & ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) - ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\|\ &\qquad\le \max_{i=1,\dots,d-	exttt{k}}\Big| rac{1}{\lambda_i+\gamma}- rac{1}{\lambda_i}\Big|\, \|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|. \end{aligned} \] Using $ ig| rac{1}{\lambda+\gamma}- rac{1}{\lambda} ig|= rac{\gamma}{\lambda(\lambda+\gamma)}$ and $\lambda_i\ge c$ gives  egin{align*} \MoveEqLeft[2] ig\| ig(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)+\gamma I ig)^{-1}
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) - ig[
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig]^\dagger
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star) ig\|\ &\le  rac{\gamma}{c(c+\gamma)}\,\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\| \le  rac{\gamma}{c^2}\,\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|. \end{align*} Multiplying by $\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,x_t^\star)\|$ and taking the supremum over $	heta\in\Theta$ yields $\|(III)\|\le C_{\mathrm{reg}}\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Eigen-expansion on the normal space bounds the ridge bias by C_reg γ.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining the three bounds gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Add the three bounds.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Derivation of Lemma 8 from Lemmas 6 and 7
nodes.statement: \Cref{lem:hg-stability} follows by taking a fixed compact set containing the \(\rho\)-tube around all \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), restricting to $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\le r(\gamma)$, and applying \Cref{lem:tube-invertibility} to bound $\kappa_\gamma\le 2/\gamma$.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the tube and plug κ_γ ≤ 2/γ from Lemma 6 into Lemma 7.

nodes.name: Stability of the inexact implicit term on the tube
nodes.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed} hold for the same \(\theta_t,\tilde x_t,\tilde v_t\), and fix $\gamma>0$ with tube radius $r(\gamma)$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-invertibility}. Let $\mathcal V=\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D+\rho)$. Fix an iteration $t$ with $\theta_t\in\Theta$ and $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\le r(\gamma)$, so that $\tilde x_t\in\mathcal V$. Assume clipping is inactive, i.e., the clipped vector used by the algorithm satisfies $v_t=\tilde v_t$. Then the algorithmic hyper-gradient error $e_t=\widehat h_t-\nabla F(\theta_t)$ obeys \[ \|e_t\| \ \le\ A_\gamma\,\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\| \ +\ \tfrac{2C_{\mathrm{lin}}}{\gamma}\,\eta_t \ +\ C_{\mathrm{reg}}\,\gamma, \] where $C_{\mathrm{lin}},C_{\mathrm{reg}}$ are as in Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed} and \[ A_\gamma := C_x\Bigl(1+\tfrac{2}{\gamma}+\tfrac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)}\Bigr), \] with $c>0$ the normal spectral gap constant from \Cref{prop:geometry} and $C_x$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed}.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1
nodes.statement_short: On the tube event with inactive clipping, ‖e_t‖ ≤ A_γ‖x̃_t−x*‖ + (2C_lin/γ)η_t + C_reg γ.
nodes.label: lem:hg-stability

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Because \(r(\gamma)\le\rho\) and \(\mathcal{S}(\theta_t)\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), the tube condition implies \(\tilde x_t\in\mathcal V\). Under this same condition, Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-invertibility} gives $\kappa_\gamma\le 2/\gamma$. Since clipping is inactive, the algorithmic \(\widehat h_t\), which is formed with \(v_t\), coincides with the quantity in Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed}, which is formed with \(\tilde v_t\). Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed} with $\mathcal V=\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D+\rho)$ and substituting this inverse-norm bound gives the claim.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 7 with the inverse-norm bound from Lemma 6 on the tube.

nodes.name: Tube gives κ_γ ≤ 2/γ
nodes.statement: Because \(r(\gamma)\le\rho\) and \(\mathcal{S}(\theta_t)\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), the tube condition implies \(\tilde x_t\in\mathcal V\). Under this same condition, Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-invertibility} gives $\kappa_\gamma\le 2/\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: On the tube x̃_t∈V and Lemma 6 gives κ_γ≤2/γ.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Since clipping is inactive, the algorithmic \(\widehat h_t\), which is formed with \(v_t\), coincides with the quantity in Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed}, which is formed with \(\tilde v_t\). Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability-detailed} with $\mathcal V=\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D+\rho)$ and substituting this inverse-norm bound gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: With clipping inactive, Lemma 7 applies and gives the claim.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Bounding the off-tube term under clipping
nodes.statement: Fix $\gamma>0$ and let \(r(\gamma)\) be the tube radius from Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-invertibility}. Assume Algorithm~\ref{alg:hg-minsel-lmc} uses the safeguard $v_t=\mathrm{Proj}_{\mathbb B_d(0;R_v)}(\tilde v_t)$, and assume the CG output $\tilde v_t$ satisfies $\|b_t-(H_t+\gamma I)\tilde v_t\|\le \eta_t$. Let \(\mathsf{D}_{t}:=\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\). Define the tube event \(\mathcal E_t:=\{\mathsf{D}_{t}\le r(\gamma)\}\). Under \Cref{assum_sample_comp} and the smoothness of \(F\) on compact \(\Theta\), there exists a constant \(C_{\mathrm{off}}<\infty\), independent of \(t,\gamma,\eta_t,R_v\), such that \[ \|e_t\|^2 \ \le\ C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}). \] Consequently, \[ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big] \ \le\ C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\, \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big]. \] Moreover, on $\mathcal E_t$ Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-invertibility} implies $\|\tilde v_t\|\le (2/\gamma)(L_{f,1}+\eta_t)$, so choosing $R_v\ge (2/\gamma)(L_{f,1}+\eta_t)$ ensures the safeguard is inactive on $\mathcal E_t$ (i.e., $v_t=\tilde v_t$).
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1
nodes.statement_short: With clipping, ‖e_t‖² ≤ C_off(1+R_v²)(1+D_t^{2n}); on the tube a large enough R_v leaves clipping inactive.
nodes.label: lem:off-tube-et

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
Since $\|v_t\|\le R_v$ by construction, \Cref{assum_sample_comp} gives \[ \|\widehat h_t\| \le \|
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|+\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|\,\|v_t\| \le L_{f,1}+ ig(C_{	heta x}\|	ilde x_t\|^{\mathsf n_{	heta x}}+D_{	heta x} ig)R_v. \] Since $F$ is smooth on compact \(\Theta\), \(B_F:=\sup_{	heta\in\Theta}\|
abla F(	heta)\|<\infty\). Using \((a+b+c)^2\le 3(a^2+b^2+c^2)\), we obtain \[ \|e_t\|^2\le C(1+R_v^2)(1+\|	ilde x_t\|^{2\mathsf n_{	heta x}}) \] for a finite constant \(C\). Because \(\mathcal{S}(	heta_t)\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), we have \(\|	ilde x_t\|\le \mathsf D+\mathsf{D}_{t}\), and hence \((1+\|	ilde x_t\|^{2\mathsf n_{	heta x}})\le C'(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{	heta x}})\). This proves the off-tube moment bound. For the final claim, on \(\mathcal E_t\), Lemma~ef{lem:tube-invertibility} and the residual relation $(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I)	ilde v_t=
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+r_t$ with $\|r_t\|\le\eta_t$ give \[ \|	ilde v_t\| \le  rac{2}{\gamma} ig(\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|+\eta_t ig) \le  rac{2}{\gamma}(L_{f,1}+\eta_t), \] where the last inequality uses the global Lipschitzness of \(f\). Under the stated choice of \(R_v\), this gives \(\|	ilde v_t\|\le R_v\), so the Euclidean projection onto \(\mathbb B_d(0;R_v)\) leaves \(	ilde v_t\) unchanged.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1
nodes.statement_short: Bound ĥ_t by clipping and polynomial growth, then bound ṽ_t on the tube by Lemma 6.

nodes.name: Bound ĥ_t
nodes.statement:
Since $\|v_t\|\le R_v$ by construction, \Cref{assum_sample_comp} gives \[ \|\widehat h_t\| \le \|
abla_	heta f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|+\|
abla^2_{	heta x}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|\,\|v_t\| \le L_{f,1}+ ig(C_{	heta x}\|	ilde x_t\|^{\mathsf n_{	heta x}}+D_{	heta x} ig)R_v. \] Since $F$ is smooth on compact \(\Theta\), \(B_F:=\sup_{	heta\in\Theta}\|
abla F(	heta)\|<\infty\).
nodes.statement_short: Clipping and polynomial growth bound ĥ_t; ∇F is bounded on compact Θ.

nodes.name: Off-tube moment bound
nodes.statement: Using \((a+b+c)^2\le 3(a^2+b^2+c^2)\), we obtain \[ \|e_t\|^2\le C(1+R_v^2)(1+\|\tilde x_t\|^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}) \] for a finite constant \(C\). Because \(\mathcal{S}(\theta_t)\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), we have \(\|\tilde x_t\|\le \mathsf D+\mathsf{D}_{t}\), and hence \((1+\|\tilde x_t\|^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\le C'(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\). This proves the off-tube moment bound.
nodes.statement_short: Square and use ‖x̃_t‖ ≤ D + D_t.
nodes.section: E.2 Hyper-gradient stability and proof of 1

nodes.name: Clipping inactive on the tube
nodes.statement:
For the final claim, on \(\mathcal E_t\), Lemma~ef{lem:tube-invertibility} and the residual relation $(
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+\gamma I)	ilde v_t=
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)+r_t$ with $\|r_t\|\le\eta_t$ give \[ \|	ilde v_t\| \le  rac{2}{\gamma} ig(\|
abla_x f(	heta_t,	ilde x_t)\|+\eta_t ig) \le  rac{2}{\gamma}(L_{f,1}+\eta_t), \] where the last inequality uses the global Lipschitzness of \(f\). Under the stated choice of \(R_v\), this gives \(\|	ilde v_t\|\le R_v\), so the Euclidean projection onto \(\mathbb B_d(0;R_v)\) leaves \(	ilde v_t\) unchanged.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6 bounds ṽ_t by (2/γ)(L_{f,1}+η_t) ≤ R_v.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Fix an iteration $t$. Split \[ \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 = \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big] \ +\ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big]. \] \paragraph{On the tube.} On $\mathcal E_t$, our choice of clipping radius ensures $v_t=\tilde v_t$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:off-tube-et}). Therefore Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability} gives \[ \|e_t\| \ \le\ A_\gamma\,\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\| \ +\ \tfrac{2C_{\mathrm{lin}}}{\gamma}\,\eta_t \ +\ C_{\mathrm{reg}}\,\gamma. \] Using $(a+b+c)^2\le 3(a^2+b^2+c^2)$ and that $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\le 1$ yields \[ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big] \ \le\ 3A_\gamma^2\,\mathbb E\big[\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big] \ +\ \tfrac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\,\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\,\gamma^2. \] Recalling $A_\gamma=C_x(1+\tfrac{2}{\gamma}+\tfrac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)})$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability} gives the first three terms in \eqref{eq:et2-explicit}. \paragraph{Off the tube.} Lemma~\ref{lem:off-tube-et} yields \[ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big] \le C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\, \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big]. \] Combining the two bounds gives \eqref{eq:et2-explicit}.
nodes.section: E.2.1 Proof of 1
nodes.statement_short: Split the second moment over the tube event (Lemma 8) and its complement (Lemma 9).

nodes.name: Split over the tube event
nodes.statement: Fix an iteration $t$. Split \[ \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 = \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big] \ +\ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big]. \]

nodes.name: On the tube
nodes.statement: \paragraph{On the tube.} On $\mathcal E_t$, our choice of clipping radius ensures $v_t=\tilde v_t$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:off-tube-et}). Therefore Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability} gives \[ \|e_t\| \ \le\ A_\gamma\,\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\| \ +\ \tfrac{2C_{\mathrm{lin}}}{\gamma}\,\eta_t \ +\ C_{\mathrm{reg}}\,\gamma. \] Using $(a+b+c)^2\le 3(a^2+b^2+c^2)$ and that $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\le 1$ yields \[ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big] \ \le\ 3A_\gamma^2\,\mathbb E\big[\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big] \ +\ \tfrac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\,\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\,\gamma^2. \] Recalling $A_\gamma=C_x(1+\tfrac{2}{\gamma}+\tfrac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)})$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:hg-stability} gives the first three terms in \eqref{eq:et2-explicit}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 8 and (a+b+c)²≤3(a²+b²+c²) give the first three terms.
nodes.section: E.2.1 Proof of 1

nodes.name: Off the tube
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Off the tube.} Lemma~\ref{lem:off-tube-et} yields \[ \mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big] \le C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\, \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9 bounds the off-tube term.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining the two bounds gives \eqref{eq:et2-explicit}.
nodes.statement_short: Add the two parts.

nodes.name: Hard selection rule and lower-tail level δ
nodes.statement: Given candidates $X_1,\dots,X_M\in\mathbb{R}^d$, our hard selection rule is \[ \tilde x \in \arg\min_{i\in[1:M]} f(\theta,X_i), \qquad \delta:=\frac1M. \]
nodes.section: E.3 Selection Error and Proof of 2

nodes.name: Lower δ-superquantile
nodes.statement: Let $Z$ be a real-valued random variable with (lower) quantile function $q_u(Z):=\inf\{t\in\mathbb{R}:\ \mathbb{P}(Z\le t)\ge u\}$ for $u\in(0,1)$. Define \[ \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta(Z):=\frac1\delta\int_0^\delta q_u(Z)\,\delta u, \qquad \delta\in(0,1). \] If $X\sim \nu$ and $Z=f(\theta,X)$, we also write $\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\nu)$.
nodes.section: E.3 Selection Error and Proof of 2
nodes.statement_short: Average of the lower u-quantiles over u∈(0,δ) (best-δ CVaR).
nodes.label: def:lower-sq

nodes.name: Bounded second fundamental form from analytic regularity
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{ass:plcirc,ass:curvature_g} hold, and let \(c>0\) be the uniform normal spectral gap from \Cref{prop:geometry}. Fix any $\theta\in\Theta$. Then the second fundamental form $\mathrm{II}$ of $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ satisfies \[ \sup_{x\in \mathcal{S}(\theta)}\ \|\mathrm{II}_x\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ \le\ \frac{L_{g,3}}{c}. \] In particular, since \(L_{g,3}\) and \(c\) are uniform over \(\theta\in\Theta\), we obtain a uniform curvature bound over the family \(\{\mathcal{S}(\theta)\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\).
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$
nodes.statement_short: The second fundamental form of S(θ) is bounded by L_{g,3}/c uniformly in θ.
conclusions: the second fundamental form $\mathrm{II}$ of $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ satisfies
nodes.label: prop:second-fund-from-g

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$ and abbreviate \(\mathcal{S}:=\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Let $H(x):=\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)$. Fix $x\in \mathcal{S}$ and unit tangent vectors $u,v\in\mathcal{T}_x^\theta$. Choose a $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ curve $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to \mathcal{S}$ with $\gamma(0)=x$ and $\dot\gamma(0)=v$, and choose a $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ tangent vector field $U(\cdot)$ along $\gamma$ with $U(0)=u$ and $U(t)\in\mathcal{T}_{\gamma(t)}^\theta$. By \Cref{prop:geometry}, \(\ker H(\gamma(t))=\mathcal{T}_{\gamma(t)}^\theta\) for all \(t\). Since \(U(t)\) is tangent along \(\gamma\), we have \(H(\gamma(t))\,U(t)=0\). Differentiating at $t=0$ gives \[ 0 =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t}\Big(H(\gamma(t))\,U(t)\Big)\Big|_{t=0} =\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u+H(x)\,\dot U(0), \] where $D_v H(x)$ denotes the directional derivative of the Hessian in direction $v$. Let $P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}$ denote the orthogonal projection onto the normal space $\mathcal{N}_x^\theta$. Since $H(x)$ is symmetric and $\ker H(x)=\mathcal{T}_x^\theta$, we have $\mathrm{range}(H(x))=(\mathcal{T}_x^\theta)^\perp=\mathcal{N}_x^\theta$ and hence $P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}H(x)=H(x)P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}$. Applying $P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}$ to the display above yields \[ H(x)\,P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\dot U(0) \;=\; -\,P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u. \] By the definition of the second fundamental form of an embedded submanifold in Euclidean space, $\mathrm{II}_x(v,u)=P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\dot U(0)$. Restricting $H(x)$ to $\mathcal{N}_x^\theta$ and using the uniform normal spectral gap gives \[ \|\mathrm{II}_x(v,u)\| \le \big\|\big(H(x)|_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\big)^{-1}\big\|\;\big\|\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u\big\| \le \frac{1}{c}\,\big\|\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u\big\|. \] Finally, by the bounded third derivative assumption, \( \|(D_v H(x))\,u\|\le \|\nabla^3_{xxx}g(\theta,x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|\,\|u\|\le L_{g,3}. \) Therefore $\|\mathrm{II}_x(v,u)\|\le L_{g,3}/c$ for all unit $u,v\in\mathcal{T}_x^\theta$, and taking the supremum over $x\in \mathcal{S}$ yields the claim.
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate H(γ(t))U(t)=0 along a curve, project onto the normal space and invert H there using the spectral gap.

nodes.name: Curve and tangent field
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$ and abbreviate \(\mathcal{S}:=\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Let $H(x):=\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)$. Fix $x\in \mathcal{S}$ and unit tangent vectors $u,v\in\mathcal{T}_x^\theta$. Choose a $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ curve $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to \mathcal{S}$ with $\gamma(0)=x$ and $\dot\gamma(0)=v$, and choose a $\mathcal{C}^{1}$ tangent vector field $U(\cdot)$ along $\gamma$ with $U(0)=u$ and $U(t)\in\mathcal{T}_{\gamma(t)}^\theta$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix x, unit tangents u,v, a curve γ and a tangent field U.
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$

nodes.name: Differentiate H U = 0
nodes.statement: By \Cref{prop:geometry}, \(\ker H(\gamma(t))=\mathcal{T}_{\gamma(t)}^\theta\) for all \(t\). Since \(U(t)\) is tangent along \(\gamma\), we have \(H(\gamma(t))\,U(t)=0\). Differentiating at $t=0$ gives \[ 0 =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t}\Big(H(\gamma(t))\,U(t)\Big)\Big|_{t=0} =\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u+H(x)\,\dot U(0), \] where $D_v H(x)$ denotes the directional derivative of the Hessian in direction $v$.
nodes.statement_short: Tangent fields lie in ker H; differentiate H(γ(t))U(t)=0.
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$

nodes.name: Project onto the normal space
nodes.statement: Let $P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}$ denote the orthogonal projection onto the normal space $\mathcal{N}_x^\theta$. Since $H(x)$ is symmetric and $\ker H(x)=\mathcal{T}_x^\theta$, we have $\mathrm{range}(H(x))=(\mathcal{T}_x^\theta)^\perp=\mathcal{N}_x^\theta$ and hence $P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}H(x)=H(x)P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}$. Applying $P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}$ to the display above yields \[ H(x)\,P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\dot U(0) \;=\; -\,P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u. \]
nodes.statement_short: H commutes with the normal projector; project the identity.
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$

nodes.name: Spectral gap bound
nodes.statement: By the definition of the second fundamental form of an embedded submanifold in Euclidean space, $\mathrm{II}_x(v,u)=P_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\dot U(0)$. Restricting $H(x)$ to $\mathcal{N}_x^\theta$ and using the uniform normal spectral gap gives \[ \|\mathrm{II}_x(v,u)\| \le \big\|\big(H(x)|_{\mathcal{N}_x^\theta}\big)^{-1}\big\|\;\big\|\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u\big\| \le \frac{1}{c}\,\big\|\big(D_v H(x)\big)\,u\big\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: II(v,u)=P_N U̇(0); invert H on the normal space with gap c.
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$

nodes.name: Third-derivative bound
nodes.statement: Finally, by the bounded third derivative assumption, \( \|(D_v H(x))\,u\|\le \|\nabla^3_{xxx}g(\theta,x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|\,\|u\|\le L_{g,3}. \) Therefore $\|\mathrm{II}_x(v,u)\|\le L_{g,3}/c$ for all unit $u,v\in\mathcal{T}_x^\theta$, and taking the supremum over $x\in \mathcal{S}$ yields the claim.
nodes.statement_short: ‖D_vH u‖ ≤ L_{g,3} gives ‖II‖ ≤ L_{g,3}/c.
nodes.section: E.3.1 Bounded curvature from analytic regularity of $g$

nodes.name: Max-distance reduction
nodes.statement: \mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)) \ \le\ \max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta)).
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$
nodes.label: eq:dist-max-bound

nodes.name: Uniform quadratic growth of g(θ,·) over Θ
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{ass:plcirc,assum_sample_comp} hold. Then there exists a constant $\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}>0$ such that for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{equation} g(\theta,x)-\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}g(\theta,z) \ \ge\ \frac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2}\,\mathrm{dist}^2\!\bigl(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)\bigr). \end{equation}
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$
nodes.statement_short: g(θ,x) − min g ≥ (μ_QG/2) dist²(x,S(θ)) for all x and θ.
conclusions: there exists a constant $\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}>0$ such that for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
nodes.label: lem:uniform-qg-g

nodes.name: Global quadratic growth of g
nodes.statement: g(\theta,x)-\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}g(\theta,z) \ \ge\ \frac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2}\,\mathrm{dist}^2\!\bigl(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)\bigr).
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

Therefore,  egin{equation} g(	heta,x)-g_\star(	heta) \ge g(	heta,x)-g(	heta,y) \ge 	frac{c}{4}\,\|u\|^2 =	frac{c}{4}\,R^2. \end{equation} \emph{Step 2: quadratic growth outside the compact ball.} By \Cref{assum_sample_comp}, there exist constants $\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}>0$ and $\mathsf D>0$ such that for all $\|x\|\ge \mathsf D$,  egin{equation} g(	heta,x)-g_\star(	heta)\ \ge\ 	frac{\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}}{2}\, \mathrm{dist}^2\! igl(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta) igr), \qquad  orall 	heta\in\Theta. \end{equation} \emph{Step 3: the middle region by compactness.} Consider the set \[ \mathcal A :=\Big\{(	heta,x):	heta\in\Theta,\ \|x\|\le \mathsf D,\ \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\ge r_{\mathrm{loc}}\Big\}. \] By the continuity of the distance map just noted, \(\mathcal A\) is closed in \(\Theta	imes \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), hence compact. If \(\mathcal A=\emptyset\), the middle region is vacuous; in this case set \(\mu_{\mathrm{mid}}:=+\infty\). Otherwise, the map $(	heta,x)\mapsto g(	heta,x)-g_\star(	heta)$ is continuous on $\Theta	imes \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)$ and is strictly positive on $\mathcal A$ (since $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta))>0$ implies $x

In the nonempty case, therefore, \[ m_{\min}:=\min_{(	heta,x)\in\mathcal A} ig(g(	heta,x)-g_\star(	heta) ig)>0. \] Moreover, if $\|x\|\le \mathsf D$ then $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\le 2\mathsf D$, so on the nonempty set \(\mathcal A\) we have \[ g(	heta,x)-g_\star(	heta)\ \ge\ m_{\min} \ \ge\  rac{m_{\min}}{(2\mathsf D)^2}\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta)). \] For this nonempty case, set \(\mu_{\mathrm{mid}}:=2m_{\min}/(2\mathsf D)^2\). \emph{Step 4: combine the three regions.} Let \[ \mu_{\mathrm{QG}} :=\min\Big\{	frac{c}{2},\ \mu_{\mathsf{qg}},\ \mu_{\mathrm{mid}}\Big\}. \] Then \eqref{eq:qg-local}, \eqref{eq:qg-outside}, and the middle-region bound above imply \eqref{eq:global-qg-g} for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and all $	heta\in\Theta$.

nodes.name: Notation
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf D$ be the compactness radius from \Cref{assum_sample_comp}, so that $\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)$ for all $\theta\in\Theta$. Write $g_\star(\theta):=\min_{z}g(\theta,z)$.

nodes.name: Compact solution graph
nodes.statement: \emph{Preliminaries on the minimizer family.} Since each minimizer set is contained in \(\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), \[ g_\star(\theta)=\min_{\|z\|\le \mathsf D} g(\theta,z). \] Thus \(g_\star\) is continuous on the compact set \(\Theta\) by Berge's maximum theorem. Consequently, the solution graph \[ \mathcal K:=\{(\theta,y):\theta\in\Theta,\ y\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\} =\{(\theta,y)\in\Theta\times \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D): g(\theta,y)=g_\star(\theta)\} \] is compact. The standard local normal-chart argument for the zero set \(\{\nabla_x g(\theta,x)=0\}\), using the normal spectral gap in \Cref{prop:geometry} around each \((\theta,y)\in\mathcal K\) and then patched by compactness, gives local Hausdorff continuity of \(\theta\mapsto\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) on \(\Theta\). In particular, the map \((\theta,x)\mapsto \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\) is continuous on \(\Theta\times \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), and the normal spaces \(\mathcal{N}_y^\theta\) vary continuously over \(\mathcal K\).
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of g_⋆ and compactness of the solution graph give continuity of the distance map.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Local growth in a uniform tube
nodes.statement:
\emph{Step 1: local quadratic growth in a uniform tube.} Let $c>0$ be the normal spectral gap from \Cref{prop:geometry}, i.e., $\langle v,
abla_{xx}^2 g(	heta,y)vangle\ge c\|v\|^2$ for all $	heta\in\Theta$, $y\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)$, and $v\in\mathcal{N}_y^	heta$. Since $(	heta,x)\mapsto 
abla^2_{xx}g(	heta,x)$ is continuous (\Cref{assum_sample_comp}) and the normal bundle over \(\mathcal K\) is compact, there exists $r_{\mathrm{loc}}>0$ such that for all $	heta\in\Theta$, all $y\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)$, and all $x$ with $\|x-y\|\le r_{\mathrm{loc}}$,  egin{equation} \langle v,
abla_{xx}^2 g(	heta,x)vangle\ \ge\ 	frac{c}{2}\,\|v\|^2 \qquad  orall v\in\mathcal{N}_y^	heta. \end{equation} Now fix any $	heta\in\Theta$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ with $R:=\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\le r_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Let $y\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)$ be a Euclidean projection of $x$ onto $\mathcal{S}(	heta)$, so that $\|x-y\|=R$. By first-order optimality of the projection problem on the manifold, $u:=x-y$ lies in the normal space $\mathcal{N}_y^	heta$. Using $
abla_x g(	heta,y)=0$ (since $y\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)$) and the integral form of Taylor's theorem, \[ g(	heta,x)-g(	heta,y) =\int_0^1 (1-t)\,u^	op 
abla_{xx}^2 g(	heta,y+t u)\,u\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Because $\|t u\|\le R\le r_{\mathrm{loc}}$, \eqref{eq:local-normal-gap} applies along the segment $y+t u$, giving $u^	op 
abla^2_{xx} g(	heta,y+t u)u\ge (c/2)\|u\|^2$ for all $t\in[0,1]$. Therefore,  egin{equation} g(	heta,x)-g_\star(	heta) \ge g(	heta,x)-g(	heta,y) \ge 	frac{c}{4}\,\|u\|^2 =	frac{c}{4}\,R^2. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Normal spectral gap persists in a uniform tube; Taylor gives growth (c/4)R².
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Growth outside the ball
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 2: quadratic growth outside the compact ball.} By \Cref{assum_sample_comp}, there exist constants $\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}>0$ and $\mathsf D>0$ such that for all $\|x\|\ge \mathsf D$, \begin{equation} g(\theta,x)-g_\star(\theta)\ \ge\ \tfrac{\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}}{2}\, \mathrm{dist}^2\!\bigl(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)\bigr), \qquad \forall \theta\in\Theta. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Assumption 4 gives growth for ‖x‖≥D.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Middle region by compactness
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 3: the middle region by compactness.} Consider the set \[ \mathcal A :=\Big\{(\theta,x):\theta\in\Theta,\ \|x\|\le \mathsf D,\ \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\ge r_{\mathrm{loc}}\Big\}. \] By the continuity of the distance map just noted, \(\mathcal A\) is closed in \(\Theta\times \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), hence compact. If \(\mathcal A=\emptyset\), the middle region is vacuous; in this case set \(\mu_{\mathrm{mid}}:=+\infty\). Otherwise, the map $(\theta,x)\mapsto g(\theta,x)-g_\star(\theta)$ is continuous on $\Theta\times \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)$ and is strictly positive on $\mathcal A$ (since $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))>0$ implies $x\notin\mathcal{S}(\theta)$). In the nonempty case, therefore, \[ m_{\min}:=\min_{(\theta,x)\in\mathcal A}\big(g(\theta,x)-g_\star(\theta)\big)>0. \] Moreover, if $\|x\|\le \mathsf D$ then $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le 2\mathsf D$, so on the nonempty set \(\mathcal A\) we have \[ g(\theta,x)-g_\star(\theta)\ \ge\ m_{\min} \ \ge\ \frac{m_{\min}}{(2\mathsf D)^2}\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)). \] For this nonempty case, set \(\mu_{\mathrm{mid}}:=2m_{\min}/(2\mathsf D)^2\).
nodes.statement_short: A positive minimum gap on the compact middle region gives μ_mid.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: \emph{Step 4: combine the three regions.} Let \[ \mu_{\mathrm{QG}} :=\min\Big\{\tfrac{c}{2},\ \mu_{\mathsf{qg}},\ \mu_{\mathrm{mid}}\Big\}. \] Then \eqref{eq:qg-local}, \eqref{eq:qg-outside}, and the middle-region bound above imply \eqref{eq:global-qg-g} for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and all $\theta\in\Theta$.
nodes.statement_short: Take μ_QG as the minimum of the three constants.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.statement: \langle v,\nabla_{xx}^2 g(\theta,x)v\rangle\ \ge\ \tfrac{c}{2}\,\|v\|^2 \qquad \forall v\in\mathcal{N}_y^\theta.

nodes.name: Tube concentration for Gibbs samples
nodes.statement: Assume the setting of \Cref{lem:uniform-qg-g} and fix any $\theta\in\Theta$. Let $X\sim \mu_\theta^\lambda$ and define $R:=\mathrm{dist}(X,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$. Then there exist constants $\lambda_0,c_{\mathrm{tube}},C_{\mathrm{tube}},C_{\mathrm{tube},2}>0$ (independent of $\theta$ and $\lambda$) such that, for every \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \begin{equation} \mathbb P(R\ge t)\ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big), \qquad \forall t\ge 0. \end{equation} Consequently, \[ \mathbb E[R]\le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda}, \qquad \mathbb E[R^2]\le C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\lambda. \] Moreover, if $X_1,\dots,X_M\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mu_\theta^\lambda$ and $\tilde x$ is any measurable selection of one of the candidates, then \begin{equation} \mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\big] \ \le\ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big] \ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\,\log(1+M)}. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\big] \ \le\ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\Big] \ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\,\log(1+M). \end{equation}
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$
nodes.statement_short: Distance of a Gibbs sample to S(θ) has a subgaussian tail at scale √λ; the max over M samples is O(√(λ log M)).
nodes.label: lem:gibbs-tube-width

nodes.name: Gibbs tube tail
nodes.statement: \mathbb P(R\ge t)\ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big), \qquad \forall t\ge 0.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$
nodes.label: eq:gibbs-tail

nodes.statement: \mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\big] \ \le\ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big] \ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\,\log(1+M)}.

nodes.statement: \mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\big] \ \le\ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\Big] \ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\,\log(1+M).
