nodes.label: eq:dist-tilde-max2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 11
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$ and abbreviate \(\mathcal{S}:=\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) and $g_\star:=\min_z g(\theta,z)$. By \Cref{lem:uniform-qg-g}, $g(\theta,x)\ge g_\star+\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2}\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S})$. Therefore, for any $t\ge 0$, \[ \mathbb P(R\ge t) =\frac{\int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t} e^{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x} \le \frac{\int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t} \exp\!\big(-\tfrac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2\lambda}\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S})\big)\,\mathrm{d} x}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-(g(\theta,x)-g_\star)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x}. \] Let \(q:=d-\texttt{k}\) be the normal dimension of \(\mathcal S\). Since \(\mathcal S\) is compact and embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), we have \(q\ge 1\). We next use a uniform tubular-coordinate estimate around the family \(\{\mathcal{S}(\theta)\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\). By compactness of the solution graph, the uniform normal spectral gap in \Cref{prop:geometry}, and the uniform curvature control in \Cref{prop:second-fund-from-g}, there are constants \(r_{\mathrm{tube}}>0\), \(0<J_{\min}\le J_{\max}<\infty\), and \(0<V_{\min}\le V_{\max}<\infty\), independent of \(\theta\), such that the normal map \[ \Phi_\theta(y,z)=y+z,\qquad y\in\mathcal S,\quad z\in\mathcal{N}_y^\theta,\quad \|z\|<r_{\mathrm{tube}}, \] is a diffeomorphism onto the \(r_{\mathrm{tube}}\)-tube around \(\mathcal S\), its Jacobian lies in \([J_{\min},J_{\max}]\), and the Riemannian volume of \(\mathcal S\) lies in \([V_{\min},V_{\max}]\). We first lower bound the denominator. Let \[ Z_\lambda(\theta):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-(g(\theta,x)-g_\star)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x . \] The small-temperature normalizing-constant lower bound used in \citet[Lem.~D.1]{masiha2025superquantile}, applied here in the normal coordinates above, gives the manifold-version scaling \begin{equation} Z_\lambda(\theta)\ge c_{\mathrm{den}}\,\lambda^{q/2} \end{equation} for all sufficiently small \(\lambda\), with \(c_{\mathrm{den}}>0\) uniform in \(\theta\). The exponent is \(q/2\), rather than \(d/2\), because the Gibbs mass only concentrates in the \(q=d-\texttt{k}\) normal directions; integration along \(\mathcal S\) contributes a bounded positive manifold-volume factor. We now upper bound the numerator. Write \(a:=\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}/(2\lambda)\) and split the domain into the part inside the uniform tube and the part outside it. \emph{Inside the tube.} Every point in the tube has a unique representation \(x=y+z\), where \(y\in\mathcal S\) and \(z\in\mathcal{N}_y^\theta\). Here \(\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathcal S}(y)\) denotes the intrinsic \(\texttt{k}\)-dimensional volume measure on \(\mathcal S\) induced by the ambient Euclidean metric; for example, it is arclength when \(\texttt{k}=1\) and surface area when \(\texttt{k}=2\). Thus \[ \int_{\mathcal S}\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathcal S}(y)=\mathrm{Vol}_{\texttt{k}}(\mathcal S). \] In these coordinates, \(\mathrm{dist}(y+z,\mathcal S)=\|z\|\) and the Euclidean volume element decomposes as \[ \mathrm{d} x=J_\theta(y,z)\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathcal S}(y), \] where \(J_\theta(y,z)\le J_{\max}\). Therefore, after integrating out the \(y\)-variable using \(\mathrm{Vol}_{\texttt{k}}(\mathcal S)\le V_{\max}\), and identifying each normal fiber \(\mathcal{N}_y^\theta\) with \(\mathbb{R}^q\) through an arbitrary orthonormal basis, the tube contribution is bounded by a \(q\)-dimensional Gaussian tail: \begin{align} \int_{\substack{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge t\\ \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)<r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal S)}\,\mathrm{d} x &\le J_{\max}V_{\max} \int_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{R}^q:\ \|z\|\ge t\\ \|z\|<r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} e^{-a\|z\|^2}\,\mathrm{d} z \nonumber\\ &\le J_{\max}V_{\max}\,|\mathbb S^{q-1}| \int_t^\infty e^{-a r^2}r^{q-1}\,\mathrm{d} r \nonumber\\ &\le C_1\,a^{-q/2}\exp\!\big(-a t^2/2\big). \end{align} The second inequality is just polar coordinates in the \(q\)-dimensional normal variable \(z\): writing \(z=r\omega\), with \(\omega\in\mathbb S^{q-1}\), gives \(\mathrm{d} z=r^{q-1}\mathrm{d} r\,\mathrm{d}\sigma(\omega)\), and integrating over \(\omega\) gives the factor \(|\mathbb S^{q-1}|\). We then upper bound the radial integral by replacing the upper limit \(r_{\mathrm{tube}}\) with \(\infty\). For the last inequality, substitute \(u=\sqrt a\,r\) and use \(\int_s^\infty u^{q-1}e^{-u^2}\,\mathrm{d} u\le C_q e^{-s^2/2}\) for all \(s\ge0\). \emph{Outside the tube.} Let \(R:=\max\{t,r_{\mathrm{tube}}\}\). We give a direct bound for this part. Since \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), every point with \(\|x\|>\mathsf D+R\) satisfies \[ \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge \|x\|-\mathsf D. \] Hence \begin{align*} \int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge R} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal S)}\,\mathrm{d} x &\le \int_{\substack{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge R\\ \|x\|\le \mathsf D+R}} e^{-aR^2}\,\mathrm{d} x \ +\ \int_{\|x\|>\mathsf D+R} e^{-a(\|x\|-\mathsf D)^2}\,\mathrm{d} x \\ &\le C_d(\mathsf D+R)^d e^{-aR^2} \ +\ C_d\int_R^\infty (\mathsf D+s)^{d-1}e^{-a s^2}\,\mathrm{d} s, \end{align*} where the last line uses polar coordinates with \(s=\|x\|-\mathsf D\) for the radial tail. Because \(R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}>0\), the polynomial factors are dominated by the Gaussian decay. More explicitly, using the standard one-dimensional Gaussian-tail bound \[ \int_R^\infty (\mathsf D+s)^{d-1}e^{-a s^2}\,\mathrm{d} s \le C_{d,\mathsf D,r_{\mathrm{tube}}}\,a^{-1}(1+R^{d-2})e^{-aR^2} \] for \(R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}\), and increasing the constant to also cover the bounded-annulus term, there exists \(a_0<\infty\) such that for all \(a\ge a_0\), \begin{align} \int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge \max\{t,r_{\mathrm{tube}}\}} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal S)}\,\mathrm{d} x &\le C_5\,a^{-q/2}\exp\!\big(-a t^2/2\big). \end{align} Indeed, the last step follows because \[ \sup_{\substack{a\ge a_0\\ R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} a^{q/2}(\mathsf D+R)^d e^{-aR^2/2} <\infty, \qquad \sup_{\substack{a\ge a_0\\ R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} a^{q/2-1}(1+R^{d-2}) e^{-aR^2/2} <\infty, \] and \(R\ge t\). Choose \(\lambda_0>0\) small enough so that the denominator lower bound above holds and \(a=\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}/(2\lambda)\ge a_0\) whenever \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\). Combining \eqref{eq:gibbs-num-near} and \eqref{eq:gibbs-num-far}, \[ \int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S})}\,\mathrm{d} x \le C_{\mathrm{num}}\,a^{-q/2}\exp\!\big(-a t^2/2\big) \le C_{\mathrm{num}}'\,\lambda^{q/2}\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{4\lambda}t^2\Big). \] Dividing this numerator bound by \eqref{eq:gibbs-den-lower} yields \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail}. Integrating \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail} over $t\ge 0$ yields $\mathbb E[R]\le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda}$. Similarly, \[ \mathbb E[R^2] =2\int_0^\infty t\,\mathbb P(R\ge t)\,\mathrm{d} t \le 2C_{\mathrm{tube}}\int_0^\infty t\,\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t \le C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\lambda \] after increasing the constant if needed. Finally, set \(R_i:=\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S})\). Since \(\tilde x\) is one of the candidates, \[ \mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S})\le \max_{1\le i\le M}R_i. \] By a union bound and \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail}, \[ \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big) \le \sum_{i=1}^M \mathbb P(R_i\ge t) \le M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big). \] To bound the expectation, use the tail integral representation \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\Big] =\int_0^\infty \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Let $t_0:=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda}{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\log(1+M)}$. Splitting the integral and using the bound above yields \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\Big] \le t_0 + \int_{t_0}^\infty M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Using $\int_{t_0}^\infty e^{-a t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t\le \frac{1}{2 a t_0}\,e^{-a t_0^2}$ for $a>0$ (with $a=c_{\mathrm{tube}}/\lambda$) gives \begin{align*} \int_{t_0}^\infty M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t &\le M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\cdot\frac{\lambda}{2c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,t_0}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t_0^2}{\lambda}\Big)\\ &= \frac{M}{1+M}\cdot\frac{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\cdot\frac{\lambda}{t_0}\\ &\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\,\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{\sqrt{\log(1+M)}}. \end{align*} Since \(M\ge1\), \(\log(1+M)\ge \log 2\), and we conclude that $\mathbb E[\max_i R_i]\le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}$ after adjusting $C_{\mathrm{tube}}$. Similarly, \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] = 2\int_0^\infty t\,\mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Splitting at the same $t_0$ and using $\int_{t_0}^\infty t e^{-a t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t=\frac{1}{2a}e^{-a t_0^2}$ with $a=c_{\mathrm{tube}}/\lambda$, we get \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] \le t_0^2+\frac{M C_{\mathrm{tube}}\lambda}{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t_0^2}{\lambda}\Big) \le C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\lambda\log(1+M), \] which yields \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2} after increasing $C_{\mathrm{tube},2}$.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic growth turns the Gibbs density into a Gaussian in normal coordinates; a λ^{q/2} lower bound on the normalizer and tube/outside numerator bounds give the tail. Key step: integrate in tubular normal coordinates.

nodes.name: Tail as a Gibbs ratio
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$ and abbreviate \(\mathcal{S}:=\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) and $g_\star:=\min_z g(\theta,z)$. By \Cref{lem:uniform-qg-g}, $g(\theta,x)\ge g_\star+\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2}\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S})$. Therefore, for any $t\ge 0$, \[ \mathbb P(R\ge t) =\frac{\int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t} e^{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x} \le \frac{\int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t} \exp\!\big(-\tfrac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2\lambda}\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S})\big)\,\mathrm{d} x}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-(g(\theta,x)-g_\star)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic growth bounds the Gibbs tail ratio.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Tubular coordinates
nodes.statement: Let \(q:=d-\texttt{k}\) be the normal dimension of \(\mathcal S\). Since \(\mathcal S\) is compact and embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), we have \(q\ge 1\). We next use a uniform tubular-coordinate estimate around the family \(\{\mathcal{S}(\theta)\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\). By compactness of the solution graph, the uniform normal spectral gap in \Cref{prop:geometry}, and the uniform curvature control in \Cref{prop:second-fund-from-g}, there are constants \(r_{\mathrm{tube}}>0\), \(0<J_{\min}\le J_{\max}<\infty\), and \(0<V_{\min}\le V_{\max}<\infty\), independent of \(\theta\), such that the normal map \[ \Phi_\theta(y,z)=y+z,\qquad y\in\mathcal S,\quad z\in\mathcal{N}_y^\theta,\quad \|z\|<r_{\mathrm{tube}}, \] is a diffeomorphism onto the \(r_{\mathrm{tube}}\)-tube around \(\mathcal S\), its Jacobian lies in \([J_{\min},J_{\max}]\), and the Riemannian volume of \(\mathcal S\) lies in \([V_{\min},V_{\max}]\).
nodes.statement_short: Uniform tubular coordinates with bounded Jacobian and volume.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Normalizer lower bound
nodes.statement: We first lower bound the denominator. Let \[ Z_\lambda(\theta):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} e^{-(g(\theta,x)-g_\star)/\lambda}\,\mathrm{d} x . \] The small-temperature normalizing-constant lower bound used in \citet[Lem.~D.1]{masiha2025superquantile}, applied here in the normal coordinates above, gives the manifold-version scaling \begin{equation} Z_\lambda(\theta)\ge c_{\mathrm{den}}\,\lambda^{q/2} \end{equation} for all sufficiently small \(\lambda\), with \(c_{\mathrm{den}}>0\) uniform in \(\theta\). The exponent is \(q/2\), rather than \(d/2\), because the Gibbs mass only concentrates in the \(q=d-\texttt{k}\) normal directions; integration along \(\mathcal S\) contributes a bounded positive manifold-volume factor.
nodes.statement_short: The normalizer is at least c λ^{q/2}.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Split numerator
nodes.statement: We now upper bound the numerator. Write \(a:=\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}/(2\lambda)\) and split the domain into the part inside the uniform tube and the part outside it.
nodes.statement_short: Split the numerator into tube and outside parts.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Inside the tube
nodes.statement: \emph{Inside the tube.} Every point in the tube has a unique representation \(x=y+z\), where \(y\in\mathcal S\) and \(z\in\mathcal{N}_y^\theta\). Here \(\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathcal S}(y)\) denotes the intrinsic \(\texttt{k}\)-dimensional volume measure on \(\mathcal S\) induced by the ambient Euclidean metric; for example, it is arclength when \(\texttt{k}=1\) and surface area when \(\texttt{k}=2\). Thus \[ \int_{\mathcal S}\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathcal S}(y)=\mathrm{Vol}_{\texttt{k}}(\mathcal S). \] In these coordinates, \(\mathrm{dist}(y+z,\mathcal S)=\|z\|\) and the Euclidean volume element decomposes as \[ \mathrm{d} x=J_\theta(y,z)\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathcal S}(y), \] where \(J_\theta(y,z)\le J_{\max}\). Therefore, after integrating out the \(y\)-variable using \(\mathrm{Vol}_{\texttt{k}}(\mathcal S)\le V_{\max}\), and identifying each normal fiber \(\mathcal{N}_y^\theta\) with \(\mathbb{R}^q\) through an arbitrary orthonormal basis, the tube contribution is bounded by a \(q\)-dimensional Gaussian tail: \begin{align} \int_{\substack{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge t\\ \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)<r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal S)}\,\mathrm{d} x &\le J_{\max}V_{\max} \int_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{R}^q:\ \|z\|\ge t\\ \|z\|<r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} e^{-a\|z\|^2}\,\mathrm{d} z \nonumber\\ &\le J_{\max}V_{\max}\,|\mathbb S^{q-1}| \int_t^\infty e^{-a r^2}r^{q-1}\,\mathrm{d} r \nonumber\\ &\le C_1\,a^{-q/2}\exp\!\big(-a t^2/2\big). \end{align} The second inequality is just polar coordinates in the \(q\)-dimensional normal variable \(z\): writing \(z=r\omega\), with \(\omega\in\mathbb S^{q-1}\), gives \(\mathrm{d} z=r^{q-1}\mathrm{d} r\,\mathrm{d}\sigma(\omega)\), and integrating over \(\omega\) gives the factor \(|\mathbb S^{q-1}|\). We then upper bound the radial integral by replacing the upper limit \(r_{\mathrm{tube}}\) with \(\infty\). For the last inequality, substitute \(u=\sqrt a\,r\) and use \(\int_s^\infty u^{q-1}e^{-u^2}\,\mathrm{d} u\le C_q e^{-s^2/2}\) for all \(s\ge0\).
nodes.statement_short: Normal coordinates reduce to a q-dimensional Gaussian tail.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Outside the tube
nodes.statement: \emph{Outside the tube.} Let \(R:=\max\{t,r_{\mathrm{tube}}\}\). We give a direct bound for this part. Since \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), every point with \(\|x\|>\mathsf D+R\) satisfies \[ \mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge \|x\|-\mathsf D. \] Hence \begin{align*} \int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge R} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal S)}\,\mathrm{d} x &\le \int_{\substack{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge R\\ \|x\|\le \mathsf D+R}} e^{-aR^2}\,\mathrm{d} x \ +\ \int_{\|x\|>\mathsf D+R} e^{-a(\|x\|-\mathsf D)^2}\,\mathrm{d} x \\ &\le C_d(\mathsf D+R)^d e^{-aR^2} \ +\ C_d\int_R^\infty (\mathsf D+s)^{d-1}e^{-a s^2}\,\mathrm{d} s, \end{align*} where the last line uses polar coordinates with \(s=\|x\|-\mathsf D\) for the radial tail. Because \(R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}>0\), the polynomial factors are dominated by the Gaussian decay. More explicitly, using the standard one-dimensional Gaussian-tail bound \[ \int_R^\infty (\mathsf D+s)^{d-1}e^{-a s^2}\,\mathrm{d} s \le C_{d,\mathsf D,r_{\mathrm{tube}}}\,a^{-1}(1+R^{d-2})e^{-aR^2} \] for \(R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}\), and increasing the constant to also cover the bounded-annulus term, there exists \(a_0<\infty\) such that for all \(a\ge a_0\), \begin{align} \int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal S)\ge \max\{t,r_{\mathrm{tube}}\}} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal S)}\,\mathrm{d} x &\le C_5\,a^{-q/2}\exp\!\big(-a t^2/2\big). \end{align} Indeed, the last step follows because \[ \sup_{\substack{a\ge a_0\\ R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} a^{q/2}(\mathsf D+R)^d e^{-aR^2/2} <\infty, \qquad \sup_{\substack{a\ge a_0\\ R\ge r_{\mathrm{tube}}}} a^{q/2-1}(1+R^{d-2}) e^{-aR^2/2} <\infty, \] and \(R\ge t\).
nodes.statement_short: Polynomial factors are dominated by Gaussian decay.
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Tail and moments
nodes.statement: Choose \(\lambda_0>0\) small enough so that the denominator lower bound above holds and \(a=\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}/(2\lambda)\ge a_0\) whenever \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\). Combining \eqref{eq:gibbs-num-near} and \eqref{eq:gibbs-num-far}, \[ \int_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t} e^{-a\,\mathrm{dist}^2(x,\mathcal{S})}\,\mathrm{d} x \le C_{\mathrm{num}}\,a^{-q/2}\exp\!\big(-a t^2/2\big) \le C_{\mathrm{num}}'\,\lambda^{q/2}\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{4\lambda}t^2\Big). \] Dividing this numerator bound by \eqref{eq:gibbs-den-lower} yields \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail}. Integrating \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail} over $t\ge 0$ yields $\mathbb E[R]\le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda}$. Similarly, \[ \mathbb E[R^2] =2\int_0^\infty t\,\mathbb P(R\ge t)\,\mathrm{d} t \le 2C_{\mathrm{tube}}\int_0^\infty t\,\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t \le C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\lambda \] after increasing the constant if needed.
nodes.statement_short: Combine numerator and denominator to get the tail, then integrate for E[R], E[R²].
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Max over candidates
nodes.statement: Finally, set \(R_i:=\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S})\). Since \(\tilde x\) is one of the candidates, \[ \mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S})\le \max_{1\le i\le M}R_i. \] By a union bound and \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail}, \[ \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big) \le \sum_{i=1}^M \mathbb P(R_i\ge t) \le M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big). \] To bound the expectation, use the tail integral representation \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\Big] =\int_0^\infty \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Let $t_0:=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda}{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\log(1+M)}$. Splitting the integral and using the bound above yields \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\Big] \le t_0 + \int_{t_0}^\infty M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Using $\int_{t_0}^\infty e^{-a t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t\le \frac{1}{2 a t_0}\,e^{-a t_0^2}$ for $a>0$ (with $a=c_{\mathrm{tube}}/\lambda$) gives \begin{align*} \int_{t_0}^\infty M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t &\le M\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\cdot\frac{\lambda}{2c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,t_0}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t_0^2}{\lambda}\Big)\\ &= \frac{M}{1+M}\cdot\frac{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\cdot\frac{\lambda}{t_0}\\ &\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\,\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{\sqrt{\log(1+M)}}. \end{align*} Since \(M\ge1\), \(\log(1+M)\ge \log 2\), and we conclude that $\mathbb E[\max_i R_i]\le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}$ after adjusting $C_{\mathrm{tube}}$. Similarly, \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] = 2\int_0^\infty t\,\mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Splitting at the same $t_0$ and using $\int_{t_0}^\infty t e^{-a t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t=\frac{1}{2a}e^{-a t_0^2}$ with $a=c_{\mathrm{tube}}/\lambda$, we get \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] \le t_0^2+\frac{M C_{\mathrm{tube}}\lambda}{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t_0^2}{\lambda}\Big) \le C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\lambda\log(1+M), \] which yields \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2} after increasing $C_{\mathrm{tube},2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound and tail integration give the max-distance bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 12
nodes.statement:
Fix $	heta$ and abbreviate \(\mathcal{S}:=\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) and \(R_i:=\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S})\). For any candidate index $i$, let \(A_t:=\{x:\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t\}\). Under $R_2(
u_i\|\mu_	heta^\lambda)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2$, Cauchy--Schwarz yields \[ 
u_i(A_t) =\int \mathbf 1_{A_t}\, rac{\delta 
u_i}{\delta \mu_	heta^\lambda}\,\delta \mu_	heta^\lambda \le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\,\mu_	heta^\lambda(A_t)^{1/2}. \] Combining this with the Gibbs tail \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail} gives $\mathbb P(R_i\ge t)\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}\exp\! ig(-	frac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}	frac{t^2}{\lambda} ig)$, and hence (by a union bound) \[ \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big) \le M\,e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}\exp\!\Big(-	frac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}	frac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big). \] This proves \eqref{eq:nu-tail-max}. To integrate the tail, set \[ A_{\mathrm R}:=e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}, \qquad  eta:= rac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2\lambda}, \qquad t_0:=\sqrt{ eta^{-1}\log(1+M)}. \] Then \eqref{eq:nu-tail-max} gives \[ \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M}R_i\ge t\Big) \le \min\{1,\;M A_{\mathrm R}e^{- eta t^2}\}. \] Using the tail integral formula and splitting at \(t_0\),  egin{align*} \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\Big] &\le t_0+M A_{\mathrm R}\int_{t_0}^{\infty}e^{- eta t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t\ &\le t_0+ rac{M A_{\mathrm R}}{2 eta t_0}e^{- eta t_0^2}\ &\le C(1+A_{\mathrm R})\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)} \le C' e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}, \end{align*} where the constants absorb \(C_{\mathrm{tube}}\), \(c_{\mathrm{tube}}\), and the fact that \(\log(1+M)\ge\log 2\). After increasing \(C_{\mathrm{tube}}\), this proves \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max-lmc}. Similarly, \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] = 2\int_0^\infty t\,\mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Splitting at the same \(t_0\) gives  egin{align*} \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] &\le t_0^2+2M A_{\mathrm R}\int_{t_0}^{\infty}t e^{- eta t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t\ &=t_0^2+ rac{M A_{\mathrm R}}{ eta}e^{- eta t_0^2}\ &\le C(1+A_{\mathrm R})\lambda\log(1+M) \le C' e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\lambda\log(1+M). \end{align*} After increasing \(C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\), this proves \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2-lmc}. Finally, since the hard-selection output \(	ilde x\in\arg\min_i f(	heta,X_i)\) is one of the candidates, \[ \mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}) \le \max_{1\le i\le M}R_i, \] which gives the first inequalities in \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max-lmc} and \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2-lmc}.

nodes.statement:
Fix $	heta$ and abbreviate \(\mathcal{S}:=\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) and \(R_i:=\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S})\). For any candidate index $i$, let \(A_t:=\{x:\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S})\ge t\}\). Under $R_2(
u_i\|\mu_	heta^\lambda)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2$, Cauchy--Schwarz yields \[ 
u_i(A_t) =\int \mathbf 1_{A_t}\, rac{\delta 
u_i}{\delta \mu_	heta^\lambda}\,\delta \mu_	heta^\lambda \le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\,\mu_	heta^\lambda(A_t)^{1/2}. \]

nodes.name: Max tail
nodes.statement: Combining this with the Gibbs tail \eqref{eq:gibbs-tail} gives $\mathbb P(R_i\ge t)\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}\exp\!\big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\big)$, and hence (by a union bound) \[ \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big) \le M\,e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big). \] This proves \eqref{eq:nu-tail-max}.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound gives (26).

nodes.name: First moment
nodes.statement: To integrate the tail, set \[ A_{\mathrm R}:=e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}, \qquad \beta:=\frac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2\lambda}, \qquad t_0:=\sqrt{\beta^{-1}\log(1+M)}. \] Then \eqref{eq:nu-tail-max} gives \[ \mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M}R_i\ge t\Big) \le \min\{1,\;M A_{\mathrm R}e^{-\beta t^2}\}. \] Using the tail integral formula and splitting at \(t_0\), \begin{align*} \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\Big] &\le t_0+M A_{\mathrm R}\int_{t_0}^{\infty}e^{-\beta t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t\\ &\le t_0+\frac{M A_{\mathrm R}}{2\beta t_0}e^{-\beta t_0^2}\\ &\le C(1+A_{\mathrm R})\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)} \le C' e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}, \end{align*} where the constants absorb \(C_{\mathrm{tube}}\), \(c_{\mathrm{tube}}\), and the fact that \(\log(1+M)\ge\log 2\). After increasing \(C_{\mathrm{tube}}\), this proves \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max-lmc}.
nodes.statement_short: Split the tail integral at t_0 to get (27).
nodes.section: E.3.2 Controlling the off-manifold term $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$

nodes.name: Second moment
nodes.statement: Similarly, \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] = 2\int_0^\infty t\,\mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i\ge t\Big)\,\mathrm{d} t. \] Splitting at the same \(t_0\) gives \begin{align*} \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M} R_i^2\Big] &\le t_0^2+2M A_{\mathrm R}\int_{t_0}^{\infty}t e^{-\beta t^2}\,\mathrm{d} t\\ &=t_0^2+\frac{M A_{\mathrm R}}{\beta}e^{-\beta t_0^2}\\ &\le C(1+A_{\mathrm R})\lambda\log(1+M) \le C' e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\lambda\log(1+M). \end{align*} After increasing \(C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\), this proves \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2-lmc}.
nodes.statement_short: Same splitting gives (28).

nodes.statement: Finally, since the hard-selection output \(\tilde x\in\arg\min_i f(\theta,X_i)\) is one of the candidates, \[ \mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}) \le \max_{1\le i\le M}R_i, \] which gives the first inequalities in \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max-lmc} and \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2-lmc}.

nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$, candidates $X_1,\dots,X_M$, and $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let \( \tilde x \in \arg\min_{i\in[1:M]} f(\theta,X_i). \) Then \[ f(\theta,\tilde x)\ \le\ \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta\big(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\widehat\nu_M\big). \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 13
nodes.statement: Under the empirical law \(\widehat\nu_M\), the random variable \(f(\theta,X)\) takes values among \(\{f(\theta,X_i)\}_{i=1}^M\). Let \(m:=\min_{1\le i\le M}f(\theta,X_i)=f(\theta,\tilde x)\). For every \(u\in(0,1)\), no value below \(m\) can have empirical probability at least \(u\), hence \(q_u(f(\theta,X))\ge m\). Averaging this pointwise inequality over \(u\in(0,\delta)\) gives the claim.

Fix $	heta$ and let $x^\star(	heta)$ be the unique minimizer of $f(	heta,\cdot)$ over $\mathcal{S}(	heta)$. Assume \(	exttt{k}\ge1\) and that $x\mapsto f(	heta,x)$ is $L_{f,1}$-Lipschitz (as in \Cref{assum_sample_comp}). Given candidates \(X_1,\ldots,X_M\), let \[ \widehat
u_M:= rac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\delta_{X_i}, \qquad 	ilde x\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le M}f(	heta,X_i), \] with any measurable tie-breaking rule, and let $ ar x$ be any measurable Euclidean projection of \(	ilde x\) onto \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\). Then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\),  egin{align} 0 \ \le\ f(	heta, ar x)-f(	heta,x^\star(	heta)) \ \le\ & L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}(	heta)) 
onumber\ &\quad + \Big[\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta ig(f(	heta,X);\,X\sim\widehat
u_M ig) - f(	heta,x^\star(	heta))\Big]. \end{align} Moreover, for any reference measure $
u$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite first moment,  egin{align} \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta ig(f(	heta,X);\,X\sim\widehat
u_M ig) - \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta ig(f(	heta,X);\,X\sim
u ig) \ \le\  rac{L_{f,1}}{\delta}\;\mathsf{W}_1(\widehat
u_M,

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 14
nodes.statement:
We first prove the deterministic bounds. Since \( ar x\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) and \(x^\star(	heta)\) minimizes \(f(	heta,\cdot)\) over \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\), the left inequality in \eqref{eq:value-gap-basic} holds. By Lipschitzness and the definition of \( ar x\), \[ f(	heta, ar x) \le f(	heta,	ilde x)+L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}(	heta)). \] Using \Cref{lem:tail-to-sq} to bound \(f(	heta,	ilde x)\) by the empirical lower superquantile gives \eqref{eq:value-gap-basic}. To prove \eqref{eq:sq-w1-lip}, use the variational representation \[ \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta(Z) = \sup_{	au\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{	au- rac1\delta\mathbb E[(	au-Z)_+]ight\}. \] For any coupling of \(X\sim\widehat
u_M\) and \(Y\sim
u\), the map \(z\mapsto(	au-f(	heta,z))_+\) is \(L_{f,1}\)-Lipschitz, and therefore, for every \(	au\), \[ 	au- rac1\delta\mathbb E[(	au-f(	heta,X))_+] \le 	au- rac1\delta\mathbb E[(	au-f(	heta,Y))_+] + rac{L_{f,1}}{\delta}\mathbb E\|X-Y\|. \] Taking the supremum over \(	au\) and then the infimum over couplings gives \eqref{eq:sq-w1-lip}. Combining \eqref{eq:value-gap-basic} and \eqref{eq:sq-w1-lip} with \(
u=\mu_	heta^\lambda\) gives \eqref{eq:value-gap-gibbs}. The deterministic bound \eqref{eq:value-gap-gibbs} is valid for any $\delta$, but when $\delta=1/M$ it yields the loose factor $\delta^{-1}=M$ multiplying the empirical discrepancy term. We therefore analyze the hard-min selection directly. Write $	ilde x\in\arg\min_i f(	heta,X_i)$. By Lipschitzness and the definition of $ ar x$, \[ f(	heta, ar x)\ \le\ f(	heta,	ilde x)+L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}(	heta)). \] Taking expectations gives  egin{equation} \mathbb E ig[f(	heta, ar x)-F(	heta) ig] \ \le\ L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E ig[\mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}(	heta)) ig] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,X_i)\Big]-F(	heta). \end{equation} \paragraph{Step 1: hard-min bound under exact Gibbs sampling.} Assume first that $X_1,\dots,X_M\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mu_	heta^\lambda$. For each $i$, let $\Pi(X_i)\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(	heta)}\|x-X_i\|$ be a Euclidean projection onto $\mathcal{S}(	heta)$ (choose any measurable selection). By Lipschitzness, \[ f(	heta,X_i)\ \le\ f(	heta,\Pi(X_i)) + L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta)). \] Taking the minimum over $i$ and using $\min_i (a_i+b_i)\le \min_i a_i + \max_i b_i$ gives \[ \min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,X_i) \ \le\ \min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,\Pi(X_i)) +\ L_{f,1}\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta)). \] Plugging this into \eqref{eq:inner-gap-split} and using $\mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\le \max_i \mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))$ yields  egin{equation} \mathbb E ig[f(	heta, ar x)-F(	heta) ig] \ \le\ 2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\Big] +\ \Big(\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,\Pi(X_i))\Big]-F(	heta)\Big). \end{equation} The tube bound in \Cref{lem:gibbs-tube-width} gives \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\Big] \le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}. \] For the on-manifold term, note that the projected points \(\Pi(X_i)\) lie on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\). Under our standing regularity assumptions, the projected Gibbs law converges, as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), to the limiting on-manifold law \(\mu_	heta^0\), whose density with respect to Riemannian volume on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) is continuous and strictly positive near \(x^\star(	heta)\); see \citep[Prop.~3.7]{masiha2025superquantile}. Therefore, after decreasing \(\lambda_0\) if needed, the projected Gibbs laws satisfy a uniform small-ball lower bound near \(x^\star(	heta)\). Combined with geodesic volume scaling on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\) \citep[Lem.~4.1]{masiha2025superquantile}--whose curvature requirement is verified in \Cref{prop:second-fund-from-g}--there are constants \(c_0>0\) and \(r_{\mathrm{nn}}>0\) such that, for every \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \[ \mathbb P ig(d_{\mathcal{S}(	heta)}(\Pi(X_1),x^\star(	heta))\le r ig)\ge c_0 r^{	exttt{k}}, \qquad 0<r\le r_{\mathrm{nn}}. \] Let \(D_M:=\min_{1\le i\le M}d_{\mathcal{S}(	heta)}(\Pi(X_i),x^\star(	heta))\). The small-ball bound gives \[ \mathbb P(D_M>r) \le (1-c_0r^{	exttt{k}})^M \le \exp(-Mc_0r^{	exttt{k}}), \qquad 0<r\le r_{\mathrm{nn}}, \] Let \(\mathrm{diam}_{\mathcal{S}}\) denote the finite geodesic diameter of \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\). Integrating this tail bound gives  egin{align*} \mathbb E[D_M] &=\int_0^{\mathrm{diam}_{\mathcal{S}}}\mathbb P(D_M>r)\,\mathrm{d} r\ &\le \int_0^{r_{\mathrm{nn}}} \exp(-Mc_0r^{	exttt{k}})\,\mathrm{d} r +\mathrm{diam}_{\mathcal{S}}\exp(-Mc_0r_{\mathrm{nn}}^{	exttt{k}})\ &\le C_{\mathrm{nn}}M^{-1/	exttt{k}}, \end{align*} where the last line uses \(	exttt{k}\ge1\) and absorbs the exponentially small term into the same polynomial rate for all \(M\ge1\). Since \(f(	heta,\cdot)\) is \(L_{f,1}\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathcal{S}(	heta)\), \[ \mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,\Pi(X_i))\Big]-F(	heta) \le L_{f,1}\mathbb E[D_M] \le C_1M^{-1/	exttt{k}}. \] Moreover, the display preceding \eqref{eq:inner-gap-max} also gives  egin{align*} &L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\Big] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,X_i)\Big]-F(	heta)\ &\qquad\le 2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\Big] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,\Pi(X_i))\Big]-F(	heta). \end{align*} Substituting the tube and nearest-neighbor bounds into this display gives the exact-Gibbs reference bound  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} &L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\Big]\ &\qquad +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,X_i)\Big]-F(	heta)\ &\le 2L_{f,1}\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)} +\ C_1\,M^{-1/	exttt{k}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} \paragraph{Step 2: transfer to R'enyi-controlled candidates.} We now return to independent candidates $X_1,\dots,X_M$ with marginal laws $
u_i$ satisfying $R_2(
u_i\|\mu_	heta^\lambda)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2$. For each $i$, choose an optimal coupling of \(X_i\sim
u_i\) with a reference variable \(X_i^\lambda\sim\mu_	heta^\lambda\) so that \[ \mathbb E\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|^2 \le \mathsf W_2(
u_i,\mu_	heta^\lambda)^2. \] Taking the product of these pairwise couplings gives a joint coupling whose first marginal is \(
u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes
u_M\), the law of the actual independent candidates, and whose second marginal is \((\mu_	heta^\lambda)^{\otimes M}\). Thus the reference variables \(X_1^\lambda,\ldots,X_M^\lambda\) are i.i.d.\ from \(\mu_	heta^\lambda\), and expectations of functions of \(X_1,\ldots,X_M\) are unchanged under this coupling. We use the two deterministic comparisons \[  egin{aligned} \mathrm{dist}(	ilde x,\mathcal{S}(	heta)) &\le \max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\ &\le \max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i^\lambda,\mathcal{S}(	heta)) +\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\| \end{aligned} \] and \[ \min_{1\le i\le M}f(	heta,X_i) \le \min_{1\le i\le M}f(	heta,X_i^\lambda)+L_{f,1}\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|, \] and combine them with \eqref{eq:inner-gap-split}, applied to the actual candidates, to obtain  egin{align*} \mathbb E ig[f(	heta, ar x)-F(	heta) ig] &\le L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i^\lambda,\mathcal{S}(	heta))\Big] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(	heta,X_i^\lambda)\Big]-F(	heta)\ &\quad +2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|\Big]. \end{align*} The first two terms on the right are controlled by the exact-Gibbs reference bound \eqref{eq:inner-gap-exact-gibbs}. It remains to bound the coupling error \[ 2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|\Big]. \] Finally, $\max_i a_i\le (\sum_i a_i^2)^{1/2}$ gives \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|\Big] \le \Big(\sum_{i=1}^M \mathbb E\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|^2\Big)^{1/2} \le \Bigg(\sum_{i=1}^M \mathsf W_2(
u_i,\mu_	heta^\lambda)^2\Bigg)^{1/2}, \] and the Poincar'e/R'enyi transportation inequality \citep{liu2020poincare} gives \[ \mathsf W_2(

u_i\|\mu_	heta^\lambda)}-1 ig)^{1/2} \le 2\sqrt{(e-1)C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}. \] The last inequality uses \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), so \(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2}-1\le (e-1)\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2\). nodes.name: Deterministic value-gap bound
nodes.statement: We first prove the deterministic bounds. Since \(\bar x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) and \(x^\star(\theta)\) minimizes \(f(\theta,\cdot)\) over \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), the left inequality in \eqref{eq:value-gap-basic} holds. By Lipschitzness and the definition of \(\bar x\), \[ f(\theta,\bar x) \le f(\theta,\tilde x)+L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)). \] Using \Cref{lem:tail-to-sq} to bound \(f(\theta,\tilde x)\) by the empirical lower superquantile gives \eqref{eq:value-gap-basic}.

u_M\) and \(Y\sim
u\), the map \(z\mapsto(	au-f(	heta,z))_+\) is \(L_{f,1}\)-Lipschitz, and therefore, for every \(	au\), \[ 	au- rac1\delta\mathbb E[(	au-f(	heta,X))_+] \le 	au- rac1\delta\mathbb E[(	au-f(	heta,Y))_+] + rac{L_{f,1}}{\delta}\mathbb E\|X-Y\|. \] Taking the supremum over \(	au\) and then the infimum over couplings gives \eqref{eq:sq-w1-lip}. nodes.name: Direct hard-min split
nodes.statement: The deterministic bound \eqref{eq:value-gap-gibbs} is valid for any $\delta$, but when $\delta=1/M$ it yields the loose factor $\delta^{-1}=M$ multiplying the empirical discrepancy term. We therefore analyze the hard-min selection directly. Write $\tilde x\in\arg\min_i f(\theta,X_i)$. By Lipschitzness and the definition of $\bar x$, \[ f(\theta,\bar x)\ \le\ f(\theta,\tilde x)+L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)). \] Taking expectations gives \begin{equation} \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big] \ \le\ L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\big] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,X_i)\Big]-F(\theta). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Avoid the factor M: split the expected gap into a distance term and an expected hard-min term.
nodes.section: E.3.3 From hard selection to a value gap on $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$

nodes.name: Exact Gibbs hard-min bound
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 1: hard-min bound under exact Gibbs sampling.} Assume first that $X_1,\dots,X_M\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mu_\theta^\lambda$. For each $i$, let $\Pi(X_i)\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\|x-X_i\|$ be a Euclidean projection onto $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ (choose any measurable selection). By Lipschitzness, \[ f(\theta,X_i)\ \le\ f(\theta,\Pi(X_i)) + L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta)). \] Taking the minimum over $i$ and using $\min_i (a_i+b_i)\le \min_i a_i + \max_i b_i$ gives \[ \min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,X_i) \ \le\ \min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,\Pi(X_i)) +\ L_{f,1}\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta)). \] Plugging this into \eqref{eq:inner-gap-split} and using $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le \max_i \mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$ yields \begin{equation} \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big] \ \le\ 2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big] +\ \Big(\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,\Pi(X_i))\Big]-F(\theta)\Big). \end{equation} The tube bound in \Cref{lem:gibbs-tube-width} gives \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big] \le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}. \] For the on-manifold term, note that the projected points \(\Pi(X_i)\) lie on \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Under our standing regularity assumptions, the projected Gibbs law converges, as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), to the limiting on-manifold law \(\mu_\theta^0\), whose density with respect to Riemannian volume on \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is continuous and strictly positive near \(x^\star(\theta)\); see \citep[Prop.~3.7]{masiha2025superquantile}. Therefore, after decreasing \(\lambda_0\) if needed, the projected Gibbs laws satisfy a uniform small-ball lower bound near \(x^\star(\theta)\). Combined with geodesic volume scaling on \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) \citep[Lem.~4.1]{masiha2025superquantile}--whose curvature requirement is verified in \Cref{prop:second-fund-from-g}--there are constants \(c_0>0\) and \(r_{\mathrm{nn}}>0\) such that, for every \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \[ \mathbb P\big(d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(\Pi(X_1),x^\star(\theta))\le r\big)\ge c_0 r^{\texttt{k}}, \qquad 0<r\le r_{\mathrm{nn}}. \] Let \(D_M:=\min_{1\le i\le M}d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(\Pi(X_i),x^\star(\theta))\). The small-ball bound gives \[ \mathbb P(D_M>r) \le (1-c_0r^{\texttt{k}})^M \le \exp(-Mc_0r^{\texttt{k}}), \qquad 0<r\le r_{\mathrm{nn}}, \] Let \(\mathrm{diam}_{\mathcal{S}}\) denote the finite geodesic diameter of \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Integrating this tail bound gives \begin{align*} \mathbb E[D_M] &=\int_0^{\mathrm{diam}_{\mathcal{S}}}\mathbb P(D_M>r)\,\mathrm{d} r\\ &\le \int_0^{r_{\mathrm{nn}}} \exp(-Mc_0r^{\texttt{k}})\,\mathrm{d} r +\mathrm{diam}_{\mathcal{S}}\exp(-Mc_0r_{\mathrm{nn}}^{\texttt{k}})\\ &\le C_{\mathrm{nn}}M^{-1/\texttt{k}}, \end{align*} where the last line uses \(\texttt{k}\ge1\) and absorbs the exponentially small term into the same polynomial rate for all \(M\ge1\). Since \(f(\theta,\cdot)\) is \(L_{f,1}\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), \[ \mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,\Pi(X_i))\Big]-F(\theta) \le L_{f,1}\mathbb E[D_M] \le C_1M^{-1/\texttt{k}}. \] Moreover, the display preceding \eqref{eq:inner-gap-max} also gives \begin{align*} &L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,X_i)\Big]-F(\theta)\\ &\qquad\le 2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big] +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,\Pi(X_i))\Big]-F(\theta). \end{align*} Substituting the tube and nearest-neighbor bounds into this display gives the exact-Gibbs reference bound \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big]\\ &\qquad +\mathbb E\Big[\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,X_i)\Big]-F(\theta)\\ &\le 2L_{f,1}\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)} +\ C_1\,M^{-1/\texttt{k}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Tube bound plus a small-ball nearest-neighbour rate M^{−1/k} on S(θ).

It remains to bound the coupling error \[ 2L_{f,1}\,\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|\Big]. \] Finally, $\max_i a_i\le (\sum_i a_i^2)^{1/2}$ gives \[ \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|\Big] \le \Big(\sum_{i=1}^M \mathbb E\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|^2\Big)^{1/2} \le \Bigg(\sum_{i=1}^M \mathsf W_2(
u_i,\mu_	heta^\lambda)^2\Bigg)^{1/2}, \] and the Poincar'e/R'enyi transportation inequality \citep{liu2020poincare} gives \[ \mathsf W_2(
u_i,\mu_	heta^\lambda) \le 2\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{1/2} ig(e^{R_2(
u_i\|\mu_	heta^\lambda)}-1 ig)^{1/2} \le 2\sqrt{(e-1)C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}. \] The last inequality uses \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), so \(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2}-1\le (e-1)\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2\). Therefore \[ 2L_{f,1}\, \mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\|X_i-X_i^\lambda\|\Big] \le 4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{M\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}. \] Combining this estimate with \eqref{eq:inner-gap-exact-gibbs} proves \eqref{eq:inner-gap-hardmin}.

nodes.name: Local quadratic growth from Riemannian non-degeneracy
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$ and suppose that $f(\theta,\cdot)$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ in a neighborhood of $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ and that $x^\star(\theta)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ is a local minimizer of \(f(\theta,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\). Assume moreover that the Riemannian Hessian of the restricted objective is positive definite at \(x^\star(\theta)\), i.e., there exists \(m_\theta>0\) such that \[ \big\langle v,\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\bar f_\theta(x^\star(\theta))[v]\big\rangle \ \ge\ m_\theta\|v\|^2, \qquad \forall v\in\mathcal{T}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta, \] where \(\bar f_\theta:=f(\theta,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\). Then there exist constants $c_{\mathrm{hg}}>0$ and $r_0>0$ such that for all $x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ with $d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))\le r_0$, \begin{equation} f(\theta,x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta)) \ \ge\ c_{\mathrm{hg}}\; d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))^2. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal M:=\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ be the embedded submanifold with the induced Riemannian metric, and define the restriction $\bar f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb{R}$ by $\bar f(x):=f(\theta,x)$. Since $f(\theta,\cdot)$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ on a neighborhood of $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal M$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ embedded, $\bar f$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ on $\mathcal M$. By the local-minimizer assumption, $x^\star:=x^\star(\theta)$ is a (local) minimizer of $\bar f$ on $\mathcal M$, so the Riemannian gradient vanishes: $\mathrm{grad}_{\mathcal M}\bar f(x^\star)=0$. Moreover, the assumed Riemannian non-degeneracy gives positive curvature of the restricted objective in every tangent direction. Define the minimal Riemannian Hessian eigenvalue \[ m \ :=\ \min_{\substack{v\in\mathcal T_{x^\star}\mathcal M\\ \|v\|=1}} \big\langle v,\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M}\bar f(x^\star)[v]\big\rangle \ >\ 0. \] Since $\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M}\bar f$ is continuous, there exists a neighborhood $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal M$ of $x^\star$ such that for all $y\in\mathcal U$ and all $w\in\mathcal T_y\mathcal M$, \begin{equation} \big\langle w,\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M}\bar f(y)[w]\big\rangle\ \ge\ \tfrac{m}{2}\,\|w\|^2. \end{equation} Let $r_0>0$ be such that the closed geodesic ball \(\{y\in\mathcal M:d_{\mathcal M}(y,x^\star)\le r_0\}\) is contained in $\mathcal U$. Fix any $x\in\mathcal M$ with $d_{\mathcal M}(x,x^\star)\le r_0$. Since $\mathcal M$ is compact (and hence complete), the Hopf--Rinow theorem guarantees the existence of a minimizing geodesic $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathcal M$ from $x^\star$ to $x$. See, e.g., \citep[Hopf--Rinow Theorem]{lee2006riemannian}. Parameterize $\gamma$ at constant speed so that $\|\dot\gamma(t)\|=d_{\mathcal M}(x,x^\star)$ for all $t\in[0,1]$. Because $\gamma$ is minimizing, each subsegment is minimizing, and hence \(d_{\mathcal M}(\gamma(t),x^\star)\le d_{\mathcal M}(x,x^\star)\le r_0\) for all \(t\in[0,1]\). Thus \(\gamma([0,1])\subset\mathcal U\). Define $\phi(t):=\bar f(\gamma(t))$. Then $\phi'(t)=\langle \mathrm{grad}_{\mathcal M}\bar f(\gamma(t)),\dot\gamma(t)\rangle$ and in particular $\phi'(0)=0$. Differentiating once more and using that $\gamma$ is a geodesic yields the standard identity \[ \phi''(t) \ =\ \big\langle \dot\gamma(t),\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M}\bar f(\gamma(t))[\dot\gamma(t)]\big\rangle. \] Therefore, by \eqref{eq:hess-lb-local} and constant speed, \[ \phi''(t) \ \ge\ \tfrac{m}{2}\,\|\dot\gamma(t)\|^2 \ =\ \tfrac{m}{2}\,d_{\mathcal M}(x,x^\star)^2 \qquad \forall t\in[0,1]. \] Using $\phi'(0)=0$ and the integral form of Taylor's theorem, \[ \phi(1)-\phi(0) =\int_0^1 (1-t)\,\phi''(t)\,\mathrm{d} t \ge \int_0^1 (1-t)\,\tfrac{m}{2}\,d_{\mathcal M}(x,x^\star)^2\,\mathrm{d} t =\tfrac{m}{4}\,d_{\mathcal M}(x,x^\star)^2. \] Recalling $\phi(1)=\bar f(x)$ and $\phi(0)=\bar f(x^\star)$ gives \eqref{eq:quadratic-growth-onS} with $c_{\mathrm{hg}}:=m/4$.

nodes.statement: Assume the setting of \Cref{sec:theory} and let \(m_{\mathrm R}>0\) be the uniform restricted-curvature constant from \Cref{prop:uniform-riem-nondeg}. Let $x^\star:\Theta\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be the global selected minimizer from \Cref{ass:unique_min}. Then there exist constants $c_{\mathrm{hg}}>0$ and $r_0>0$ such that for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all $x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ with $d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))\le r_0$, \[ f(\theta,x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta)) \ \ge\ c_{\mathrm{hg}}\; d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))^2. \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 16
nodes.statement: If \(\texttt{k}=0\), then each connected compact zero-dimensional manifold \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is a singleton. Hence the only point \(x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) is \(x^\star(\theta)\), and the claim is trivial for any fixed positive \(c_{\mathrm{hg}}\) and \(r_0\). We therefore assume \(\texttt{k}\ge1\). For each $\theta\in\Theta$, let $\mathcal M_\theta:=\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ and define the restriction $\bar f_\theta:\mathcal M_\theta\to\mathbb{R}$ by $\bar f_\theta(x):=f(\theta,x)$. By \Cref{ass:unique_min}, \(x^\star(\theta)\) is the unique minimizer of \(\bar f_\theta\) on \(\mathcal M_\theta\). By \Cref{prop:uniform-riem-nondeg}, for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), \[ \big\langle v,\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M_\theta}\bar f_\theta(x^\star(\theta))[v]\big\rangle \ge m_{\mathrm R}\|v\|^2, \qquad \forall v\in\mathcal T_{x^\star(\theta)}\mathcal M_\theta . \] We next make the neighborhood on which this lower bound persists uniform. For each \(\bar\theta\in\Theta\), continuity of the Riemannian Hessian in local charts gives a parameter neighborhood \(V_{\bar\theta}\) and a radius \(r_{\bar\theta}>0\) such that, for every \(\theta\in V_{\bar\theta}\), every \(y\in\mathcal M_\theta\) with \(d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(y,x^\star(\theta))\le r_{\bar\theta}\), and every \(w\in\mathcal T_y\mathcal M_\theta\), \[ \big\langle w,\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M_\theta}\bar f_\theta(y)[w]\big\rangle\ \ge\ \tfrac{m_{\mathrm R}}{2}\,\|w\|^2. \] Choose a finite subcover \(V_{\bar\theta_1},\ldots,V_{\bar\theta_J}\) of \(\Theta\) and set \[ r_0:=\min_{1\le j\le J} r_{\bar\theta_j}>0. \] Then, for all $\theta\in\Theta$, all $y\in\mathcal M_\theta$ with $d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(y,x^\star(\theta))\le r_0$, and all $w\in\mathcal T_y\mathcal M_\theta$, \[ \big\langle w,\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M_\theta}\bar f_\theta(y)[w]\big\rangle\ \ge\ \tfrac{m_{\mathrm R}}{2}\,\|w\|^2. \] Fix any $\theta\in\Theta$ and $x\in\mathcal M_\theta$ with $d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(x,x^\star(\theta))\le r_0$. Since $\mathcal M_\theta$ is compact, the Hopf--Rinow theorem yields a minimizing geodesic $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathcal M_\theta$ from $x^\star(\theta)$ to $x$. Parameterize $\gamma$ at constant speed so that $\|\dot\gamma(t)\|=d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(x,x^\star(\theta))$ for all $t\in[0,1]$. Since \(\gamma\) is minimizing, \(d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(\gamma(t),x^\star(\theta))\le r_0\) for all \(t\in[0,1]\), so the uniform Hessian lower bound above applies along the whole curve. As in the proof of \Cref{lem:hg-from-nondeg}, define $\phi(t):=\bar f_\theta(\gamma(t))$. Then $\phi'(0)=0$ and \[ \phi''(t) \ =\ \big\langle \dot\gamma(t),\ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal M_\theta}\bar f_\theta(\gamma(t))[\dot\gamma(t)]\big\rangle \ \ge\ \tfrac{m_{\mathrm R}}{2}\,d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(x,x^\star(\theta))^2, \] so the same integral argument yields \[ f(\theta,x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta)) \ =\ \phi(1)-\phi(0) \ \ge\ \tfrac{m_{\mathrm R}}{4}\,d_{\mathcal M_\theta}(x,x^\star(\theta))^2. \] The claim follows with $c_{\mathrm{hg}}:=m_{\mathrm R}/4$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 17
nodes.statement: If all \(\mathcal{S}_{r_0}(\theta)\) are empty, the claim is immediate by convention. Otherwise, consider \[ \mathcal A_{r_0} := \{(\theta,x):\theta\in\Theta,\ x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta),\ d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))\ge r_0\}. \] Under the uniform regularity assumptions used in \Cref{lem:uniform-hg}, the compact manifolds \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) vary continuously in local charts over compact \(\Theta\); hence their graph is compact and the geodesic distance to the continuous selected branch \(x^\star(\theta)\) is continuous on this graph. Therefore \(\mathcal A_{r_0}\) is compact. It is also disjoint from the selected graph \(\{(\theta,x^\star(\theta)):\theta\in\Theta\}\). The gap map \((\theta,x)\mapsto f(\theta,x)-F(\theta)\) is continuous and strictly positive on \(\mathcal A_{r_0}\): if it vanished at some \((\theta,x)\in\mathcal A_{r_0}\), then \(x\) would be another minimizer of \(f(\theta,\cdot)\) over \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), contradicting the uniqueness in \Cref{ass:unique_min}. A positive continuous function on a compact set has a positive minimum, which is exactly \(\Delta_{r_0}\).

Then for any $\theta\in\Theta$, \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 &\ \le\ \Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}+\frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg)\, \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big]. \end{aligned} \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 18
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta\in\Theta$ and define the suboptimality gap $\Delta(\bar x):=f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\ge 0$. Consider the event $\mathcal A:=\{\Delta(\bar x)<\Delta_{r_0}\}$. By definition of $\Delta_{r_0}$, on $\mathcal A$ we must have $d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(\bar x,x^\star(\theta))<r_0$, so \Cref{lem:uniform-hg} gives \[ d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(\bar x,x^\star(\theta)) \ \le\ \left(\frac{\Delta(\bar x)}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}\right)^{1/2}. \] Since the ambient Euclidean distance is bounded by the geodesic distance, this implies $\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2\le \Delta(\bar x)/c_{\mathrm{hg}}$ on $\mathcal A$. On $\mathcal A^c$, use $\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2\le 4\mathsf D^2$ (since $\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)$). Therefore, \[ \mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \ \le\ \frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}\mathbb E\big[\Delta(\bar x)\big] \ +\ 4\mathsf D^2\,\mathbb P(\mathcal A^c). \] Finally, $\mathbb P(\mathcal A^c)=\mathbb P(\Delta(\bar x)\ge \Delta_{r_0})\le \mathbb E[\Delta(\bar x)]/\Delta_{r_0}$ by Markov, yielding the claim.

nodes.name: ULA convergence in order-2 Rényi divergence
nodes.statement: Consider the unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA) iteration \[ X^{k+1}=X^{k}-h\nabla G(X^{k})+\sqrt{2h}\,\xi^{k}, \qquad \xi^{k}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d), \] targeting $\pi(\mathrm dx)\propto e^{-G(x)}\,\mathrm dx$. Assume $\nabla G$ is $L_{G,2}$-Lipschitz and that $\pi$ satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality with constant $C_{\mathrm{PI}}$. Let $\widehat\mu_n$ be the law of $X^{n}$. Then for any sufficiently small $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and an appropriate stepsize choice (as required by the ULA theory), one can ensure $R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\pi)\le \varepsilon^2$ after \begin{equation} n \;=\; \Theta\!\left( C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}L_{G,2}^{2}\,d\,\varepsilon^{-2}\Big(R_3(\widehat\mu_0\|\pi)^2+\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\Big) \right) \end{equation} iterations, where $R_q(\cdot\|\cdot)$ denotes the order-$q$ R\'enyi divergence. Moreover, using the transportation-variance implication of the Poincar\'e inequality \citep{liu2020poincare} to relate \(W_2\) and \(R_2\), we obtain \begin{equation} \mathsf W_2(\widehat\mu_n,\pi) \ \le\ 2\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{1/2}\,\big(e^{R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\pi)}-1\big)^{1/2} \ \le\ 2\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{1/2}\,C^{1/2}\,\varepsilon, \end{equation} where one may take the numerical constant $C:=2(e^{1/2}-1)$.

nodes.name: Order-3 Rényi warm start for λ-scaled Gaussian initialization
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum_sample_comp} hold, and let \(g_\star(\theta):=\min_x g(\theta,x)\). Since \(\mu_\theta^\lambda(\mathrm{d} x)=(Z_\theta^\lambda)^{-1}e^{-g(\theta,x)/\lambda}\mathrm{d} x\), the order-$3$ R\'enyi divergence is \[ R_3\!\left(\widehat\mu_{0,z}^{\lambda}\middle\|\mu_\theta^\lambda\right) = \frac12\log\left[ (Z_\theta^\lambda)^2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}p_{z,\lambda}(x)^3\exp\{2g(\theta,x)/\lambda\}\,\mathrm{d} x \right]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write R_3 via the Gibbs normalizer.
nodes.section: E.3.5 Sampler accuracy from R\'enyi divergence

nodes.name: Normalizer upper bound
nodes.statement: First, by \Cref{lem:uniform-qg-g} and \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D)\), \[ Z_\theta^\lambda \le e^{-g_\star(\theta)/\lambda} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \exp\!\left\{-\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2\lambda}\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\right\}\mathrm{d} x \le C_Z e^{-g_\star(\theta)/\lambda} \] for all \(0<\lambda\le1\), with \(C_Z\) uniform in \(\theta\). The last inequality follows because \(\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\ge(\|x\|-\mathsf D)_+\), and the resulting Gaussian tail is integrable uniformly for \(\lambda\le1\).
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic growth bounds Z_θ^λ ≤ C_Z e^{−g_⋆/λ}.
nodes.section: E.3.5 Sampler accuracy from R\'enyi divergence

nodes.name: Gaussian integral
nodes.statement: Next, set \(u=x-z\). By \(L_{g,2}\)-smoothness in \(x\), \[ g(\theta,z+u) \le g(\theta,z)+\langle \nabla_x g(\theta,z),u\rangle+\frac{L_{g,2}}{2}\|u\|^2. \] Since \[ p_{z,\lambda}(z+u)^3=(2\pi\tau\lambda)^{-3d/2} \exp\!\left\{-\frac{3}{2\tau\lambda}\|u\|^2\right\}, \] and \(a:=3/(2\tau)-L_{g,2}>0\), Gaussian integration gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}p_{z,\lambda}(x)^3\exp\{2g(\theta,x)/\lambda\}\,\mathrm{d} x\\ &\qquad\le C\,\lambda^{-d} \exp\!\left\{ \frac{2g(\theta,z)}{\lambda} +\frac{\|\nabla_x g(\theta,z)\|^2}{a\lambda} \right\}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: L_{g,2}-smoothness and Gaussian integration bound the integral.
nodes.section: E.3.5 Sampler accuracy from R\'enyi divergence

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining the two displays yields \[ R_3\!\left(\widehat\mu_{0,z}^{\lambda}\middle\|\mu_\theta^\lambda\right) \le \frac{g(\theta,z)-g_\star(\theta)}{\lambda} \ +\ \frac{\|\nabla_x g(\theta,z)\|^2}{2a\lambda} \ +\ \frac d2\log(1/\lambda)+C. \] The first two terms are uniformly bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{init}}/\lambda\), because \(\Theta\times\mathcal Z\) is compact and \(g_\star\) is continuous on \(\Theta\). This proves \eqref{eq:gaussian-init-r3}. If \(z\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), then \(g(\theta,z)=g_\star(\theta)\) and \(\nabla_x g(\theta,z)=0\), so only the logarithmic term remains, proving \eqref{eq:gaussian-init-r3-ons}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine; the first terms are O(1/λ), and vanish when z∈S(θ).
nodes.section: E.3.5 Sampler accuracy from R\'enyi divergence

nodes.name: Specialization of ULA Rényi accuracy to Gibbs sampling
nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{prop:lmc-renyi} with $G(x)=g(\theta,x)/\lambda$ and $\pi=\mu_\theta^\lambda$. Then $L_{G,2}=L_{g,2}/\lambda$ and the ULA update \[ X^{k+1}=X^{k}-h\nabla_x g(\theta,X^{k})+\sqrt{2\lambda h}\,\xi^{k} \] corresponds to the same ULA scheme with stepsize $h' = \lambda h$ for $G$. In particular, for any target R\'enyi tolerance $\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\in(0,1)$, running the chain for \[ n = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left( d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\lambda^{-2}\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2} \bigl(1+R_3(\widehat\mu_0\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)^2\bigr) \right) \] iterations ensures \(R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{2}\). If, moreover, \(\widehat\mu_0=\widehat\mu_{0,z}^{\lambda}\) is the \(\lambda\)-scaled Gaussian initialization in \Cref{lem:gaussian-init-r3} with \(z\in\mathcal Z\), then it suffices to run \begin{equation} n\ =\ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\lambda^{-4}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2}\right) \end{equation} iterations. If the Gaussian center satisfies \(z\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), then the sharper logarithmic bound \eqref{eq:gaussian-init-r3-ons} gives the improved sufficient count \[ n\ =\ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\lambda^{-2}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2}\right). \] In all cases, once \[ R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)\ \le\ \varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{2}, \] we have \[ \mathsf W_2(\widehat\mu_n,\mu_\theta^\lambda) \ \le\ 2\sqrt{(e-1)C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}, \qquad\text{and hence}\qquad \mathsf W_1(\widehat\mu_n,\mu_\theta^\lambda) \ \le\ 2\sqrt{(e-1)C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}. \]
nodes.section: E.3.5 Sampler accuracy from R\'enyi divergence
nodes.statement_short: For the Gibbs target, ULA needs Õ(d C_PI² λ^{−4} ε_R^{−2}) steps from a λ-scaled Gaussian start, and R_2 accuracy gives W_2, W_1 ≲ √C_PI ε_R.
nodes.label: cor:lmc-gibbs-w2

nodes.name: ULA step count from Gaussian warm start
nodes.statement: n\ =\ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\lambda^{-4}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2}\right)
nodes.section: E.3.5 Sampler accuracy from R\'enyi divergence
nodes.label: eq:lmc-n-final

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Let \(\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\|x-\tilde x\|\) be a measurable Euclidean projection of \(\tilde x\) onto \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). By the Euclidean triangle inequality and $(a+b)^2\le 2a^2+2b^2$, \[ \|\tilde x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \le 2\|\tilde x-\bar x\|^2+2\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 = 2\,\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2+2\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2. \] Taking expectations and applying \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2-lmc} from \Cref{lem:tube-width}, together with \(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2/2}\le e^{1/2}\) since \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), gives \[ \mathbb E\|\tilde x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \le 2e^{1/2}C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\log(1+N) +2\,\mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2. \] Then \Cref{lem:barx-distance} yields \[ \mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \le \Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}+\frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg)\, \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big]. \] Finally, the R\'enyi-controlled hard-selection bound \eqref{eq:inner-gap-hardmin} from \Cref{lem:inner-quality-gap} gives \[ \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big] \le 2L_{f,1}\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} +C_1\,N^{-1/\texttt{k}} +4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}, \] which gives \eqref{eq:final-Ex2-bound}.
nodes.section: E.3.6 Final assembly of the selection-error bound
nodes.statement_short: Split into tube error (Lemma 12) and on-manifold distance (Lemma 18 with the value gap of Lemma 14).

nodes.name: Triangle split
nodes.statement: Let \(\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\|x-\tilde x\|\) be a measurable Euclidean projection of \(\tilde x\) onto \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). By the Euclidean triangle inequality and $(a+b)^2\le 2a^2+2b^2$, \[ \|\tilde x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \le 2\|\tilde x-\bar x\|^2+2\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 = 2\,\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2+2\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Split the error into tube distance and on-manifold distance.
nodes.section: E.3.6 Final assembly of the selection-error bound

nodes.name: Tube term
nodes.statement: Taking expectations and applying \eqref{eq:dist-tilde-max2-lmc} from \Cref{lem:tube-width}, together with \(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2/2}\le e^{1/2}\) since \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), gives \[ \mathbb E\|\tilde x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \le 2e^{1/2}C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\log(1+N) +2\,\mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 12 bounds the tube term.
nodes.section: E.3.6 Final assembly of the selection-error bound

nodes.name: On-manifold distance
nodes.statement: Then \Cref{lem:barx-distance} yields \[ \mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2 \le \Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}+\frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg)\, \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 18 converts the value gap into distance.
nodes.section: E.3.6 Final assembly of the selection-error bound

nodes.name: Value gap
nodes.statement: Finally, the R\'enyi-controlled hard-selection bound \eqref{eq:inner-gap-hardmin} from \Cref{lem:inner-quality-gap} gives \[ \mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big] \le 2L_{f,1}\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} +C_1\,N^{-1/\texttt{k}} +4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}, \] which gives \eqref{eq:final-Ex2-bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 14 bounds the value gap, giving (6).
nodes.section: E.3.6 Final assembly of the selection-error bound

nodes.name: Hyper-gradient error in terms of algorithmic parameters
nodes.statement: Using the notation of \Cref{thm:et2-bound,thm:selection-error-bound}, suppose the assumptions therein hold. Assume additionally that \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\) and \(0<\gamma\le1\). Then, uniformly over \(t\), \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 &= \mathcal{O}\!\Bigg( \frac{1}{\gamma^2} \Big[ \lambda\log(1+N) \ +\ \sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} \ +\ N^{-1/\texttt{k}} \ +\ \sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} \ +\ \eta_t^2 \Big] \ +\ \gamma^2\\ &\qquad \ +\ (1+R_v^2)N \big(1+r(\gamma)^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}+\lambda^{\mathsf n_{\theta x}}\big)\\ &\qquad\qquad\qquad \times\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{4}\tfrac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda}\Big) \Bigg). \end{aligned} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 20 and Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: We first condition on the current outer iterate \(\theta_t\). The constants in \Cref{thm:selection-error-bound} and \Cref{lem:tube-width} are uniform over \(\theta\in\Theta\), so the resulting conditional bounds can be averaged over \(\theta_t\) without changing the constants. Combining \eqref{eq:et2-explicit} with \eqref{eq:final-Ex2-bound} from \Cref{thm:selection-error-bound} and the bound $\mathbb E\big[\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big]\le \mathbb E\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2$, we obtain the following bound, uniformly over \(t\): \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 \le\;& 3C_x^2 B_\gamma^2\,\mathcal R_{\mathrm{sel}}(N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}) \ +\ \frac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\,\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\gamma^2\\ &\quad \ +\ C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\, \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big], \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \[ B_\gamma := 1+\frac{2}{\gamma}+\frac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)} \] and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal R_{\mathrm{sel}}(N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}) :=\;& 2e^{1/2}C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\log(1+N)\\ &+ 2\Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}} \ +\ \frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg) \Big( 2L_{f,1}C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} \ +\ C_1N^{-1/\texttt{k}}\\ &\hspace{4.9cm} \ +\ 4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} \Big). \end{aligned} \end{equation} To control the off-tube moment, the candidate-marginal tube bound from Appendix~\ref{append:selection-error} (Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-width}) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\) yield, for \(\mathsf{D}_{t}=\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\), \[ \mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>s) \le N\,e^{1/2}\,\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}} \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}\tfrac{s^2}{\lambda}\Big), \qquad s\ge 0. \] Indeed, \(\mathsf{D}_{t}\le \max_i\mathrm{dist}(X_{t,i},\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\), so the maximum-tail bound in \Cref{lem:tube-width} applies. Integrating the tail gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big] \le\;& C_{\mathrm{tail}}\,N \big(1+r(\gamma)^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}+\lambda^{\mathsf n_{\theta x}}\big)\\ &\quad\times \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{4}\tfrac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda}\Big), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \(C_{\mathrm{tail}}\) depends only on \(\mathsf n_{\theta x}\) and problem-data constants. One way to see \eqref{eq:offtube-tail-moment} is to use the identity \[ \mathbb E\big[\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2p}\mathbf 1_{\{\mathsf{D}_{t}>r\}}\big] = r^{2p}\mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>r) \ +\ \int_r^\infty 2p\,s^{2p-1}\mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>s)\,\mathrm{d} s, \] with \(p=\mathsf n_{\theta x}\) and \(r=r(\gamma)\). In particular, if \(\mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>s)\le K\exp(-a s^2/\lambda)\), then \[ \mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>r) \ +\ \mathbb E\big[\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2p}\mathbf 1_{\{\mathsf{D}_{t}>r\}}\big] \le C_pK\big(1+r^{2p}+\lambda^p\big) \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{a}{2}\tfrac{r^2}{\lambda}\Big), \] which gives \eqref{eq:offtube-tail-moment} with \(a=c_{\mathrm{tube}}/2\) and \(K=N e^{1/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}\). Substituting \eqref{eq:offtube-tail-moment} into \eqref{eq:et2-plugged} gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 \le\;& C\,B_\gamma^2 \Big[ \lambda\log(1+N) \ +\ \sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} \ +\ N^{-1/\texttt{k}} \ +\ \sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} \Big]\\ &\quad +\frac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\gamma^2\\ &\quad \ +\ C(1+R_v^2)N \big(1+r(\gamma)^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}+\lambda^{\mathsf n_{\theta x}}\big) \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{4}\tfrac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda}\Big), \end{aligned} \end{equation} for a problem-data constant \(C<\infty\) independent of \(N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R},\gamma,\eta_t,R_v\), and \(t\). Since \(c>0\) is fixed and \(0<\gamma\le1\), \[ B_\gamma^2 = \mathcal{O}\!\Big(\frac{1}{\gamma^2}\Big). \] Applying this simplification to \eqref{eq:et2-before-simplification}, and absorbing numerical and problem-data constants, gives \eqref{eq:app-et2-bigO}. Since \Cref{thm:main-et2-bound} is the same bound with the exponentially small off-tube term abbreviated as \(\mathsf{OT}_{\gamma,\lambda,N,R_v}\), this proves the hyper-gradient error bound stated in \Cref{sec:theory}.

The constants in \Cref{thm:selection-error-bound} and \Cref{lem:tube-width} are uniform over \(\theta\in\Theta\), so the resulting conditional bounds can be averaged over \(\theta_t\) without changing the constants. Combining \eqref{eq:et2-explicit} with \eqref{eq:final-Ex2-bound} from \Cref{thm:selection-error-bound} and the bound $\mathbb E\big[\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big]\le \mathbb E\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2$, we obtain the following bound, uniformly over \(t\): \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 \le\;& 3C_x^2 B_\gamma^2\,\mathcal R_{\mathrm{sel}}(N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}) \ +\ \frac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\,\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\gamma^2\\ &\quad \ +\ C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\, \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big], \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \[ B_\gamma := 1+\frac{2}{\gamma}+\frac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)} \] and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal R_{\mathrm{sel}}(N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}) :=\;& 2e^{1/2}C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\log(1+N)\\ &+ 2\Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}} \ +\ \frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg) \Big( 2L_{f,1}C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} \ +\ C_1N^{-1/\texttt{k}}\\ &\hspace{4.9cm} \ +\ 4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} \Big). \end{aligned} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Off-tube moment
nodes.statement: To control the off-tube moment, the candidate-marginal tube bound from Appendix~\ref{append:selection-error} (Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-width}) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\) yield, for \(\mathsf{D}_{t}=\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\), \[ \mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>s) \le N\,e^{1/2}\,\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}} \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}\tfrac{s^2}{\lambda}\Big), \qquad s\ge 0. \] Indeed, \(\mathsf{D}_{t}\le \max_i\mathrm{dist}(X_{t,i},\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\), so the maximum-tail bound in \Cref{lem:tube-width} applies. Integrating the tail gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big] \le\;& C_{\mathrm{tail}}\,N \big(1+r(\gamma)^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}+\lambda^{\mathsf n_{\theta x}}\big)\\ &\quad\times \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{4}\tfrac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda}\Big), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \(C_{\mathrm{tail}}\) depends only on \(\mathsf n_{\theta x}\) and problem-data constants. One way to see \eqref{eq:offtube-tail-moment} is to use the identity \[ \mathbb E\big[\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2p}\mathbf 1_{\{\mathsf{D}_{t}>r\}}\big] = r^{2p}\mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>r) \ +\ \int_r^\infty 2p\,s^{2p-1}\mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>s)\,\mathrm{d} s, \] with \(p=\mathsf n_{\theta x}\) and \(r=r(\gamma)\). In particular, if \(\mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>s)\le K\exp(-a s^2/\lambda)\), then \[ \mathbb P(\mathsf{D}_{t}>r) \ +\ \mathbb E\big[\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2p}\mathbf 1_{\{\mathsf{D}_{t}>r\}}\big] \le C_pK\big(1+r^{2p}+\lambda^p\big) \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{a}{2}\tfrac{r^2}{\lambda}\Big), \] which gives \eqref{eq:offtube-tail-moment} with \(a=c_{\mathrm{tube}}/2\) and \(K=N e^{1/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}\).
nodes.statement_short: The Rényi tube tail of Lemma 12 integrates to an exponentially small moment.

nodes.name: Substitute
nodes.statement: Substituting \eqref{eq:offtube-tail-moment} into \eqref{eq:et2-plugged} gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\|e_t\|^2 \le\;& C\,B_\gamma^2 \Big[ \lambda\log(1+N) \ +\ \sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} \ +\ N^{-1/\texttt{k}} \ +\ \sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} \Big]\\ &\quad +\frac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\eta_t^2 \ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\gamma^2\\ &\quad \ +\ C(1+R_v^2)N \big(1+r(\gamma)^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}+\lambda^{\mathsf n_{\theta x}}\big) \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{4}\tfrac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda}\Big), \end{aligned} \end{equation} for a problem-data constant \(C<\infty\) independent of \(N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R},\gamma,\eta_t,R_v\), and \(t\).

Since \Cref{thm:main-et2-bound} is the same bound with the exponentially small off-tube term abbreviated as \(\mathsf{OT}_{\gamma,\lambda,N,R_v}\), this proves the hyper-gradient error bound stated in \Cref{sec:theory}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2 (parameter choice and oracle count)
nodes.statement: In the non-singleton regime \(\texttt{k}\ge1\), fix a sufficiently small target $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. As in \Cref{thm:selection-error-bound}, \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\) denotes the square-root R\'enyi tolerance, so the sampler accuracy condition is \(R_2(\nu_i\|\mu_{\theta_t}^\lambda)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2\). We take \(\varepsilon\) small enough that the choices below satisfy \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), and \(0<\gamma\le1\). To ensure $\sup_t\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$ it suffices to make each term on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:app-et2-bigO} of order at most $\varepsilon^2$. One convenient choice is: (i) set $\gamma=\varepsilon$ so that $C_{\mathrm{reg}}\gamma=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, (ii) solve the ridge system to residual $\eta_t=\gamma\varepsilon=\varepsilon^2$, so that \(\eta_t^2/\gamma^2=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)\), (iii) choose \(R_v\ge (2/\gamma)(L_{f,1}+\eta_t)\), so \(R_v=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})\), and (iv) choose the sampling/selection parameters so that the remaining bracketed terms satisfy \[ \lambda\log(1+N) \ +\ \sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)} \ +\ N^{-1/\texttt{k}} \ +\ \sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} = \mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^4). \] A sufficient scaling is \[ N=\left\lceil\varepsilon^{-4\texttt{k}}\right\rceil, \qquad \lambda=\frac{\varepsilon^{8}}{\log(1+N)}, \qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm R}=\varepsilon^{4+2\texttt{k}}. \] Then $\lambda\log(1+N)=\varepsilon^{8}$, $\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)}=\varepsilon^{4}$, and $N^{-1/\texttt{k}}=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{4})$. Moreover, treating \(C_{\mathrm{PI}}\) as a problem-data constant, \[ \sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R} = \mathcal{O}\!\Big(\varepsilon^{-2\texttt{k}}\cdot \varepsilon^{4+2\texttt{k}}\Big) = \mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{4}). \] Thus the displayed sampling/selection term is $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^4)$, and the corresponding contribution to $\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2$ is $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$ after multiplication by the prefactor $\mathcal{O}(1/\gamma^2)=\mathcal{O}(1/\varepsilon^2)$. It remains to check the off-tube moment term. By Lemma~\ref{lem:tube-invertibility}, \[ r(\gamma)=\min\left\{\rho,\frac{\gamma}{2\bar L_{g,3}}\right\}, \] so for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), \(r(\gamma)\ge c_r\varepsilon\) for a problem-data constant \(c_r>0\). Consequently, \[ \frac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda} \ \ge\ c_r'\,\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1+N). \] Since \(R_v=\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})\), the off-tube term \[ (1+R_v^2)N \big(1+r(\gamma)^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}+\lambda^{\mathsf n_{\theta x}}\big) \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{4}\tfrac{r(\gamma)^2}{\lambda}\Big) \] is bounded by a polynomial in \(\varepsilon^{-1}\) times \(\exp(-c\,\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1+N))\) for a problem-data constant \(c>0\). It is therefore super-polynomially small in \(\varepsilon^{-1}\) and, in particular, is \(\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)\). Substituting this control into \Cref{prop:outer-inexact} (with stepsize $1/L_F$) yields an $\varepsilon$-stationary guarantee after \[ T=\mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{L_F\,(F(\theta_0)-F_\star)}{\varepsilon^2}\right) \] outer iterations. \paragraph{Total oracle complexity.} Per outer iteration, \textsc{HG-MS} uses (a) $NK$ evaluations of $\nabla_x g$ for the sampler (\Cref{alg:lmc-ula}), (b) $N$ evaluations of $f(\theta_t,X_{t,i})$ for hard selection, and (c) $\#\mathrm{HVP}$ Hessian--vector products for CG to reach residual tolerance $\eta_t$. First consider the sampler/function-evaluation cost, \[ \mathcal{O}\big(T(NK+N)\big). \] Assume each ULA chain is initialized from the \(\lambda\)-scaled Gaussian warm start in \Cref{lem:gaussian-init-r3}, with centers in a fixed compact set. If the ULA sampler is run for $K$ steps so that the square-root R\'enyi tolerance satisfies $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}=\varepsilon^{4+2\texttt{k}}$, then \Cref{cor:lmc-gibbs-w2} gives $K=\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\lambda^{-4}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^{-2})$. Under the above scaling of \((N,\lambda,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R})\), this gives $K=\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\big(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\log^{4}(1+N)\,\varepsilon^{-40-4\texttt{k}}\big)$ and hence \[ T\,N\,K =\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\big(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,N\log^{4}(1+N)\,\varepsilon^{-42-4\texttt{k}}\big) =\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\big(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\varepsilon^{-42-8\texttt{k}}\big), \] which dominates the additional \(TN\) hard-selection evaluations. If HVPs are counted as oracle calls, the total accounting becomes \[ \mathcal{O}\big(T(NK+N+\#\mathrm{HVP})\big) = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\big(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\varepsilon^{-42-8\texttt{k}}\big) +\mathcal{O}(T\,\#\mathrm{HVP}). \] The following remark computes the CG/HVP count and shows that the displayed sampler term dominates it under the parameter choice above.
nodes.section: E.4 Parameter choices and oracle complexity
nodes.statement_short: Choose γ=ε, η=ε², N=ε^{−4k}, λ=ε^8/log N, ε_R=ε^{4+2k} so E‖e_t‖²=O(ε²), apply Proposition 3, and count ULA, selection and HVP oracle calls.
